# 0.1.0-preview.18
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/changelog/v0-1-0-preview-18

## Added

- Element-valued content overloads for `HyperlinkButton`, `RepeatButton`,
  `ToggleButton` / `ThreeStateToggleButton`, `DropDownButton`, `SplitButton`,
  `ToggleSplitButton`, `CheckBox` / `ThreeStateCheckBox`, and `RadioButton`
  (issue [#1482](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1482)).
- `Imperative<TElement, TControl>.Unmount`, an optional teardown callback the engine
  runs when a tagged control using that children strategy unmounts, so a handler can
  unmount the children its `Reconcile` mounted (issue [#1482](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1482)).
- Reactor's render timing is recordable by a non-elevated **private** ETW session (the kind
  `winapp perf` attaches with), which never enables the `Microsoft-UI-Reactor` EventSource.
  A new raw TraceLogging provider, `Microsoft-UI-Reactor-Perf`
  (`0902a96c-4e92-5b91-4d2b-5a8058055c78`), writes a `RenderPass` span per host render pass,
  an inclusive `ComponentRender` span per component render (mount, update, the host root, and
  rows a virtualized list realizes during layout), `Reconcile`, `Effects` and `ChildReconcile`
  spans (with inserted/removed/moved/replaced counts), `StateChange` naming the component whose
  setter ran, and `KeyedListDiagnostic`. `RenderPass` Start names the component whose
  re-render request scheduled the pass (`requesterId`, `requesterName`, `requestCount`), with
  no need for the verbose `State` keyword. `ComponentRender` Start carries the C# call site that
  created the component from the source map (`callSiteFile` (the file name only),
  `callSiteLine`, `callSiteColumn`). `Reconcile` Stop counts the panel child edits made during
  the entry at the default level (`inserted`, `removed`, `moved`, `replaced`). Function and memo
  components are named by their render function, as DevTools names them
  (`RenderEachTime in MainPage.Render`). With no session listening each emit site is one
  enabled check. The provider ships at schema revision 2; schema:
  `docs/reference/perf-trace-events.md` (issues [#1484](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1484), [#1489](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1489); call-site fields follow the
  spec 044 §6.2.1 payload PII policy).

- `TitleBarElement.LeftHeader` and `.LeftHeader(Element)` support declarative content
  before the title bar's title, using the same child lifecycle as `RightHeader`
  (issue [#1478](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1478)).

- Opt-in message-wide Markdown text selection in Reactor Advanced:
  `MarkdownOptions.TextSelection`, `MarkdownTextSelection.Scope`, semantic `Surface`
  and composable `Visibility` gates coordinate separately rendered Markdown leaves,
  lists, code and tables. Includes grapheme-aware caret movement, modern ScrollView /
  ItemsView scrolling, UIA TextPattern ranges and feedback-only `OnCopyResult` after
  Reactor's single clipboard write (openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#1844).

- `PersonPictureElement.ProfilePicture(string? uri)` fluent modifier, matching the existing
  `DisplayName` / `Initials` sugar. ReactorGallery's PersonPicture page uses it to show an
  avatar loaded over HTTPS (issue [#1460](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1460)).

- `ControlDescriptor.HandCodedControlled` takes `armOnMount`. With `valueDiffEcho`, it arms
  the Mount write's echo as well as Update's, for a control whose change event arrives
  after the trampoline is wired, as `RichEditBox`'s `Document.SetText` does
  (spec 047 §8.3).

## Changed

- **`AsyncValue<T>` and `LoadState` are now C# 15 `closed` records (breaking for
  subclasses).** They were abstract records whose `private protected` constructor was meant
  to keep the case set closed, but a subclass in another assembly could still chain to the
  compiler-generated `protected` copy constructor (`: base(other)`); such subclasses now fail
  with CS9382. The built-in cases and pattern matching are unchanged. Consumers compiling
  with C# 15 can `switch` over the cases exhaustively without a `_` arm, and a missing case
  is warning CS8509. Reactor still targets `net10.0` and stays consumable from the .NET 10
  SDK; building Reactor from source now requires the .NET 11 SDK (spec 020 §5).
- Public `SingleContent` strategies leave native setter-supplied content intact
  when no Element child is declared (on mount or on both sides of an update).
  Declare `Empty()` to clear the slot explicitly; this also applies to
  third-party control handlers (issue [#1482](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1482)).
- `Button` and the button family share content reconciliation that preserves
  descendant state. For `Button`, replaced declared content is now cleaned up when
  it gives way to text or native setter-supplied content. A declared `ContentElement`
  now also supplies `Button`'s caption-derived accessible name instead of `Label`;
  icon-only content should supply `.AutomationName(...)` (issue [#1482](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1482)).
- `CheckBox(value, callback, null)` and `ThreeStateCheckBox(value, callback, null)`
  are now ambiguous between string and Element content overloads. Use `label: null`
  or cast to `(string?)null` to select the existing text overload (issue [#1482](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1482)).
- **`ExpanderElement.HeaderTemplate` and `.HeaderTemplate(Element)` are renamed to
  `HeaderContent` and `.HeaderContent(Element)` (breaking).** This Element-valued
  child is mounted into WinUI's `Expander.Header`, not its `HeaderTemplate`
  DataTemplate property. Rename fluent calls, object/`with` initializers, and
  property reads, then recompile consumers; string-header fallback and child
  lifecycle behavior are unchanged (issue [#1480](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1480)). See the [migration notes](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/layout#migration-expanderheadertemplate-renamed-to-headercontent).

- `.Set` writes to `BorderThickness` or `BorderBrush` on `Grid` and `StackPanel`
  now report `REACTOR_POOL_001` (Warning). Builds using `TreatWarningsAsErrors`
  may need to use the corresponding fluent modifiers instead. The same writes on
  `RelativePanel` now report `REACTOR_MOD_002` (Info), since it is not pooled
  (issue [#1039](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1039)).

- The generated API index now includes Reactor Advanced factories, modifiers, hooks,
  enums and public types alongside the core Reactor surface, keeping `mur --api` and
  both shipped agent-reference copies complete (PR [#1475](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1475)).

- The internal Yoga layout engine behind `FlexPanel` is synced to upstream
  facebook/yoga@41118bd (pinned in `cgmanifest.json`), with a few documented local
  divergences. `FlexPanel` layouts are unchanged apart from the fixes listed under Fixed.
- **The guide, README, agent kit and `bootstrap.ps1` now describe Windows App SDK template pack
  `0.0.8-alpha`** (microsoft/WindowsAppSDK#6845; spec 022). That pack adds `reactor-singlefile`, a
  one-file app with no `.csproj`, and a `--packaging Packaged|Unpackaged` option on the four project
  templates, so the unpackaged shape no longer needs a hand edit after scaffolding. Its scaffolds no
  longer reference the `Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK` metapackage and the `--wasdk-version` option is
  gone: the Windows App SDK arrives through `Microsoft.UI.Reactor` at the version Reactor depends on.
  Add the metapackage yourself for a self-contained app or a newer WinUI. An older installed pack
  rejects `--packaging` and lacks `reactor-singlefile`; update it with
  `winapp new --list --template-version latest`.

## Fixed

- In diagnostics mode (`REACTOR_DIAGNOSTICS=1`), mounting a different root over content
  that keeps a closed `CommandBarFlyout` no longer leaves that flyout's commands holding
  a collected `ReactorSource` value. CsWinRT boxes a string written to a
  DependencyProperty as a managed CCW, and XAML stops keeping it alive on those commands
  after the swap. The next garbage collection freed the renamed value, and any later read
  of the property threw `NullReferenceException`, including Reactor's own walk on the next
  root swap. The renamed values are now held for the process, like the values written
  when the commands mounted (spec 010).

- Removing a subtree through the pooled teardown path now unregisters the
  `ErrorBoundary` nodes inside it, as the non-pooled path already did, so a
  recycled wrapper control no longer keeps a stale boundary record (issue [#1482](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1482)).

- `ContentDialog` resolves the application implicit style, falling back to
  `DefaultContentDialogStyle`, before its first template realization. This restores
  the native entrance animation for programmatically created dialogs while
  preserving app-level implicit styles. Caller `.Set(...)` styles keep priority
  (issue [#1487](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1487);
  [WinUI #8476](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/issues/8476)).

- Flyout, MenuFlyout and CommandBarFlyout targets retain their own event callbacks
  after mount, update and pool reuse. Decorator identity is stored separately so
  flyout callbacks and teardown still use the current decorator. Exit transitions
  and connected-animation keys use the first configured value from the outermost
  decorator inward. Animated modifiers select the current render's `.Animate()`
  curve when a flyout target or decorator updates, with ambient curves taking
  precedence. Unmount also releases refs and animation state on intermediate
  decorators. Nested decorators attach only
  the outermost native flyout, including through transparent Memo or RegisterType
  targets. They clean up displaced content and keep inner updates
  from changing the outer flyout or duplicating its callbacks. For these
  decorators, the provisional `Reconciler.GetElementTag` now returns the target's
  tag instead of the decorator element (spec 047 §14 Phase 1; [#942](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/942)).

- A controlled `RichEditBox` or `AutoSuggestBox` no longer drops the user's first edit after
  a state write ([#1455](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1455)). Both now suppress their asynchronous echo with the value-diff arm
  instead of the suppress counter, which kept a token after every write. A `RichEditBox`
  whose state value contains line breaks no longer calls `SetText` on every render, and
  `onTextChanged` keeps a trailing break the user types (spec 047 §8.3).

- `BorderBrush`, `BorderThickness`, and `BorderInlineStart` now apply to `Grid`,
  `StackPanel`, and `RelativePanel`, including themed border brushes. Pooled grids
  and stack panels release their border values before reuse. The Regedit example
  uses the supported fluent modifiers (issue [#1039](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1039)).

- Pooled controls release `HorizontalContentAlignment` and `VerticalContentAlignment`
  on return, preventing content alignment from leaking into the next element that
  reuses the control ([issue #1013](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1013)).

- `UseInfiniteResource` and `UseDataSource` hooks that share a `CacheKeyPrefix` isolate
  cached pages by the hook's initial page size. Hooks with different sizes no longer reuse
  incompatible pages, while hooks with matching sizes and query dependencies can still
  share them (spec 020 §14 D6; [#1452](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1452), case 3).
- `UseDataSource` retains its initial normalized page size across rerenders and
  query restarts, keeping requests and cursor offsets aligned with resource row
  positions. A later render that asks for a different size logs one
  `UseDataSource.PageSize` diagnostic warning per hook instead. To use a different size,
  remount the calling component by changing its key from the parent (part of [#1452](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1452), case 2).
- `DataGrid` under `ReactorFeatureFlags.UseHookBasedPaging` now keeps its mount-time page
  size, matching the legacy paging path. Changing `RowHeight` or `EstimatedRowHeight` at
  runtime no longer restarts pagination or discards loaded rows when a sort or filter is
  active (part of [#1452](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1452)).

- `PersonPicture`'s `ProfilePicture` no longer throws during reconciliation for empty,
  relative, or malformed URIs; it shows no picture instead. Removing `ProfilePicture` on
  a later render now clears the previous image rather than leaving it on screen (issue [#1460](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1460)).
- **`FlexPanel` no longer gives shrinking children astronomically large sizes.** When every
  shrinkable item in a line froze at its minimum size, the remaining shrink total could be a
  float residual instead of exactly 0, and dividing by it produced sizes around 10⁹–10¹¹ px
  (or, once clamped, children squeezed to their minimum and text wrapped into very tall
  panels). Ported from upstream Yoga (facebook/yoga#1665, facebook/yoga#2038).
- **`FlexPanel` sizes now land exactly on the device-pixel grid.** Rounded widths and heights
  are computed in double precision, so far from the origin a child no longer comes out one
  float step short (e.g. 43.9998 instead of 44) of its measured size, and a measured child
  whose size is a whole number of device pixels keeps exactly that size instead of gaining
  or losing a pixel (which could wrap or truncate its text). Ported from upstream Yoga
  (facebook/yoga#2037, facebook/yoga#2040).
- **Wrapping `FlexPanel` rows no longer break a line on float rounding noise** when arranged
  at exactly their content-sized width (facebook/yoga#2022).
- **`Collapsed` children of a `FlexPanel` with `Wrap = WrapReverse` are no longer arranged
  with a NaN rect.** The wrap-reverse pass mirrored hidden children too, using their
  undefined measured size; they now keep the zero layout Yoga gives `display: none` nodes.
  This bug is also present in upstream Yoga.

---

# Controls
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls

```csharp
class ControlsCatalogApp : Component
{
    public override Element Render() => VStack(8,
        TextBlock("Controls catalog").FontSize(20).Bold(),
        TextBlock("Every Reactor control, grouped by category.").Opacity(0.7),
        Button("Open Forms", () => { })
    ).Padding(16);
}
```

The ten categories below cover the full set Reactor
exposes today. Pick a category, open its detail page, and you'll find
the factory signature, modifier matrix, and screenshots for every
control inside it.

Two ground rules apply across the catalog:

1. **Every control has a Reactor factory.** No XAML in `Render()` — the
   factories on [`Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Factories`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks) are the
   only thing you need to compose UI.
2. **WinUI-wrapper controls link out, not duplicate.** When a control
   (like `DatePicker` or `AutoSuggestBox`) is a transparent WinUI
   wrapper, the Reactor page covers the factory and modifier surface
   and links to the Microsoft Learn design page for theming, layout
   guidance, and accessibility behavior. Reactor-original controls
   (`DataGrid`, `Markdown`, `VirtualList`, `FlexPanel`) are
   documented exhaustively in their own pages.

<!-- ai:lock -->
**What "every control" means here, precisely.** The tables below are the
mountable control catalog: every element type registered with the
`ControlRegistry` by
[`ReactorApp.RegisterAllBuiltIns()`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/extending-reactor-controls),
minus nine framework elements that are plumbing rather than something you
pick off a shelf. `CommandHost` and `NavigationHost` are wiring emitted by
[commanding](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/commanding) and [navigation](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/navigation); `FormField`,
`ValidationRule`, and `ValidationVisualizer` are the
[forms](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/forms) validation decorators; `Semantic` is the
[accessibility](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/accessibility) annotation wrapper; `XamlHost` and
`XamlPage` are the [XAML interop](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/get-started/xaml-developers#host-xaml-inside-reactor) hosts; and
`AnnounceRegion` is internal — it exists only to back the
[`UseAnnounce`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/accessibility) hook and has no public factory. A unit
test (`ControlCatalogCompletenessTests`) fails the build when a newly
registered control is missing from this page, so the claim above is
checked rather than asserted.
<!-- /ai:lock -->

## Forms [#forms]

Text input, choice, sliders, buttons, and the validation pipeline.
Forms is the category most apps spend time in; the detail page
([forms.md](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/forms)) covers controlled-input patterns and the
`FormField` validation surface.

```csharp
class FormsGroup : Component
{
    public override Element Render()
    {
        var (name, setName) = UseState("Ada");
        var (agree, setAgree) = UseState(true);
        var (volume, setVolume) = UseState(60.0);

        return VStack(8,
            TextBox(name, setName, placeholderText: "Name", header: "Name").Width(200),
            CheckBox(agree, setAgree, label: "I agree"),
            Slider(volume, 0, 100, setVolume).Width(200),
            Button("Submit", () => { })
        ).Padding(16);
    }
}
```

![Forms category thumbnail](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/controls/forms-thumb.png)

| Control | Description |
|---|---|
| `TextBox` | Single-line text input with placeholder + header. |
| `PasswordBox` | Obscured text input. |
| `NumberBox` | Numeric input with up/down spinner. |
| `AutoSuggestBox` | Text input with a filtered suggestion list. |
| `CheckBox` / `ThreeStateCheckBox` | Two- or three-state checkbox with optional label. |
| `ToggleSwitch` | Two-state switch with optional header. |
| `Slider` | Min/max-bounded numeric value. |
| `ComboBox` | Drop-down list of strings. |
| `RadioButtons` | Single-select radio group. |
| `RadioButton` | A single radio, for hand-built groups. |
| `DatePicker` | Inline three-spinner date picker (non-null). |
| `CalendarDatePicker` | Compact button that opens a popup calendar (nullable). |
| `CalendarView` | Full month grid with single / multiple / range selection. |
| `TimePicker` | Hour / minute / period spinner. |
| `ColorPicker` | Continuous color selection with spectrum and hex input. |
| `Button` | Click handler with label. |
| `RepeatButton` | Fires repeatedly while held. |
| `ToggleButton` / `ThreeStateToggleButton` | Button that latches a state. |
| `HyperlinkButton` | Link-styled button with a navigate target. |
| `DropDownButton` | Button that opens an attached flyout. |
| `SplitButton` / `ToggleSplitButton` | Primary action plus a drop-down half. |

WinUI design page: [Buttons](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/design/controls/buttons),
[Text controls](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/design/controls/text-controls).

### Composing button content [#composing-button-content]

Button-family controls accept an `Element` instead of a string, so icons,
labels, and other controls can share the native content slot. The native
control still owns focus, invocation, and checked-state visuals.

| Controls | Content overload |
|---|---|
| `Button`, `RepeatButton`, `HyperlinkButton` | Pass an `Element` as the first argument. |
| `ToggleButton`, `ThreeStateToggleButton` | Pass an `Element` first, followed by the checked value and callback. |
| `DropDownButton`, `SplitButton`, `ToggleSplitButton` | Pass primary content first; `flyout:` remains a separate slot. |
| `RadioButton` | Pass content first; checked state and group name are unchanged. |
| `CheckBox`, `ThreeStateCheckBox` | Pass content as the third argument, after the checked value and callback. |

```csharp
class ButtonContentExample : Component
{
    public override Element Render()
    {
        var (selected, setSelected) = UseState(false);
        return ToggleButton(
            HStack(8,
                Icon(FontIcon("\uE8B9")).AccessibilityHidden(),
                TextBlock("Images")),
            selected,
            setSelected)
            .AutomationName("Images");
    }
}
```

The text overloads remain available. On a direct element record,
`ContentElement` takes precedence over its text property; setting it back
to `null` restores that text. Updating the content preserves compatible
child controls and their component state. Replacing or removing the subtree
runs its cleanup.

Content assigned through `.Set(c => c.Content = nativeElement)` remains available
when no Reactor `ContentElement` is declared, including when switching from an
Element subtree to native content. For composed content, set an explicit
`.AutomationName(...)` when it has no directly readable text caption; hidden fallback
text is not used as the accessible name. An explicit `.AutomationName(...)` is
preserved when switching content, even if it matches the previous visible caption.

## Collections [#collections]

Bound-list rendering and virtualization. Use `ListView` when the data
fits in memory and the row template is uniform, `VirtualList` when the
list is large enough that mounting all rows would hurt frame time, and
`LazyVStack` when the layout must be a stack but mounting cost is the
bottleneck.

```csharp
class CollectionsGroup : Component
{
    public override Element Render()
    {
        var items = new[] { "Alpha", "Bravo", "Charlie", "Delta" };
        return VStack(4,
            TextBlock("Items").Bold(),
            ForEach(items, item => TextBlock($"  • {item}").WithKey(item))
        ).Padding(16);
    }
}
```

![Collections category thumbnail](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/controls/collections-thumb.png)

| Control | Description |
|---|---|
| `ListView<T>` | Bound, keyed list with per-item view builder. |
| `GridView<T>` | Tiled bound collection. |
| `ListBox` | Compact non-virtualizing selection list. |
| `LazyVStack<T>` / `LazyHStack<T>` | Defer-mounted vertical / horizontal stack. |
| `VirtualList` | Index-driven virtual list with scroll API. |
| `ItemsRepeater<T>` | Bare virtualizing panel — no chrome, no selection. |
| `ItemsView<T>` | Modern items host with typed selection. |
| `ItemContainer` | Selection / hover chrome for a hand-built item host. |
| `TreeView<T>` | Hierarchical list with expand / collapse. |
| `ForEach` | Compose a sequence of elements without a list control. |

Detail page: [Collections](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/collections).

## Text & Media [#text-media]

|---|---|

| `Title` / `Heading` / `SubHeading` / `Subtitle` | Semantic heading sizes. |
| `Body` / `BodyLarge` / `BodyStrong` / `Caption` | Semantic body and metadata sizes. |
| `RichTextBlock` | Inline-formatted text. |
| `RichEditBox` | Editable rich text. |
| `Markdown` | Reactor-original Markdown renderer (`Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Advanced`). |
| `Image` | Bitmap source. |
| `MediaPlayerElement` | Video / audio playback. |
| `WebView2` | Embedded Chromium surface. |
| `MapControl` | Bing-Maps-backed map surface. |

## Layout & Containers [#layout-containers]

Panels that position children, and single-child hosts that add chrome,
scrolling, or clipping. These are the structural half of the catalog —
they rarely appear on their own, but every screen is made of them.

```csharp
class LayoutGroup : Component
{
    public override Element Render() => VStack(8,
        Card(
            HStack(8,
                TextBlock("Border / Card").Bold(),
                TextBlock("wraps one child").Opacity(0.7)
            ).Padding(8)
        ),
        Expander("Expander", TextBlock("Collapsible section body.")),
        Viewbox(TextBlock("Viewbox scales its child").FontSize(10))
    ).Padding(16);
}
```

![Layout category thumbnail](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/controls/layout-thumb.png)

| Control | Description |
|---|---|
| `VStack` / `HStack` | Spaced linear stacks — the default panel. |
| `Grid` / `UniformGrid` / `InterspersedGrid` | Row / column grid layout. |
| `FlexRow` / `FlexColumn` | CSS-Flexbox layout via Yoga ([flex-layout](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/flex-layout)). |
| `WrapGrid` | Items flow and wrap to the next line. |
| `RelativePanel` | Constraint-based sibling positioning. |
| `Canvas` | Absolute X/Y positioning. |
| `Border` / `Card` | Single-child chrome: background, corner radius, stroke. |
| `Viewbox` | Uniformly scales one child to fit. |
| `ScrollView` / `ScrollViewer` | Scroll hosts (modern / classic). |
| `AnnotatedScrollBar` | Scroll bar with labelled tick marks. |
| `SplitView` | Collapsible side pane plus content. |
| `Expander` | Collapsible header + content section. |
| `RefreshContainer` | Pull-to-refresh wrapper. |
| `SwipeControl` | Swipe-revealed commands on an item. |
| `SemanticZoom` | Paired zoomed-in / zoomed-out views. |
| `ParallaxView` | Background that scrolls at an offset rate. |

## Navigation [#navigation]

Controls that move the user between screens or sections. Pair them with
the routing hooks on [navigation.md](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/navigation) — the control is the
chrome, the navigation state is a hook.

```csharp
class NavigationGroup : Component
{
    public override Element Render()
    {
        var (tab, setTab) = UseState(1);

        return VStack(8,
            BreadcrumbBar([
                new BreadcrumbBarItemData("Home"),
                new BreadcrumbBarItemData("Controls"),
            ]),
            SelectorBar([
                new SelectorBarItemData("All"),
                new SelectorBarItemData("Forms"),
                new SelectorBarItemData("Layout"),
            ], tab, setTab)
        ).Padding(16);
    }
}
```

![Navigation category thumbnail](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/controls/navigation-thumb.png)

| Control | Description |
|---|---|
| `NavigationView` | Top or left app navigation shell. |
| `Frame` | Page host with back-stack integration. |
| `BreadcrumbBar` | Ancestor trail with click-to-jump. |
| `TabView` | Closable, reorderable document tabs. |
| `Pivot` | Swipeable top-level section switcher. |
| `SelectorBar` | Compact inline segment picker. |
| `FlipView` | One-item-at-a-time paged view. |
| `TitleBar` | Custom window title bar content. |

Detail page: [Navigation](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/navigation); window chrome in [Windows](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/windows).

## Shapes & Icons [#shapes-icons]

Vector primitives and icon sources. Shapes take a `Brush` for `Fill` /
`Stroke` (not the color string that panel-level `.Background(...)`
accepts). For imperative 2D drawing, see [Win2D canvas](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/win2d-canvas).

```csharp
class ShapesGroup : Component
{
    // Shape fills/strokes take a WinUI Brush (not a color string like the
    // panel-level .Background(string) modifier).
    static SolidColorBrush Swatch(byte r, byte g, byte b) =>
        new(Color.FromArgb(255, r, g, b));

    public override Element Render() => HStack(12,
        Rectangle().Width(48).Height(32).Fill(Swatch(0x4a, 0x7e, 0xbb)),
        Ellipse().Width(40).Height(40).Fill(Swatch(0xbb, 0x4a, 0x7e)),
        Line(0, 0, 48, 32).Stroke(Swatch(0x7e, 0xbb, 0x4a)).StrokeThickness(3)
    ).Padding(16);
}
```

![Shapes category thumbnail](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/controls/shapes-thumb.png)

| Control | Description |
|---|---|
| `Rectangle` | Rectangle with optional corner radii. |
| `Ellipse` | Ellipse / circle. |
| `Line` | Straight segment between two points. |
| `Path2D` | Arbitrary geometry from path data. |
| `Icon` | Polymorphic icon source (font glyph, symbol, bitmap, path). |
| `AnimatedIcon` | Icon that plays a transition between states. |
| `AnimatedVisualPlayer` | Lottie / composition animation host. |

Detail pages: [Styling](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/styling), [Animation](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/animation).

## Dialogs & Flyouts [#dialogs-flyouts]

Modal and ephemeral surfaces. Reactor wires these through the
[commanding](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/commanding) system so the same `Command<T>` can light
up a button, a menu item, and a keyboard shortcut without duplicating
logic.

```csharp
class DialogsGroup : Component
{
    public override Element Render() => VStack(8,
        TextBlock("Confirm action").Bold(),
        TextBlock("This cannot be undone.").Opacity(0.8),
        HStack(8,
            Button("Cancel", () => { }),
            Button("Delete", () => { })
        )
    ).Padding(16);
}
```

![Dialogs & Flyouts category thumbnail](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/controls/dialogs-and-flyouts-thumb.png)

| Control | Description |
|---|---|
| `ContentDialog` | Modal full-screen confirmation. |
| `Flyout` | Lightweight anchored surface with arbitrary content. |
| `MenuFlyout` | Context menu attached to a target. |
| `CommandBarFlyout` | Mini-toolbar with commands. |
| `CommandBar` | Persistent primary / secondary command strip. |
| `MenuBar` | Classic top-level menu bar. |
| `Popup` | Free-form anchored surface. |

Detail page: [Dialogs & Flyouts](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/dialogs-and-flyouts).

## Data System [#data-system]

`DataGrid` and the data-source / column / paging primitives. The
data-system surface is Reactor-original (no WinUI parallel) and is
documented exhaustively in [data-system.md](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/data-system).

```csharp
class DataSystemGroup : Component
{
    public override Element Render()
    {
        var rows = new[] { ("Ada", 36), ("Linus", 55), ("Grace", 85) };
        return VStack(4,
            HStack(16,
                TextBlock("Name").Bold(),
                TextBlock("Age").Bold()
            ),
            ForEach(rows, r => HStack(16,
                TextBlock(r.Item1),
                TextBlock(r.Item2.ToString())
            ).WithKey(r.Item1))
        ).Padding(16);
    }
}
```

![Data System category thumbnail](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/controls/data-system-thumb.png)

| Control / Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `DataGrid<T>` | Virtualized grid with sort / filter / inline edit. |
| `Column<T>` | Column descriptor + builder. |
| `IDataSource<T>` | Pluggable data source abstraction. |
| `ListDataSource<T>` | In-memory source with client-side sort/filter. |
| `DataPageCache<T>` | Incremental paging cache. |

Detail page: [Data System](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/data-system).

| `LineChart<T>` | Line series with axes. |
| `BarChart<T>` | Bar / column series. |
| `AreaChart<T>` | Filled area under a line. |
| `PieChart<T>` | Categorical share. |
| `TreeChart<T>` | Hierarchical layout. |
| `ForceGraph` | Force-directed node graph. |

Detail page: [Charting](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/charting).

## Tips [#tips]

**Don't reach for a custom Component before checking the catalog.**
Most needs are met by composing existing factories — a "card" is a
`VStack` inside a `Border`, a "stat tile" is two `TextBlock`s stacked.
The cost of a custom Component is the cost of maintaining its render
function forever.

**Reactor-original vs. WinUI wrapper matters for documentation.**
Wrappers point to Microsoft Learn for design guidance; Reactor-originals
own their full surface here. When the per-control page is missing a
section like "accessibility behavior", check whether the control is a
wrapper — the answer is usually upstream.

**Catalog thumbnails are not micro-tutorials.** They show the control
in a representative state, no more. The detail page covers usage,
modifiers, and the "Don't" cases.

- **[Components](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/components)** — Previous: how a `Component` is the
  thing that hosts a tree of controls.
- **[Forms](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/forms)** — Next: the biggest catalog category, with the
  full input + validation surface.
- **[Layout](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/layout)** — How `VStack` / `HStack` / `Grid` /
  `FlexPanel` compose any control into a real screen.
- **[Styling](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/styling)** — `ThemeRef` tokens, modifier chaining, and
  named styles applied across the catalog.
- **[Recipes](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/recipes)** — Real-world compositions that pull
  controls together into common shapes.

# Charting
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/charting

ReactorD3 sits on two layers and you choose the level you author at.
The high-level DSL — `LineChart`, `BarChart`, `AreaChart`, `PieChart`,
plus `TreeChart` and `ForceGraph` — covers the cases dashboards keep
asking for: a series, an x accessor, a y accessor, and an opinionated
visual surface that the library wires up for you (axes, grids,
palettes, keyboard navigation, screen-reader summary). When the
opinionated surface doesn't fit — when you want a slice's percent
rendered inside the slice itself, when you want a heatmap, when you
want a bespoke parallel-coordinates view — the same library exposes
the D3 primitives that built the high-level shapes: `LinearScale`,
`BandScale`, `D3Canvas`, `D3LinePath<T>`, `D3ArcPath`, and the
`*LabelView` escape hatches on the high-level charts. This is the
same trade-off Recharts and Observable Plot draw — convenience first,
escape hatch beneath — except every D3 primitive renders as a WinUI
shape on the same `Canvas` the high-level charts use, so dropping a
level never means switching renderers. Pick the high level by default;
drop into D3 only when the higher-level surface refuses what you need.

Import the DSL alongside the standard Reactor factories. Charting ships in the
optional `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Advanced` package (spec 062 §7), so add its
package reference first:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Advanced" Version="0.1.0-preview.18" />
```

```csharp
using static Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Factories;
using static Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Charting.Charts;
```

## Line Chart [#line-chart]

`LineChart` draws a continuous line through your data points. Pass a
collection and accessor functions for X and Y:

```csharp
class LineChartDemo : Component
{
    private static readonly SalesPoint[] Data =
    [
        new(1, 120), new(2, 180), new(3, 150),
        new(4, 220), new(5, 310), new(6, 280),
        new(7, 350), new(8, 400), new(9, 380),
        new(10, 420), new(11, 460), new(12, 510)
    ];

    public override Element Render()
    {
        return VStack(12,
            SubHeading("Line Chart"),
            LineChart(Data, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue)
                .Title("Monthly Revenue — Line")
                .SeriesName("Revenue")
                .Units("months", "USD")
                .AxisLabel(ChartAxisType.X, "Month")
                .AxisLabel(ChartAxisType.Y, "Revenue (USD)")
                .Width(600).Height(250)
                .Stroke("#0078D4").StrokeWidth(2.5)
                .ShowGrid(true).ShowAxes(true)
        ).Padding(24);
    }
}
```

![Line chart](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/charting/line-chart.png)

The chart auto-scales axes to fit your data with `.Nice()` rounding. Toggle
grid lines with `.ShowGrid()` and axis labels with `.ShowAxes()`.

## Bar Chart [#bar-chart]

`BarChart` renders vertical bars. Each data point becomes a bar whose height
maps to the Y value:

```csharp
class BarChartDemo : Component
{
    private static readonly SalesPoint[] Data =
    [
        new(1, 340), new(2, 420), new(3, 510), new(4, 380)
    ];

    public override Element Render()
    {
        return VStack(12,
            SubHeading("Bar Chart"),
            BarChart(Data, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue)
                .Title("Quarterly Revenue — Bar")
                .SeriesName("Revenue")
                .Units("quarters", "USD")
                .AxisLabel(ChartAxisType.X, "Quarter")
                .AxisLabel(ChartAxisType.Y, "Revenue (USD)")
                .Width(600).Height(250)
                .Fill("#50C878")
                .ShowGrid(true).ShowAxes(true)
        ).Padding(24);
    }
}
```

![Bar chart](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/charting/bar-chart.png)

Bar width is calculated automatically based on the number of data points.
Use `.Fill()` to set the bar color and `.FillOpacity()` to control
transparency.

## Area Chart [#area-chart]

`AreaChart` fills the region between the data line and the baseline. It
combines a filled area with a line overlay:

```csharp
class AreaChartDemo : Component
{
    private static readonly SalesPoint[] Data =
    [
        new(1, 50), new(2, 120), new(3, 200),
        new(4, 350), new(5, 480), new(6, 600),
        new(7, 720), new(8, 850), new(9, 1020),
        new(10, 1150), new(11, 1300), new(12, 1500)
    ];

    public override Element Render()
    {
        return VStack(12,
            SubHeading("Area Chart"),
            AreaChart(Data, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue)
                .Title("Monthly Revenue — Area")
                .SeriesName("Revenue")
                .Units("months", "USD")
                .AxisLabel(ChartAxisType.X, "Month")
                .AxisLabel(ChartAxisType.Y, "Revenue (USD)")
                .Width(600).Height(250)
                .Stroke("#9B59B6").Fill("#9B59B6")
                .FillOpacity(0.2)
                .ShowGrid(true).ShowAxes(true)
        ).Padding(24);
    }
}
```

![Area chart](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/charting/area-chart.png)

Use `.FillOpacity()` to control area transparency. A low value (0.15--0.3)
lets grid lines show through while still filling the shape.

## Pie Chart [#pie-chart]

`PieChart` divides data into proportional arcs. Set `.InnerRadius()` > 0
for a donut chart:

```csharp
class PieChartDemo : Component
{
    private static readonly CategoryData[] Data =
    [
        new("Engineering", 42),
        new("Marketing", 18),
        new("Sales", 25),
        new("Support", 15)
    ];

    public override Element Render()
    {
        return VStack(12,
            SubHeading("Pie Chart"),
            PieChart(Data, d => d.Value, d => d.Name)
                .Title("Team Distribution")
                .Description("Pie chart showing team size across Engineering, Marketing, Sales, and Support.")
                .Width(300).Height(300)
                .InnerRadius(60)
                .PadAngle(0.03)
        ).Padding(24);
    }
}
```

![Pie chart](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/charting/pie-chart.png)

Pass a label accessor to display text at each arc's centroid. Colors cycle
through the Category10 palette by default — override with `.SetColors()`.

## Chart Configuration [#chart-configuration]

All chart types share a common set of builder methods:

| Method | Default | Purpose |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `.Width(n)` | 400 | Canvas width in pixels |
| `.Height(n)` | 300 | Canvas height in pixels |
| `.Margin(l, t, r, b)` | 40, 20, 20, 30 | Axis/label margins, in `left, top, right, bottom` order |
| `.Stroke(color)` | `#4285f4` | Line/border color |
| `.Fill(color)` | `#4285f4` | Fill color |
| `.StrokeWidth(n)` | 2 | Line thickness |
| `.FillOpacity(n)` | 0.3 | Fill transparency (0--1) |
| `.ShowAxes(bool)` | true | Show axis lines and labels |
| `.ShowGrid(bool)` | true | Show horizontal grid lines |

Colors accept any CSS-style string: `#RGB`, `#RRGGBB`, `rgb(r,g,b)`, or
named colors like `steelblue`. For palette-aware colors that adapt to
dark mode, see [styling](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/styling) and the
[`.Palette(...)` accessibility modifier](#accessibility-modifiers) below.

## Binding Data to State [#binding-data-to-state]

Charts are standard Reactor elements. When state changes, the chart re-renders
with the new data:

```csharp
class CombinedChartDemo : Component
{
    private static readonly SalesPoint[] Data2024 =
    [
        new(1, 100), new(2, 140), new(3, 180),
        new(4, 200), new(5, 260), new(6, 300)
    ];

    private static readonly SalesPoint[] Data2025 =
    [
        new(1, 160), new(2, 220), new(3, 280),
        new(4, 320), new(5, 390), new(6, 450)
    ];

    private static readonly string[] Years = ["2024", "2025"];

    public override Element Render()
    {
        var (year, setYear) = UseState(0);
        var data = year == 0 ? Data2024 : Data2025;

        return VStack(12,
            SubHeading("Interactive Chart"),
            ComboBox(Years, year, setYear).AutomationName("Year"),
            AreaChart(data, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue)
                .Title("Revenue by Year")
                .SeriesName("Revenue")
                .Units("months", "USD")
                .Interactive()
                .Width(600).Height(250)
                .Stroke("#0078D4").Fill("#0078D4")
                .FillOpacity(0.15)
                .ShowGrid(true).ShowAxes(true)
        ).Padding(24);
    }
}
```

![Interactive chart](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/charting/combined-chart.png)

Use [hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks) like `UseState` to drive data selection. The chart
rebuilds on every render — keep datasets small (under ~1000 points) for
smooth interaction.

## Dynamic Data Updates [#dynamic-data-updates]

Charts are native Reactor elements, so changing state is all you need. Use
`UseState`, `UseReducer`, or any hook to update the data — the reconciler
diffs the old and new element trees and patches only what changed:

```csharp
class DynamicDataDemo : Component
{
    private static readonly List<SalesPoint> InitialPoints =
        Enumerable.Range(1, 8)
            .Select(i => new SalesPoint(i, Random.Shared.Next(50, 500)))
            .ToList();

    public override Element Render()
    {
        var (points, updatePoints) = UseReducer(InitialPoints);

        return VStack(12,
            SubHeading("Dynamic Data"),
            Button("Randomize", () => updatePoints(_ =>
                Enumerable.Range(1, 8)
                    .Select(i => new SalesPoint(i, Random.Shared.Next(50, 500)))
                    .ToList())),
            BarChart<SalesPoint>(points, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue)
                .Title("Dynamic Revenue Data")
                .SeriesName("Revenue")
                .Units("months", "USD")
                .Width(600).Height(250)
                .Fill("#E74C3C")
                .ShowGrid(true).ShowAxes(true)
        ).Padding(24);
    }
}
```

![Dynamic data](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/charting/dynamic-data.png)

For high-frequency updates (60fps streaming), use `OnReady` to get a
handle that exposes the underlying `Canvas` for direct manipulation.
This is the same compositor-property escape hatch the
[animation pipeline](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/animation-pipeline) uses — render the static
geometry through Reactor, then mutate the live values directly.

## Custom Label Elements [#custom-label-elements]

Most charts only need the string-based label APIs (`AxisLabel`,
`LabelAccessor`, `DataLabel`). Reach for the `*View` extensions only when
plain text isn't enough — for icon-plus-text ticks, multi-line labels with
mixed typography, or rendering a slice's percent inside the slice itself.

### Pie slice labels [#pie-slice-labels]

`LabelView` replaces the built-in text label on each pie slice. The delegate
receives the slice's data item plus a `PieSliceLayout` describing its
geometry, and returns any Element:

```csharp
// Percent rendered inside the slice. The string label accessor
// is still passed so screen readers describe the slice.
PieChart(Data, d => d.Value, d => d.Name)
    .Title("Team Distribution")
    .Width(300).Height(300)
    .InnerRadius(50).PadAngle(0.02)
    .LabelView((d, layout) =>
        TextBlock($"{layout.Fraction:P0}")
            .FontSize(12).Bold().Foreground(Theme.AccentText))
```

![Pie chart with the percent rendered inside each slice](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/charting/pie-label-view.png)

`PieSliceLayout` exposes the slice's `Index`, `Value`, `Fraction`,
`CentroidX`/`CentroidY`, `StartAngle`/`EndAngle`, `InnerRadius`/`OuterRadius`,
and the resolved palette `Color` so a label can echo slice geometry without
recomputing it.

### Axis tick labels [#axis-tick-labels]

`XTickLabelView` and `YTickLabelView` replace the numeric tick labels with
any Element. Each delegate receives the tick's domain value:

```csharp
// X axis ticks: render month name plus a caption per tick.
LineChart(Data, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue)
    .Title("Revenue by Month")
    .SeriesName("Revenue")
    .Width(600).Height(220)
    .Stroke("#0078D4").StrokeWidth(2.5)
    .ShowGrid(true).ShowAxes(true)
    .XTickLabelView(t => VStack(2,
        TextBlock(Months[Math.Clamp((int)t - 1, 0, Months.Length - 1)])
            .FontSize(11).SemiBold(),
        TextBlock("month").FontSize(8).Opacity(0.6)))
```

![Line chart with month-name axis ticks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/charting/axis-tick-view.png)

| Method | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `PieChartElement<T>.LabelView(Func<T, PieSliceLayout, Element>, Func<T, string>? name = null, bool interactive = false)` | Replace the built-in slice text with any Element, anchored on the slice centroid |
| `ChartElement<T>.XTickLabelView(Func<double, Element>, Func<double, string>? name = null, bool interactive = false)` | Replace the X-axis tick label, horizontally centered on the tick |
| `ChartElement<T>.YTickLabelView(Func<double, Element>, Func<double, string>? name = null, bool interactive = false)` | Replace the Y-axis tick label, right-anchored to the axis edge |

By default the element you return is rendered non-interactive: the chart
force-applies `AccessibilityView.Raw` to the **entire realized subtree** (not
just the outer wrapper) and clears `IsTabStop` on every inner control, so no
inner peer surfaces to assistive tech and nothing inside the label joins the
keyboard tab order. The chart's structured accessibility description (see
below) therefore stays the single source of truth. The element is also
auto-anchored — you don't need a known size at construction time, and the
chart re-positions on layout.

Two optional parameters refine this:

- `name` supplies an accessible-name projection for cases where you use a
  `*View` override **without** a string `LabelAccessor` (pie) / `DataLabel`
  (line/bar/area). For pie slices the projection feeds the chart's own slice
  descriptor, so the announced name matches the visible label instead of
  falling back to `Slice {n}`. For axis ticks it sets `AutomationName` on the
  realized tick element (ticks have no per-tick descriptor). Prefer the string
  `LabelAccessor`/`DataLabel` when you have one; reach for `name` only when the
  visual lives entirely in the `*View`.
- `interactive: true` is an opt-in escape hatch: it leaves the subtree's peers
  and tab stops intact so focusable children inside your label remain reachable.
  When you set it, **you** own the label's accessibility — the chart no longer
  hides it. Toggling `interactive` at runtime remounts the label so the
  hide/un-hide takes effect immediately.

## Chart Accessibility [#chart-accessibility]

Charts are fully accessible out of the box. Add `.Title()` and
`.SeriesName()` for screen-reader identification, `.Units()` for axis
annotations, and `.Interactive()` for keyboard navigation:

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Canonical accessible chart pattern — demonstrates all recommended accessibility
/// modifiers for both static and interactive charts. Follow this pattern to ensure
/// charts are fully accessible to screen readers, keyboard users, and users who
/// need forced-colors or reduced-motion.
/// </summary>
class AccessibleChartDemo : Component
{
    private static readonly SalesPoint[] Data =
    [
        new(1, 120), new(2, 180), new(3, 150),
        new(4, 220), new(5, 310), new(6, 280)
    ];

    public override Element Render()
    {
        return VStack(12,
            SubHeading("Accessible Chart"),

            // Static accessible chart: Title + SeriesName + Units
            LineChart(Data, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue)
                .Title("Monthly Revenue 2024")
                .SeriesName("Revenue")
                .Units("months", "USD")
                .AxisLabel(ChartAxisType.X, "Month")
                .AxisLabel(ChartAxisType.Y, "Revenue (USD)")
                .Width(600).Height(250)
                .Stroke("#0078D4").StrokeWidth(2.5)
                .ShowGrid(true).ShowAxes(true),

            // Interactive accessible chart: adds keyboard nav and point invocation
            BarChart(Data, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue)
                .Title("Monthly Revenue — Interactive")
                .SeriesName("Revenue")
                .Units("months", "USD")
                .Interactive()
                .Width(600).Height(250)
                .Fill("#50C878")
                .ShowGrid(true).ShowAxes(true)
        ).Padding(24);
    }
}
```

![Accessible chart](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/charting/accessible-chart.png)

### Accessibility Modifiers [#accessibility-modifiers]

| Method | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `.Title(str)` | Visible title and accessible name |
| `.Description(str)` | Override auto-generated summary |
| `.SeriesName(str)` | Name the data series |
| `.Units(x, y)` | Axis unit annotations (e.g., "months", "USD") |
| `.AxisLabel(axis, str)` | Explicit axis label |
| `.Interactive()` | Enable keyboard navigation and virtual focus |
| `.OnPointInvoke(handler)` | Callback when Enter/Space pressed on a point |
| `.AlternateView(element)` | Toggle between chart and data table (T key) |
| `.Palette(palette)` | Curated colorblind-safe palette |
| `.SeriesColors(colors)` | Custom series colors (scanner-validated) |
| `.SetColors(colors)` | Custom pie-slice colors (scanner-validated; pie counterpart to `.SeriesColors`) |
| `.RawColors(colors)` | Raw series colors — escape hatch, no validation (Tier 4) |
| `.ChartBackground(color)` | Declare the rendered background so palette-contrast (A11Y_CHART_011) is checked against that single active background (warning) instead of either fixed light/dark background (info) |
| `.SeriesShapes(shapes)` | Marker shapes for double-encoding |
| `.SeriesDashes(dashes)` | Dash patterns for double-encoding |

Screen readers announce the chart type, series count, data range, and
individual point values. Keyboard users navigate with arrow keys, invoke
points with Enter, and toggle an alternate data-table view with T. The
full a11y story for the framework is in [accessibility](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/accessibility);
the chart-specific contract is that color is never the only encoding —
combine `.Palette(...)` with `.SeriesShapes(...)` or `.SeriesDashes(...)`
for any multi-series chart that ships to forced-colors users.

## Low-Level Drawing [#low-level-drawing]

For custom visualizations, ReactorD3 provides shape generators and a Canvas
DSL. Import `using static Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Charting.D3Charts;` for:

- **`D3Canvas(w, h, children)`** — create a drawing surface
- **`D3Rect`, `D3Circle`, `D3Line`, `D3Path`** — primitive shapes
- **`Text`, `TextRight`, `TextCenter`** — positioned text
- **`D3LinePath<T>`, `D3AreaPath<T>`, `D3ArcPath`** — generator helpers
- **`D3Axes`, `D3Grid`, `D3Legend`** — axis/legend composites
- **`Brush(color)`, `Palette`** — brushes and the default categorical palette

These three are **positional**: `Text(x, y, text, …)` takes canvas
coordinates and is unrelated to the core `TextBlock(...)` factory. Reactor has
no core `Text(...)` element factory — the `Text(...)` members that exist
elsewhere are the DataGrid cell-renderer and editor helpers, which return
`Func<object, Element>`, not an `Element`.

The scales are types, not `D3Charts` members — they live one namespace deeper.
Add `using Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Charting.D3;` to reach them.

## Scale Types [#scale-types]

Every scale exposes `.Map(value)` to project a domain value into range space —
scales are objects, not delegates, so `scale(v)` does not compile. Construct
one with `new LinearScale(domain, range)` or configure it fluently with
`.SetDomain(...)` / `.SetRange(...)`.

| Scale | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `LinearScale` | Continuous numeric mapping with `.Nice()` and `.Ticks()` |
| `BandScale<T>` | Categorical mapping with bandwidth (bar charts) |
| `LogScale` | Logarithmic mapping for exponential data |
| `PowScale` | Power/sqrt mapping |
| `OrdinalScale<T>` | Discrete-to-discrete mapping |

> **Caveat:** Recreate the data array inside `Render()` only at your own peril.
> Charts compare incoming data by reference on the fast path — a new
> array on every render means the chart re-derives scales, re-runs the
> pie layout, and re-allocates the WinUI shape pool every frame, even
> when nothing changed. The symptom is a chart that flickers when an
> unrelated piece of state updates. The fix is the same shape Reactor
> uses everywhere: wrap the data in `UseMemo(() => …, deps)` keyed on
> whatever actually changes. The pattern is most obvious with
> `PieChart` — a fresh `new[] { … }` on every render makes each slice
> remount, the `.Transition()` enter/exit fires for slices that haven't
> moved, and the chart "redraws itself" on every keystroke into an
> unrelated `TextBox`.

## Patterns [#patterns]

### Live-updating chart from a ticking source [#live-updating-chart-from-a-ticking-source]

A streaming chart — a price feed, a sensor reading — drives a sliding
window of points. Hold the window in `UseReducer` (each tick derives the
next window from the previous one), append on tick, drop the head once
`Count` exceeds the window size. `UseEffect` takes a synchronous
`Action`/`Func<Action>`, never an `async` lambda, so start the pump from
the effect and cancel it from the returned cleanup:

```csharp
record Sample(DateTime Time, double Value);

class LiveChartDemo : Component
{
    public override Element Render()
    {
        var (samples, updateSamples) = UseReducer<IReadOnlyList<Sample>>(Array.Empty<Sample>());

        // UseEffect takes a synchronous Action/Func<Action> — never an async lambda.
        // Start the pump from the effect and cancel it from the returned cleanup.
        UseEffect(() =>
        {
            var cts = new CancellationTokenSource();
            _ = PumpAsync(cts.Token);
            return () => { cts.Cancel(); };
        }, Array.Empty<object>());

        return VStack(12,
            SubHeading("Live feed"),
            LineChart(samples, s => s.Time.Ticks, s => s.Value)
                .Title("Live feed")
                .SeriesName("Value")
                .Width(600).Height(220)
                .Stroke("#0078D4")
        ).Padding(24);

        async Task PumpAsync(CancellationToken token)
        {
            using var timer = new PeriodicTimer(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(200));
            try
            {
                while (await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(token))
                {
                    updateSamples(prev =>
                    {
                        var next = prev.Append(new Sample(DateTime.Now, Random.Shared.Next(0, 100))).ToList();
                        return next.Count > 60 ? next.Skip(next.Count - 60).ToList() : next;
                    });
                }
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException)
            {
                // Expected on unmount.
            }
        }
    }
}
```

The chart redraws on every tick. For sub-100ms cadence, drop into
`OnReady` and mutate the `Canvas` directly — the reconciler is fast
but it isn't free. See [effects-scheduling](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/effects-scheduling) for
the timer-cleanup pattern.

### Switching chart type without losing the data binding [#switching-chart-type-without-losing-the-data-binding]

The same data feeds a line, a bar, or an area chart — let users pick
the shape. Hold the selected `ComboBox` **index** in state and switch the
factory call on it:

```csharp
class ChartSwitchDemo : Component
{
    private static readonly SalesPoint[] Data =
    [
        new(1, 120), new(2, 180), new(3, 150), new(4, 220), new(5, 310), new(6, 280)
    ];

    public override Element Render()
    {
        // ComboBox reports the selected *index*, so hold an int and branch on it.
        var (kind, setKind) = UseState(0);
        var kinds = new[] { "line", "bar", "area" };

        // Each factory returns ChartElement<T>, so the switch has one common type
        // and the modifier chain below is shared.
        ChartElement<SalesPoint> chart = kind switch
        {
            0 => LineChart(Data, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue),
            1 => BarChart(Data, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue),
            _ => AreaChart(Data, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue),
        };

        return VStack(8,
            SubHeading("Switch chart type"),
            ComboBox(kinds, kind, setKind).AutomationName("Chart type"),
            chart
                .Title("Revenue")
                .SeriesName("Revenue")
                .Width(600).Height(250)
                .Stroke("#0078D4")
        ).Padding(24);
    }
}
```

Because each factory returns a `ChartElement<T>`, the modifier chain is
identical — the only branching is the constructor.

### Dropping into D3 for a custom shape [#dropping-into-d3-for-a-custom-shape]

When the high-level surface doesn't fit (heatmap, parallel coordinates,
swarm plot), render `D3Canvas` directly and compose D3 shape generators.
The `LinearScale` / `BandScale` types are the same ones the high-level
charts use internally, so behavior matches — `.Nice()`, `.Ticks()`, and
the domain/range setters work identically. `D3Axes` and `D3Grid` return
`Element[]`, so spread them into the canvas children with `..`:

```csharp
class D3CustomDemo : Component
{
    public override Element Render()
    {
        const double w = 600, h = 240;
        const double left = 50, top = 20, right = 20, bottom = 40;
        double plotW = w - left - right, plotH = h - top - bottom;

        var data = Enumerable.Range(0, 40)
            .Select(i => (x: (double)i, y: 40 + 30 * Math.Sin(i / 4.0) + i))
            .ToArray();

        var (yMin, yMax) = D3Extent.Extent(data.Select(d => d.y));

        // Scales are plain objects: Set* mutates fluently, Map projects a value.
        var xs = new LinearScale([0, 39], [left, left + plotW]);
        var ys = new LinearScale([yMax, yMin], [top, top + plotH]).Nice();

        var line = D3Charts.Brush("#0078D4");

        return VStack(12,
            SubHeading("Custom D3 canvas"),
            D3Charts.D3Canvas(w, h,
                [.. D3Charts.D3Grid(ys, left, plotW),
                 .. D3Charts.D3Axes(xs, ys, left, top, plotW, plotH),
                 D3Charts.D3LinePath(data, x: d => xs.Map(d.x), y: d => ys.Map(d.y),
                     stroke: line, strokeWidth: 2),
                 .. data.Select(d => (Element)(D3Charts.D3Circle(xs.Map(d.x), ys.Map(d.y), 3)
                     with { Fill = line }))])
        ).Padding(24);
    }
}
```

This is the same composition strategy Observable Plot uses — geometric
primitives over scales — except the primitives render as WinUI shapes,
not SVG. For a heatmap, swap `D3LinePath` for nested
`D3Rect`s; for parallel coordinates, repeat the line-path call per axis.

## Common Mistakes [#common-mistakes]

### Constructing the data array in Render [#constructing-the-data-array-in-render]

```csharp
// Don't:
public override Element Render()
{
    var data = new SalesPoint[] { new(1, 120), new(2, 180), /* … */ };
    return LineChart(data, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue);
}
```

```csharp
class DynamicDataDemo : Component
{
    private static readonly List<SalesPoint> InitialPoints =
        Enumerable.Range(1, 8)
            .Select(i => new SalesPoint(i, Random.Shared.Next(50, 500)))
            .ToList();

    public override Element Render()
    {
        var (points, updatePoints) = UseReducer(InitialPoints);

        return VStack(12,
            SubHeading("Dynamic Data"),
            Button("Randomize", () => updatePoints(_ =>
                Enumerable.Range(1, 8)
                    .Select(i => new SalesPoint(i, Random.Shared.Next(50, 500)))
                    .ToList())),
            BarChart<SalesPoint>(points, d => d.Month, d => d.Revenue)
                .Title("Dynamic Revenue Data")
                .SeriesName("Revenue")
                .Units("months", "USD")
                .Width(600).Height(250)
                .Fill("#E74C3C")
                .ShowGrid(true).ShowAxes(true)
        ).Padding(24);
    }
}
```

Every render allocates a new array, so the chart's reference-equality
check fails, scales re-derive, and shape pools reset — even though
nothing visible changed. Hoist the static data into a `static readonly`
field or wrap dynamic data in `UseMemo(() => BuildData(...), deps)`.

### Using color as the only series encoding [#using-color-as-the-only-series-encoding]

```csharp
// Don't:
LineChart(serverA, ...).Stroke("red"),
LineChart(serverB, ...).Stroke("green"),
LineChart(serverC, ...).Stroke("blue")
```

In forced-colors mode (Windows High Contrast), every stroke collapses
to the active accent color and the user can't tell the series apart.
Pair color with
`.SeriesShapes(MarkerShape.Circle, MarkerShape.Square, MarkerShape.Triangle)`
or `.SeriesDashes(DashStyle.Solid, DashStyle.Dash4_2, DashStyle.Dash2_2)`
so the series is identifiable without color. Same principle as charts in
WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1.

### Animating individual D3 shapes by hand [#animating-individual-d3-shapes-by-hand]

```csharp
// Don't:
D3Circle(xs.Map(d.X), ys.Map(d.Y), 3)
    .Set(c =>
    {
        var anim = c.Compositor.CreateScalarKeyFrameAnimation();
        anim.InsertKeyFrame(0f, 0.0f);
        anim.InsertKeyFrame(1f, 1.0f);
        anim.Target = "Opacity";
        c.StartAnimation(anim);
    })
```

Inline composition animation duplicates what `.OpacityTransition()`
and `.Transition(Transition.Fade)` already do, and it bypasses the
reduced-motion preference Reactor honors at the
[animation pipeline](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/animation-pipeline) level. Use the Reactor
animation modifiers on the D3 shape — they work the same way they do
on a `Border` or `TextBlock`.

## Tips [#tips]

**Start with the high-level DSL.** `LineChart`, `BarChart`, `AreaChart`, and
`PieChart` cover most dashboard needs without touching scales or generators.

**Use `.ShowGrid(true)` for readability.** Grid lines make it much easier
to read values from a chart, especially line and area charts.

**Keep datasets under 1000 points.** Each data point creates WinUI shapes on
a Canvas. For larger datasets, aggregate or sample before charting.

**Just change state for live data.** Charts diff efficiently — updating
state triggers the reconciler to patch only what changed. For 60fps
escape hatches, use `OnReady` to access the underlying Canvas directly.

**Use donut charts (`InnerRadius > 0`) for proportional data.** The center
space works well for displaying a total or label.
