## `RichTextInlineUIContainer` [#richtextinlineuicontainer]

Mirrors WinUI's `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Documents.InlineUIContainer` — an inline that embeds a UIElement inside a flowing [`RichTextBlockElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/text#richtextblockelement).

**Two embedding routes** (issue #480):

- **Route A — Reactor element ([`RichTextInlineUIContainer.Child`](#child)):** the embedded UI is described declaratively as any other Reactor [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) (e.g. `Button("+", () => ...)`) and is mounted through the reconciler. The descriptor uses an incremental rich-text update path: re-renders of the owning `RichTextBlock` preserve the existing inline UIElement and reconcile the Reactor child via the standard child-reconciliation pipeline, so embedded interactive controls (sliders, buttons, etc.) keep their drag focus and component state across renders. A structural change to the surrounding paragraph tree (different paragraph count, mismatched inline shape) falls back to a full rebuild that tears down and remounts the child along with the rest of the block.
- **Route B — imperative native factory ([`RichTextInlineUIContainer.Factory`](#factory)):** the embedded UI is produced by a caller-supplied lambda returning a raw WinUI [`FrameworkElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.frameworkelement). Useful as an escape hatch for native controls that have no Reactor element counterpart. The factory is opaque to the reconciler, so the incremental path re-invokes it only when the delegate identity itself changes (capture-equal lambdas are treated as unchanged) — pass a stable delegate reference if you want the native UIElement to survive renders.

Exactly one of [`RichTextInlineUIContainer.Child`](#child) / [`RichTextInlineUIContainer.Factory`](#factory) should be non-null. If both are null the inline expands to a zero-size empty container; if both are set, [`RichTextInlineUIContainer.Child`](#child) wins.

```csharp
public record RichTextInlineUIContainer : RichTextInline
```

# Async values
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/async-values

**Learn more:** [Async Resources](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/async-resources)

## `AsyncValue<T>` [#asyncvaluet]

Algebraic data type representing the four observable states of an async fetch: [`AsyncValue<T>.Loading`](#asyncvaluetloading), [`AsyncValue<T>.Data`](#asyncvaluetdata), [`AsyncValue<T>.Error`](#asyncvalueterror), and [`AsyncValue<T>.Reloading`](#asyncvaluetreloading). Designed for exhaustive pattern matching with C# switch expressions: the hierarchy is `closed`, so a C# 15+ `switch` that handles all four cases needs no discard arm, and omitting a case is a CS8509 warning naming the missing case.

```csharp
public abstract record AsyncValue<T>
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`.

### Remarks [#remarks]

See spec `docs/specs/020-async-resources-design.md` §5 for the design rationale and §6.2 for the transition rules driven by `UseResource`.

### Type parameters [#type-parameters]

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `T` | The value type produced by the fetcher. |

### Constructors [#constructors]

#### `AsyncValue` [#asyncvalue]

```csharp
protected AsyncValue()
```

### Methods [#methods]

#### `Match` [#match]

Convenience match that renders the `loading` arm for [`AsyncValue<T>.Reloading`](#asyncvaluetreloading) by default. Pass `reloading` explicitly to show stale content while a refresh is in progress (stale-while-revalidate).

```csharp
public TResult Match<TResult>(Func<TResult> loading, Func<T, TResult> loaded, Func<Exception, TResult> error, Func<T, TResult>? reloading = null)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `loading` | `Func<TResult>` |  |  |
| `loaded` | `Func<T, TResult>` |  |  |
| `error` | `Func<Exception, TResult>` |  |  |
| `reloading` | `Func<T, TResult>?` | `null` |  |

**Remarks**

Omitting `reloading` means a refresh shows the loading UI, so authors don't have to duplicate the loading arm. Provide `reloading` to keep the previous value visible while revalidating.

The success arm is named `loaded`. This is a source-breaking rename from the previous `data` parameter for named-argument callers; a back-compat overload is impossible because overloads cannot differ by parameter name alone.

Allocates a delegate per arm at the call site; prefer a `switch` expression in per-row render paths (see spec §5.1).

### `AsyncValue<T>.Data` [#asyncvaluetdata]

Fetch succeeded; `Value` is authoritative. Transitions to [`AsyncValue<T>.Reloading`](#asyncvaluetreloading) when a refetch starts, or back to [`AsyncValue<T>.Data`](#asyncvaluetdata) on cache hit within `StaleTime`.

```csharp
public sealed record Data(T Value) : AsyncValue<T>
```

# FocusRevalidationService
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/FocusRevalidationService

Central service that invalidates stale [`QueryCache`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/query-cache#querycache) entries when the app window is reactivated or resumed, so consumers that opted in via `ResourceOptions.RefetchOnWindowFocus = true` see fresh data after an Alt-Tab or resume. Disabled by default — see [`ReactorFeatureFlags.FocusRevalidation`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorFeatureFlags#focusrevalidation).

```csharp
public sealed class FocusRevalidationService
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`.

**Learn more:** [Async Resources](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/async-resources)

## Remarks [#remarks]

**Per-resource enrollment.** Hooks that opt in call [`FocusRevalidationService.Enroll`](#enroll) with their cache key; the service tracks enrolled keys as a set and invalidates only those whose entry is past `StaleTime` at activation time. Non-enrolled keys are untouched.

**Throttling.** A default 30-second window between activation-driven revalidation sweeps prevents Alt-Tab thrashing from refetching on every transient focus event. Adjustable via [`FocusRevalidationService.ThrottleWindow`](#throttlewindow).

**Threading.** All members are thread-safe. Activation callbacks may fire on the UI thread or the dispatcher thread — the service does not marshal. Invalidation in turn fires `QueryCache.EntryChanged`, which the `UseResource` hook listens to and re-renders from.

## Constructors [#constructors]

### `FocusRevalidationService` [#focusrevalidationservice_1]

```csharp
public FocusRevalidationService(QueryCache cache)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cache` | [`QueryCache`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/query-cache#querycache) |  |

```csharp

```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` |  |

### `RevalidateNow` [#revalidatenow]

Revalidate enrolled entries. Invalidates every enrolled key whose entry is past its `StaleTime`. Returns the keys that were invalidated.

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<string> RevalidateNow()
```

**Remarks**

Short-circuits if the last call fired within [`FocusRevalidationService.ThrottleWindow`](#throttlewindow) — returns an empty list without touching the cache.

### `RevalidateNowForce` [#revalidatenowforce]

Forces a revalidation sweep, bypassing the throttle window. Diagnostic / test-only — production code paths should go through [`FocusRevalidationService.RevalidateNow`](#revalidatenow).

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<string> RevalidateNowForce()
```

## `DataPageCache<T>` [#datapagecachet]

Caches pages of data from IDataSource, keyed by sort/filter state + page index. Evicts blocks outside the viewport via LRU when max capacity is reached.

Follows a pull model (matching Compose Paging 3): accessing a row index that falls in an unloaded block triggers the fetch. The virtualizer tells the cache which blocks are needed; the cache returns immediately for loaded blocks and initiates async loads for missing ones.

```csharp
public class DataPageCache<T>
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Data`.

### Constructors [#constructors_2]

#### `DataPageCache` [#datapagecache]

Creates a new DataPageCache.

```csharp
public DataPageCache(IDataSource<T> source, int blockSize = 50, int maxBlocks = 20)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | [`IDataSource<T>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/IDataSource) |  | The data source to cache. |
| `blockSize` | `int` | `50` | Number of items per block (page size). Default 50. |
| `maxBlocks` | `int` | `20` | Maximum number of blocks to keep in cache. Default 20. |

### Properties [#properties_2]

Number of items per block.

```csharp
public int BlockSize  // get
```

#### `RequestBlock` [#requestblock]

Request that a block be loaded if it isn't already cached or in-flight. The fetch is deferred via Task.Yield so it never runs synchronously in the caller's stack frame, but stays on the caller's thread (UI thread). Fires [`DataPageCache.BlockLoaded`](#blockloaded) on completion.

## `InfiniteResource<TItem>` [#infiniteresourcetitem]

Pull-model paginated result view. Each call-site of `UseInfiniteResource` owns a single [`InfiniteResource<TItem>`](#infiniteresourcetitem); virtualized controls call [`InfiniteResource.ItemAt`](#itemat) / [`InfiniteResource.EnsureRange`](#ensurerange) per row to drive fetches, and render `null` slots as placeholders.

```csharp
public sealed class InfiniteResource<TItem>
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`.

### Remarks [#remarks]

All mutating methods are UI-thread-affined. Internally the implementation shares a lock for structural mutations (page table, cursor, load state). Callers should not enumerate [`InfiniteResource.Items`](#items_2) from a background thread.

### Properties [#properties_3]

#### `EstimatedRemaining` [#estimatedremaining]

Approximate number of items not yet loaded. 0 once [`InfiniteResource.HasMore`](#hasmore) is false.

```csharp
public int EstimatedRemaining  // get
```

#### `HasMore` [#hasmore]

True iff the server has not yet reported `NextCursor == null`.

```csharp
public bool HasMore  // get
```

#### `Items` [#items_2]

Flat, virtualized view. Indices beyond loaded content are either null-placeholders (in-flight or about-to-fetch) or, past the known end, not returned.

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<TItem?> Items  // get
```

Current load state — updated on every fetch lifecycle event.

## `QueryCache` [#querycache]

Process-wide query cache with TTL, ref-counted subscriptions, and pattern invalidation. Shared across components via [`Context<T>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/Context) — see [`AppContexts.QueryCache`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/AppContexts#querycache).

```csharp
public sealed class QueryCache : IDisposable
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`.

### Remarks [#remarks]

**Threading.** All public methods are safe to call from any thread. Slots are protected by a per-key lock; [`QueryCache.EntryChanged`](#entrychanged) fires either inline or on the configured [`QueryCache.DispatcherPost`](#dispatcherpost) callback (set by `ReactorHost` at bootstrap). Tests can leave it null to observe events inline.

**Eviction.** A single shared timer (started lazily on first subscription) polls all slots every [`QueryCache.EvictionPollInterval`](#evictionpollinterval). Slots whose `SubscriberCount == 0` for longer than their `CacheTime` are evicted. Using one timer keeps the entry count's impact on system timers O(1).

### Constructors [#constructors_1]

#### `QueryCache` [#querycache_1]

```csharp
public QueryCache()
```

### Properties [#properties_1]

#### `Count` [#count]

Snapshot the current cache size. Diagnostic only — do not use for correctness.

```csharp
public int Count  // get
```

#### `DispatcherPost` [#dispatcherpost]

Injected marshaller for [`QueryCache.EntryChanged`](#entrychanged). Null → fires inline.

```csharp
public Action<Action>? DispatcherPost  // get, set
```

#### `EvictionPollInterval` [#evictionpollinterval]

How often the eviction timer checks every slot for expiry. Default 1s.

```csharp
public static TimeSpan EvictionPollInterval  // get, set
```

#### `UtcNow` [#utcnow]

Clock override for deterministic tests.

```csharp
public Func<DateTime> UtcNow  // get, set
```

### Methods [#methods]

#### `Clear` [#clear]

Removes every entry. Subscribers are retained. Fires [`QueryCache.EntryChanged`](#entrychanged) once per key that actually held a value.

```csharp
public void Clear()
```

#### `Dispose` [#dispose]

Releases the resources that this object holds.

```csharp
public void Dispose()
```

#### `EvictNow` [#evictnow]

Test / diagnostic hook: drive the eviction sweep explicitly rather than waiting for the background [`QueryCache.EvictionPollInterval`](#evictionpollinterval) timer. Returns the set of keys that were evicted on this pass. Safe to call from any thread.

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<string> EvictNow()
```

**Remarks**

Production code should not need this — subscribers keep entries alive and the shared timer evicts zero-subscriber entries past their `CacheTime`. It's exposed publicly so framerate / stress tests can make eviction deterministic.

#### `Invalidate` [#invalidate]

Removes the entry (if any) for `key`. Subscribers are retained — the next [`QueryCache.Set`](#set) will see their count. Fires [`QueryCache.EntryChanged`](#entrychanged) if there was an entry to remove.

```csharp
public void Invalidate(string key)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` |  |

#### `InvalidatePattern` [#invalidatepattern]

Invalidates every key that starts with `keyPrefix`. O(n) in the number of cached keys — document the pattern prefix carefully if you store a lot of unrelated keys under one cache.

```csharp

```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

#### `TryGet` [#tryget]

Retrieves the current entry for `key` if present and typed as `T`. Returns false on miss or on type-mismatch. Staleness is a caller-side decision — the entry's [`CacheEntry.FetchedAt`](#fetchedat) and [`CacheEntry.StaleTime`](#staletime) are both returned on a hit.


**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` |  |
| `entry` | [`CacheEntry<T>`](#cacheentryt) |  |

#### `Unsubscribe` [#unsubscribe]

Decrements the subscriber count. When it reaches zero, starts the eviction clock based on the slot's most recent [`QueryCache.Set`](#set) `cacheTime`. Throws [`InvalidOperationException`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.invalidoperationexception) if called on a slot that has no subscribers — this catches hook-logic bugs that would otherwise hide underflow forever.

```csharp
public int Unsubscribe(string key)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` |  |

# ReactorEvent
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/diagnostics/ReactorEvent

A single event captured from the `Microsoft-UI-Reactor` [`EventSource`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.tracing.eventsource), delivered to subscribers of [`ReactorTrace.Subscribe`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/diagnostics/ReactorTrace#subscribe).

The payload arrays come from [`EventWrittenEventArgs.Payload`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.tracing.eventwritteneventargs.payload) and [`EventWrittenEventArgs.PayloadNames`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.tracing.eventwritteneventargs.payloadnames) directly — no reflection is involved, so this surface is AOT/trim-clean.

PII discipline: every framework event has already stripped sensitive fields (no [`Exception.Message`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.exception.message), no window titles, no instantiated route paths). Subscribers should respect that policy in any downstream sink they forward to.

```csharp
public readonly record struct ReactorEvent(int EventId, string EventName, EventLevel Level, EventKeywords Keywords, DateTime TimestampUtc, int ThreadId, IReadOnlyList<object?> Payload, IReadOnlyList<string> PayloadNames)
```

# ReactorSourceMap
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/diagnostics/ReactorSourceMap

**Why a runtime flag at all.** Interceptors are baked in at compile time, so without a runtime gate every Debug build would pay the stamping cost whether or not anyone is inspecting. This flag is what the emitted interceptor checks before writing a location, so an un-inspected Debug session allocates nothing extra.

**It does not change control tagging for leaves.** The reconciler attaches a `ReactorState` (the control → element back-pointer) only to controls that something will read back — callbacks, a key, extras, or reference modifiers (see `Reconciler.NeedsTag`), which is the allocation win PR #468 landed. `NeedsTag` has no arm for this flag on ordinary elements: a stamped element carries its `CallSite` in the `Extensions` bucket and so already satisfies the existing `Extensions is not null` test. Adding one would only tag *unstamped* elements, which have no location to return, while re-introducing the per-leaf allocation. Elements the generator does not reach (wrapper factories, bare-string children) therefore stay untagged and report no location rather than a wrong one. The one exception is component boundaries: while this flag is on, every component's Border wrapper is tagged so an inspector can find where each component starts — one allocation per component, never per leaf.

**Who turns it on.** The devtools session switch. `ReactorApp` sets [`ReactorSourceMap.Enabled`](#enabled) when the process was launched with `--devtools app` / `--devtools run`, so a retail session never pays. It is public-settable so a host that embeds its own inspector (or a test) can opt in without going through the CLI.

```csharp
public static class ReactorSourceMap
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Diagnostics`.

**Learn more:** [Diagnostics](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/tools/diagnostics)

## Properties [#properties]

### `Enabled` [#enabled]

True when source mapping is active for this process. Read by every generated factory interceptor before it stamps, so it is an `int` + `Volatile` rather than a lock.

```csharp
public static bool Enabled  // get, set
```

## Methods [#methods]

### `GetSource` [#getsource]

Resolves the DSL call site that produced `control`.

This is the whole read chain, and it deliberately reuses the back-pointer that already exists rather than adding a second attached property: `UIElement` → `ReactorAttached.StateProperty` → `ReactorState.Element` → [`Element.CallSite`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element#callsite).

Returns `null` when the control was not produced by Reactor, or when the element behind it carries no [`Element.CallSite`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element#callsite) — because it was built while [`ReactorSourceMap.Enabled`](#enabled) was false, or because no provider reaches that factory (see the known limitations in the source-mapping guide). Note this is a property of the ELEMENT, not of tagging: a control can be tagged for unrelated reasons (callbacks, a key, other extras) and still report no location, and an element hand-stamped with a `CallSite` reports one even with the flag off.

Target-wrapping decorators are resolved through. `Flyout`, `MenuFlyout` and `CommandBarFlyout` mount their `Target`'s control and then deliberately replace that control's tag with themselves, because their Opened/Closed handlers read it back. The realized control is still the target's — a `Button` inside a `Flyout(...)` was created by the `Button(` line — so reporting the decorator's line would name the wrong creator, the same misattribution the generator avoids for pass-through factories. The walk is a loop so nested decorators resolve to the innermost target.

Native AOT in diagnostics mode does not tag a control whose element's only extra is its call site (no managed inspector can load to read the tag); there the location is resolved from the control's published `ReactorSource` value and is the same [`SourceLocation`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/SourceLocation) the tag would give.

Menu and command-bar items a flyout, menu bar or command bar builds from item records (`MenuItem(…)`, `AppBarButton(…)`) carry no element tag; in diagnostics mode their location is resolved the same way, from their published value.

```csharp
public static SourceLocation? GetSource(UIElement control)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `control` | `UIElement` |  |

# ReactorSourceTransparentAttribute
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/diagnostics/ReactorSourceTransparentAttribute

Without this, a thin forwarding helper collapses every one of its call sites onto a single line, because an interceptor replaces the *call site* and the call site of `TextBlock(...)` in `static Element MyHeader() => TextBlock("header");` is inside `MyHeader`. Annotating `MyHeader` flips the attribution outward: the source-map generator emits no interceptor for the factory calls in its body, and instead intercepts calls *to* `MyHeader` and stamps the caller's line.

**Deliberately opt-in.** It is not a blanket rule for helpers, because for most element-returning methods the body line is the RIGHT answer — a `Component.Render()` body is where the author actually wrote the UI, and deferring it to the reconciler's call site would be a regression. Only a thin forwarder, whose own line carries no information a reader wants, benefits. This attribute is how that intent is expressed.

**Nesting.** Annotated methods compose: a transparent helper calling another transparent helper keeps deferring outward until it reaches a caller that is not annotated, and that caller's line is what gets stamped.

``[ReactorSourceTransparent] internal static Element Field(string label, string value) => HStack(TextBlock(label), TextBlock(value)); // Both rows report THEIR OWN line, instead of both reporting the // `HStack(` line inside Field. var form = VStack( Field("Name", name), Field("Email", email));``

```csharp
public sealed class ReactorSourceTransparentAttribute : Attribute
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Diagnostics`. Inherits from [`Attribute`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.attribute).

**Learn more:** [Diagnostics](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/tools/diagnostics)

## Remarks [#remarks]

**Requirements.** The generator has to be able to emit an interceptor that forwards to the annotated method, so it must be `static`, return an `Element`, and be reachable by name from a generated file in the same compilation — i.e. `public` or `internal` (never `private`), not declared in a `file`-local or generic type, and not a local function (C# interceptors cannot intercept those). An annotation the generator cannot honour is reported as `REACTOR_SOURCEMAP_001` rather than silently doing nothing, and attribution falls back to today's behaviour — the helper's own line — so a bad annotation never makes attribution worse than no annotation.

**Where it takes effect.** Rule 1 (suppressing stamps inside the body) applies in the compilation that *declares* the method; rule 2 (stamping at the call site) applies in the compilation that *calls* it. Both need the source-map generator loaded, so annotating a method in a library whose consumer has not enabled `ReactorSourceMap` simply leaves those elements unstamped.

A plain marker attribute with no members and no reflection surface, so it is trim- and AOT-safe. It is read by the generator from metadata, which is why it must be `public`.

## Constructors [#constructors]

### `ReactorSourceTransparentAttribute` [#reactorsourcetransparentattribute_1]

```csharp
public ReactorSourceTransparentAttribute()
```

# ReactorTrace
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/diagnostics/ReactorTrace

In-process subscription helper for the `Microsoft-UI-Reactor` [`EventSource`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.tracing.eventsource). Lets an app developer (or an internal devtools surface — `reactor.logs` MCP, an `ILogger` bridge) observe framework events without writing an [`EventListener`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.tracing.eventlistener) subclass.

This is deliberately **not** a file-capture API. The .NET runtime already provides three:

- `DOTNET_EnableEventPipe` + `DOTNET_EventPipeOutputPath` environment variables (zero app code).
- `dotnet-trace collect --providers Microsoft-UI-Reactor`.
- Visual Studio Performance Profiler → Events Viewer.

See `docs/guide/diagnostics.md` for end-to-end examples.

```csharp
public static class ReactorTrace
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Diagnostics`.

**Learn more:** [Diagnostics](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/tools/diagnostics)

## Methods [#methods]

### `GetComponentControl` [#getcomponentcontrol]

Resolves the `componentId` carried by a `ComponentRendered` event (`Microsoft-UI-Reactor` EventId 40) to the realized control whose bounds are that component's — the component's wrapper, or for a host's root component the host's current root content control. Use it to flash the region that just re-rendered ("highlight updates").

Returns `null` for `0`, for an id this process never issued, once the component has unmounted or its control was collected, and while the control does not exist yet: a component's mount event is raised before its subtree mounts (the id is mapped once that finishes), and a root's first event before its reconcile pass has produced the content. An id from a render whose subtree was then discarded — caught by an `ErrorBoundary`, or a failure that propagated — may never resolve. So resolve after the pass completes (e.g. on the next dispatcher tick) rather than inside the event callback, and treat `null` as "nothing on screen for this id". Ids are only issued, and controls only recorded, while the event is enabled, so subscribe first.

Call on the UI thread; the returned control is a live WinUI object.

```csharp
public static UIElement? GetComponentControl(long componentId)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `componentId` | `long` | The event's `componentId` payload field. |

### `Subscribe` [#subscribe]

Subscribes to `Microsoft-UI-Reactor` events in-process. Returns an [`IDisposable`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.idisposable) token; dispose it to detach.

The callback fires on the emission thread — typically the UI dispatcher when an event originates from reconcile / render, or a thread-pool thread otherwise. Keep the callback work minimal and never let it throw across the framework boundary — a throwing subscriber propagates into [`EventSource`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.tracing.eventsource)'s emit path and surfaces as an ETW failure.

Multiple concurrent subscribers are supported. Each subscriber's `level` and `keywords` are independently active until the returned token is disposed; the runtime unions them when computing whether `IsEnabled` on the event source returns true. Be aware that a broad subscriber ([`EventLevel.Verbose`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.tracing.eventlevel.verbose) + all keywords) raises the cost of every hot-path call site on the framework for as long as it lives.

For writing a trace file, use one of:

- `DOTNET_EnableEventPipe` / `DOTNET_EventPipeOutputPath` env vars.
- `dotnet-trace collect --providers Microsoft-UI-Reactor`.
- Visual Studio Performance Profiler → Events Viewer.

```csharp
public static IDisposable Subscribe(Action<ReactorEvent> onEvent, EventLevel level = (EventLevel)5, EventKeywords keywords = (EventKeywords)-1)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onEvent` | `Action<ReactorEvent>` |  | Callback invoked once per matching event. Must be non-null. |
| `level` | `EventLevel` | `(EventLevel)5` | Minimum severity to forward. Defaults to [`EventLevel.Verbose`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.tracing.eventlevel.verbose) so subscribers see everything (state changes, per-trampoline dispatches) unless they explicitly pass a stricter level. |
| `keywords` | `EventKeywords` | `(EventKeywords)-1` | Keyword mask to forward. Defaults to all keywords (`(EventKeywords)(-1)`). |

**Returns:** Disposable token. Disposing detaches the underlying [`EventListener`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.tracing.eventlistener); subsequent events do not reach `onEvent`.

**Exceptions**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`ArgumentNullException`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentnullexception) | If `onEvent` is `null`. |

### `TryGetComponentId` [#trygetcomponentid]

The reverse of [`ReactorTrace.GetComponentControl`](#getcomponentcontrol): the `componentId` that `ComponentRendered` events use for the component rendering into `control` (a component's wrapper control). Lets an inspector filter the event stream down to the component a user selected.

Returns `false` when `control` is not a component wrapper, or when that component has not rendered since `ComponentRendered` was enabled. A host's root id is never returned here — the root content control is often also a child component's wrapper, and that child keeps the mapping.

Call on the UI thread: the id is read from the control's Reactor state.

```csharp
public static bool TryGetComponentId(UIElement control, out long componentId)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `control` | `UIElement` |  |
| `componentId` | `long` |  |

**Exceptions**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`ArgumentNullException`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentnullexception) | If `control` is `null`. |

Values are not redacted: an inspector that shows them where a secret must not appear hides them itself. Empty when the hook has no value (effects).

```csharp
public string Value  // get, init
```

## `KeyedListDiagnostic` [#keyedlistdiagnostic]

One captured keyed-list key diagnostic: a null key, or duplicate keys in a keyed list or among a panel's `.WithKey` siblings. A list with duplicate keys is rebuilt in full when it changes (a bailout); a null-keyed item is matched by position and the list keeps diffing incrementally. Reported at mount as well as on update. Immutable record so the dev tools overlay can display an arbitrary subset without locking the producer.

```csharp
public sealed record KeyedListDiagnostic(DateTime TimestampUtc, string? ControlContext, KeyedListDiagnosticKind Kind, IReadOnlyList<string> SampleKeys, int Count)
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.Diagnostics`.

### Constructors [#constructors_3]

#### `KeyedListDiagnostic` [#keyedlistdiagnostic_1]

A list with duplicate keys is rebuilt in full when it changes (a bailout); a null-keyed item is matched by position and the list keeps diffing incrementally. Reported at mount as well as on update. Immutable record so the dev tools overlay can display an arbitrary subset without locking the producer.


**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TimestampUtc` | `DateTime` | When the diagnostic was first observed. |
| `ControlContext` | `string?` | Human-readable label — the host control's type name. May be `null` when the diff ran outside a control context (e.g. direct unit-test invocation of `KeyedListDiff.Apply`). |
| `Kind` | [`KeyedListDiagnosticKind`](#keyedlistdiagnostickind) | Which class of key problem was found (null key vs. duplicate keys). |

## `ReactorDiagnostics` [#reactordiagnostics]

Process-wide diagnostic collector for structural problems the reconciler can detect at runtime (today: keyed-list bailouts). Read-only surface for agents, tests, and the in-app dev overlay; the producer side is `internal`.

```csharp
public static class ReactorDiagnostics
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.Diagnostics`.

### Remarks [#remarks]

The collector deduplicates by (control instance, kind, hashed sample keys). The first occurrence is logged in full; subsequent occurrences of the same triple bump a counter rather than appending a fresh entry. This matches the spec 042 §9 Q1 resolution ("warn-and-bailout via a one-shot diagnostic") and avoids drowning the dev overlay during a run-away render loop.

The buffer is bounded to [`ReactorDiagnostics.MaxRecentEntries`](#maxrecententries); once full, the oldest entry is dropped. This is intentionally generous — keyed-list bailouts are a per-app rarity, not a per-frame event.

Reads are lock-free against a snapshot; writes take a short lock.

### Properties [#properties_4]

#### `IsSourcePublishingEnabled` [#issourcepublishingenabled]

True when Reactor is publishing [`ReactorDiagnostics.SourceProperty`](#sourceproperty) in this process: the `Reactor.DevtoolsSupport` build switch is on and the process was started with `REACTOR_DIAGNOSTICS=1`.

```csharp
public static bool IsSourcePublishingEnabled  // get
```

#### `RecentKeyedListWarnings` [#recentkeyedlistwarnings]

Recent keyed-list key diagnostics (see [`KeyedListDiagnostic`](#keyedlistdiagnostic)), newest first. Returns an independent snapshot — safe to enumerate while producers continue running. Empty when no key problem has ever been found (the common case).

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<KeyedListDiagnostic> RecentKeyedListWarnings  // get
```

#### `SourceProperty` [#sourceproperty]

Attached string property, registered as `"ReactorSource"`, that Reactor sets on every control it realizes while diagnostics publishing is on. Its value describes where the control came from — call site, owning component, element kind, key, declared name, and for component boundaries the component's hooks — in the v1 grammar:

```csharp
v=1|at=path:line[:col][|rel=<root|0>]|owner=Comp|element=Kind[|mounts=Comp][|root=Comp][|key=k][|name=n][|hooks=i:name@line;...]
```

with `%` escaped as `%25` and `|` as `%7C` in values. `at` is never an absolute developer path: it is relative to the project directory, or to the solution/repo root (`rel=root`), or just the file name (`rel=0`) — the same posture as XAML's runtime source info, which reports `ms-appx:///` paths.

**Why a string on the control.** An out-of-process inspector reads it through XamlDiagnostics like any other property (it is reported as `.ReactorSource`), with no managed code in the app — so it works for Native AOT apps, where no managed inspector agent can be loaded.

**When it is set.** Only when the app was built with the `Reactor.DevtoolsSupport` switch on AND launched with `REACTOR_DIAGNOSTICS=1`; see [`ReactorDiagnostics.IsSourcePublishingEnabled`](#issourcepublishingenabled). Otherwise no control carries it and the publishing code is trimmed from AOT/trimmed builds. Reading this property registers the attached property (once) but publishes nothing.

```csharp
public static DependencyProperty SourceProperty  // get
```

### Methods [#methods]

#### `ClearRecentKeyedListWarnings` [#clearrecentkeyedlistwarnings]

```csharp
public static void ClearRecentKeyedListWarnings()
```

#### `DescribeComponent` [#describecomponent]

Describes the component hosted at `element`: a component's wrapper `Border` (every class, function and memo component is mounted into one), or a host's root content (its rendered root control, the window content or `ContentTarget` it was installed into, or a `ReactorHostControl` itself). Returns `null` for any other element. Works with or without source mapping.

```csharp
public static ComponentSnapshot? DescribeComponent(UIElement element)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `element` | `UIElement` |  |

**Remarks**

Must be called on the UI thread.

One element can anchor two components: when a root renders a component directly (`Render() => Component<Shell>()`), the root's rendered control *is* `Shell`'s wrapper. The wrapper wins — the element describes `Shell`, the innermost component it hosts — and [`ReactorDiagnostics.TrySetState`](#trysetstate) / [`ReactorDiagnostics.Rerender`](#rerender) address the same component. The root stays reachable through its other anchors: a `ContentTarget`, a `ReactorHostControl`, or the dev-overlay wrapper. A host that installs straight into `Window.Content` has none of those, so in that one shape its root is not reachable.

#### `GetAppliedProperties` [#getappliedproperties]

The WinUI properties Reactor writes on `control` from the common modifiers of the element that produced it, so an inspector can mark a property as set in C# (and overwritten when the element's value changes). Empty when the control is not tagged with its element — Reactor tags only controls something reads back (callbacks, a key, or a stamped source location), so turn on [`ReactorSourceMap.Enabled`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/diagnostics/ReactorSourceMap#enabled) for full coverage.

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<AppliedProperty> GetAppliedProperties(UIElement control)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `control` | `UIElement` |  |

**Remarks**

Covers [`ElementModifiers`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/ElementModifiers) and [`AccessibilityModifiers`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/AccessibilityModifiers), plus the `AutomationProperties.Name` Reactor derives from a captioned control (`Button("Save")`, `CheckBox("Agree")`, …) when the author sets none. That one is reported as `"DefaultAutomationName"`, and only while the live name still equals it; a different live name was written by the app. Properties a control's own element record sets (`TextBlock("hi")` → `Text`) are not listed. Must be called on the UI thread.

#### `GetHosts` [#gethosts]

Snapshot of every live Reactor host in the process, in creation order: windows opened through `ReactorApp` (including ones not yet mounted), hosts created with `new ReactorHost(window)`, and [`ReactorHostControl`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHostControl) islands. Disposed hosts are excluded. Safe to call from any thread; see [`ReactorHostInfo`](#reactorhostinfo) for consistency rules.

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<ReactorHostInfo> GetHosts()
```

**Remarks**

Provisional diagnostics API for external inspectors. A [`ReactorHostControl`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHostControl) that was removed from the tree but never disposed stays listed until it is collected — Reactor cannot tell a transient reparent from a removal (issue #344); check its `XamlRoot` to skip detached islands.

#### `GetReferenceEdges` [#getreferenceedges]

The references `control` declares to other controls — including pending ones whose target has not mounted yet, for which the WinUI property itself (e.g. `XYFocusRight`, `AutomationProperties.LabeledBy`) still reads null. Grouped by property in a fixed order (control-descriptor references, then bindings, then the modifier references), then list position; both `LabeledBy` forms are adjacent, the `ElementRef` one first.

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<ReferenceEdgeSnapshot> GetReferenceEdges(UIElement control)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `control` | `UIElement` |  |

**Remarks**

`ElementRef` references (modifiers such as `.LabeledBy(ref)` or `.XYFocusRight(ref)`, control descriptors and bindings) are always reported. An AutomationId `.LabeledBy("id")` is reported while pending; once resolved it is reported only while the control is loaded and tagged with its element (turn source mapping on). Reads existing reconciler state on demand. Must be called on the UI thread.

Reads [`ReactorDiagnostics.SourceProperty`](#sourceproperty) from `element`; `null` when unset.

#### `Rerender` [#rerender]

Schedules a re-render of the component hosted at `element`, bypassing its memoization (the path a state setter takes).

```csharp
public static bool Rerender(UIElement element)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `element` | `UIElement` |  |

**Returns:** False when no component is hosted at `element` or it has never rendered.

**Remarks**

A re-render diffs the new element tree against the previous one, so it re-applies a property only when the element's value for it changed: it does **not** restore a property that was edited directly on the control while the element's value stayed the same. Must be called on the UI thread that renders the component.

#### `TrySetState` [#trysetstate]

Development-time state edit: parses `text` to the value type of hook `hookIndex` of the component hosted at `element`, writes it, and — when the value changed — schedules a re-render exactly as the hook's own setter would.

```csharp
public static bool TrySetState(UIElement element, int hookIndex, string text, out string? error)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `element` | `UIElement` | A component wrapper or host root, as for [`ReactorDiagnostics.DescribeComponent`](#describecomponent). |
| `hookIndex` | `int` | The hook's [`DiagnosticValue.Index`](#index). |
| `text` | `string` | Invariant-culture text: a number, a single character, `true`/`false`, an enum member name, a date, time span or GUID, or the string itself (unquoted). `null` sets a string or nullable to null. |
| `error` | `string?` | Why the edit was refused, when this returns false. |

**Returns:** True when the value was written (including when it was already equal).

**Remarks**

Only state, reducer and persisted hooks of a text-typed value can be set. Must be called on the UI thread that renders the component.

### Fields [#fields]

#### `MaxRecentEntries` [#maxrecententries]

Maximum number of distinct (control, kind, sample-set) entries retained. New entries beyond this drop the oldest.

```csharp
public const int MaxRecentEntries = 64
```

#### `MaxSampleKeys` [#maxsamplekeys]

Maximum number of representative keys captured per entry. Larger duplicate sets are truncated and an ellipsis is appended.

## `ReactorHostInfo` [#reactorhostinfo]

Point-in-time description of one live Reactor host: where it renders, what its root is, and where that root was mounted. Returned by [`ReactorDiagnostics.GetHosts`](#gethosts).

```csharp
public sealed class ReactorHostInfo
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.Diagnostics`.

### Remarks [#remarks_1]

Provisional diagnostics API for external inspectors (for example `winapp devtools`); shape may change while Reactor is in preview.

Deliberately exposes no reconciler internals: the root is described by name and call site, and reached on screen through [`ReactorHostInfo.RootControl`](#rootcontrol) — the same WinUI control an inspector already walks. Everything else is an existing public WinUI or Reactor hosting type.

A snapshot, not a live view: re-query after a render, window open, or close. The snapshot itself can be taken from any thread, and every value in it is read atomically (never half of one mount and half of another). A snapshot taken while the UI thread is remounting may still pair the outgoing root's name with the incoming root's site; take it on the UI thread when the values must agree with each other or with the visual tree you are about to walk. Touching the returned WinUI objects is subject to their usual UI-thread rules.

Holding a snapshot keeps its host, window and root control alive; the registry behind [`ReactorDiagnostics.GetHosts`](#gethosts) does not.

# Elements
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements

Every control in Reactor is described by an element record. Factory methods create them and modifiers return changed copies. The reconciler turns them into real WinUI controls.

**Learn more:** [Controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls), [Reconciliation](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/reconciliation)

## Areas [#areas]

| Area | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Layout](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/layout) | Panels, stacks, grids, scrolling and other containers. |
| [Text](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/text) | Text blocks, rich text and the typography factories. |
| [Buttons](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons) | Buttons, toggle buttons, split buttons and hyperlink buttons. |
| [Input](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/input) | Text boxes, check boxes, combo boxes, sliders, pickers and other input controls. |
| [Collections](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/collections) | Lists, grids, trees, flip views and virtualized collections. |
| [Navigation](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/navigation) | Navigation views, tabs, pivots, breadcrumbs and the title bar. |
| [Menus and commands](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/menus-and-commands) | Menus, menu bars, command bars and keyboard accelerators. |
| [Dialogs and flyouts](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/dialogs-and-flyouts) | Content dialogs, flyouts, popups and teaching tips. |
| [Media and icons](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/media) | Images, icons, animated visuals, media playback and person pictures. |
| [Shapes](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/shapes) | Rectangles, ellipses, lines, paths and brushes. |
| [Status and info](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/status-and-info) | Info bars, badges and progress indicators. |
| [Forms](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/forms) | Form fields, validation rules, validation visualizers and the property grid. |
| [Composition](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/composition) | Components, memoization, error boundaries, conditionals and other structural elements. |
| [Interop](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/interop) | Hosted XAML content, web views and maps. |

# Elements: Buttons
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons

Element records are immutable descriptions of a control. You usually create them with a factory method and change them with modifiers.

**Learn more:** [Controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls), [Commanding](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/commanding)

## `ButtonElement` [#buttonelement]

The element record that describes a WinUI [`Button`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.button) control.

```csharp
public record ButtonElement(string Label, Action? OnClick = null) : Element
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`. Inherits from [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element).

**Created by:** [`Button`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/factories/buttons#button)

**Modifiers:** [`AccentButton`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/buttons#accentbutton), [`Click`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/buttons#click), [`Command`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/buttons#command), [`DisabledFocusable`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/buttons#disabledfocusable), [`IsDisabledFocusable`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/buttons#isdisabledfocusable), [`Set`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/native-properties#set), [`SubtleButton`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/buttons#subtlebutton), [`TextLink`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/buttons#textlink)

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Command` | [`Command?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command) |  | The [`ButtonElement.Command`](#buttonelement) bound to this button via the `Button(Command)` factory, the `.Command()` modifier, or a direct `new ButtonElement(cmd.Label) { Command = cmd }` / `with { Command = cmd }` record-init (issue #153, made fully uniform in issue #637). Carries the command so the reconciler can compare it field-aware in [`Element.ShallowEquals`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) and apply its metadata + enabled state through a descriptor entry — no per-render [`ButtonElement.Setters`](#buttonelement) lambda. **Every** binding path is now equivalent: dispatch (Execute/ExecuteAsync) is invoked by the click trampoline when [`ButtonElement.OnClick`](#buttonelement) is null, [`Command.IsEnabled`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command#isenabled) is folded into the IsEnabled descriptor entry (see [`ButtonElement.EffectiveIsEnabled`](#buttonelement)), and the command counts as a callback source for [`ButtonElement.HasCallbacks`](#buttonelement). The `init` accessor is public: a bare record-init invokes the command on click exactly like the factory/modifier. |
| `ContentElement` | [`Element?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |  |
| `IsDisabledFocusable` | `bool` |  | When true, the button is visually dimmed and its `OnClick` handler is suppressed, but it stays keyboard-focusable and reachable via Tab. Use for submit buttons gated on validation so users can discover them and the disable state doesn't trap keyboard navigation through commit- on-blur inputs. Conceptually equivalent to Fluent UI React's `disabledFocusable` / ARIA's `aria-disabled`. UIA still reports the button as enabled — full assistive-tech "unavailable" reporting requires a custom `ButtonAutomationPeer` and is tracked as a follow-up. |
| `IsEnabled` | `bool` |  |  |
| `Label` | `string` |  |  |
| `OnClick` | `Action?` | `null` |  |

## `ItemsRepeaterElementBase` [#itemsrepeaterelementbase]

Spec 047 §14 Phase 3 finish — Port (7). Non-generic intermediate base for [`ItemsRepeaterElement<T>`](#itemsrepeaterelementt). Same role as [`LazyStackElementBase`](#lazystackelementbase): lets the reconciler match on a single type AND lets the descriptor's [`Reconciler.RegisterHandlerForDerivedTypes`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler#registerhandlerforderivedtypes) registration catch every closed-T variant. Implements `IKeyedItemSource` + `IItemsRepeaterFactorySource` for the Engine (1) ItemsRepeater arm in [`Reconciler.BindErasedKeyedItemsSource`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler).

**Distinct from [`LazyStackElementBase`](#lazystackelementbase):** no hard-coded [`StackLayout`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.stacklayout). The element exposes a nullable [`ItemsRepeaterElementBase.Layout`](#itemsrepeaterelementbase) property — the descriptor / legacy mount arm assigns it directly when non-null, otherwise leaves the ItemsRepeater on its default (Stack vertical). No [`ScrollViewer`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.scrollviewer) wrapping either — the rendered [`UIElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.uielement) is the bare [`ItemsRepeater`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.itemsrepeater). Authors who need scrolling host the element inside their own `ScrollViewer` / `ScrollView` / `RefreshContainer`.

```csharp
public abstract record ItemsRepeaterElementBase : Element, IKeyedItemSource, IItemViewSource
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`. Inherits from [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element).

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ItemCount` | `int` | Total number of items in the source list. |
| `Layout` | `Layout?` | Optional WinUI [`Layout`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.layout). Null = leave the ItemsRepeater on its default layout (which itself defaults to vertical [`StackLayout`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.stacklayout)). Authors typically pass a `UniformGridLayout` or `LinedFlowLayout` instance configured up-front; the engine reuses it across renders by reference identity (no per-update Layout allocation). |

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `BuildItemView(int)` | Per-index Element factory — same shape as [`LazyStackElementBase.BuildItemView`](#lazystackelementbase). |
| `CreateFactory(Reconciler, Action, ElementPool?)` |  |
| `RefreshRealizedItems(IElementFactory, ItemsRepeater)` |  |
| `TryUpdateFactory(IElementFactory)` |  |

## `TemplatedTreeViewElementBase` [#templatedtreeviewelementbase]

Abstract non-generic base for the typed, data-driven `TreeView`. Non-generic so the reconciler can match a single type in its switch expression (same type-erasure pattern as [`TemplatedListElementBase`](#templatedlistelementbase)).

This is the hierarchical peer of [`TemplatedListViewElement<T>`](#templatedlistviewelementt): the developer supplies their own data items, a key selector, a children selector (the hierarchy), and a `viewBuilder` (`data → Element`, the WinUI `ItemTemplate` equivalent). It exists because WinUI's node-mode `TreeView` stringifies `TreeViewNode.Content` and cannot host a pre-built `UIElement` — rich per-node visuals must come from a template, never an element instance (the root cause of issue #447).

The base exposes object-erased accessors; the generic leaf casts back to `T`. Reference-type `T` flows through the covariant [`IReadOnlyList`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.ireadonlylist-1) → `IReadOnlyList<object>` conversion; value-type `T` is boxed once via the leaf's projection helper.

```csharp
public abstract record TemplatedTreeViewElementBase : Element
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`. Inherits from [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element).

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ApplyControlSetters(object)` |  |
| `BuildView(object)` | Builds the per-node view (the `ItemTemplate` equivalent). |
| `GetAllowDrop()` |  |
| `GetCanDragItems()` |  |
| `GetCanReorderItems()` |  |
| `GetChildren(object)` | The children of `item`, or null for a leaf. |
| `GetIsExpanded(object)` | Whether `item`'s node should start expanded. |
| `GetKey(object)` | The stable identity string for `item` (the keyed-diff key). |
| `GetRoots()` | The root data items (object-erased), in document order. |
| `GetSelectionMode()` |  |
| `InvokeExpanding(object)` | Dispatches `OnExpanding` with the developer's own `T`. |
| `InvokeItemInvoked(object)` | Dispatches `OnItemInvoked` with the developer's own `T`. |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `GetItemKey` | `Func<int, string>?` | Optional key function for stable identity across re-renders. When provided, the reconciler uses this to match items across reorderings. When omitted, identity is positional: an unchanged item count preserves row identities without projecting all keys again. Realized content still refreshes. |
| `ItemCount` | `int` | Total number of items (drives the virtualizer's extent). |
| `ItemHeight` | `double?` | Fixed item height in pixels. When set, enables the fixed-height fast path with O(1) offset calculation — no per-item measurement needed. When null, variable-height mode is used with EstimatedItemHeight. |
| `OnVisibleRangeChanged` | `Action<int, int>?` | Callback fired when the visible range changes (viewport tracking). Receives the first and last visible item indices. Native view changes use the current callback, item height (or estimate), and spacing. Setting this to null stops notifications without remounting. |
| `Ref` | `Action<VirtualListRef>?` | Callback ref for scroll operations. When set, receives a VirtualListRef that exposes ScrollToIndex and scroll position save/restore. |
| `RenderItem` | `Func<int, Element>` | Render callback: given an index, return the Element for that row. Called only for visible items (virtualized). |
| `Spacing` | `double` | Spacing between items in pixels (default 0). |

## `ComponentElement<TProps>` [#componentelementtprops]

Strongly-typed [`ComponentElement`](#componentelement) that exposes [`ComponentElement.Props`](#componentelementtprops) as `TProps` instead of `object?`, so callers can use a record `with`-expression to produce a modified copy of the element with updated props:

```csharp
var grid = DataGrid<Foo>(source, columns);
var taller = grid with { Props = grid.Props with { RowHeight = 60 } };
```

The typed [`ComponentElement.Props`](#componentelementtprops) is a thin view over the base [`ComponentElement.Props`](#componentelement) slot — there is no second storage field, so the reconciler (which reads `base.Props`) always sees the same value as the typed accessor on the cloned record.

```csharp
public record ComponentElement<TProps> : ComponentElement
```

## `KeyedMemoElement` [#keyedmemoelement]

Issue #327 — an opt-in, typed keyed memo wrapper produced by the `Memo(key, factory)` factory (see [`Factories`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/factories)). The author asserts [`KeyedMemoElement.Factory`](#keyedmemoelement) is a **pure function of [`KeyedMemoElement.MemoKey`](#keyedmemoelement)**: when a virtualized [`ElementFactory<T>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/ElementFactory) recycles a container and asks for the same key again, the factory-scoped LRU returns the previously-built inner [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) instance unchanged instead of rebuilding+diffing the subtree. Returning the *same* instance lets `Element.ShallowEquals` hit its `ReferenceEquals` fast-path so the per-row reconcile descent is skipped entirely.

**Purity contract.** The key must capture *every* input the factory reads. Closing over unkeyed mutable state (a `UseState` cell, an external counter, the theme) without folding it into the key will serve stale content — that is the author's responsibility. Widen the key to a tuple (e.g. `Memo((item.Id, isSelected), …)`) to capture extra inputs. [`KeyedMemoElement.MemoKey`](#keyedmemoelement) is compared with [`Object.Equals`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.object.equals) / [`Object.GetHashCode`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.object.gethashcode), so value keys (ints, strings, records, value tuples) dedupe by value — this is what makes the int-index VirtualList path hit the cache where the reference-identity `_viewBuilderCache` cannot.

**Used outside a virtualized factory** (e.g. a plain `VStack` child), the reconciler treats it as a *transparent, keyed* wrapper: a re-render with the same [`KeyedMemoElement.MemoKey`](#keyedmemoelement) is a no-op (by the purity contract the factory output is identical to the mounted inner, so there is nothing to diff), and a CHANGED key replaces the inner (unmount + fresh mount of the new [`KeyedMemoElement.Factory`](#keyedmemoelement) output). The old factory is never re-invoked at update time, so it is always safe to drop a `Memo(key, …)` anywhere a normal element is expected. The one exception to the no-op: when a component inside the mounted subtree updates its own state, the reconciler runs the current [`KeyedMemoElement.Factory`](#keyedmemoelement) again and walks that output against itself to reach the component, so the update renders. The cross-recycle cache benefit only applies on the [`ElementFactory<T>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/ElementFactory) recycle path.

The positional parameter is named `MemoKey` (not `Key`) so it does not clash with the inherited [`Element.Key`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element#key) string used for keyed reconciliation.

```csharp
public sealed record KeyedMemoElement(object MemoKey, Func<Element> Factory) : Element
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`. Inherits from [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element).

**Created by:** [`Memo`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/factories/composition#memo)

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Factory` | `Func<Element>` |  |
| `MemoKey` | `object` |  |

## `ContentDialogElement` [#contentdialogelement]

Declarative content dialog. Set IsOpen to true to show, false to close; content is reconciled live while the dialog is open. OnClosed reports how the dialog was dismissed — the button the user chose, or [`ContentDialogResult.None`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.contentdialogresult.none) for a declared IsOpen = false. It does not fire when the dialog is torn down because its owner unmounted or its host/reconciler was disposed. Disposal also cancels deferred opens without OnOpened. Defaults to `false` — drive it from state.  **Edge-triggered.** This declares a *transition*, not a mirror: after the initial render Reactor writes the control only when the declared value *changes*. A light dismiss or the tip's own close button sets `IsOpen` to `false` on the control without touching the declared value, so re-rendering the same declared `true` will not re-open it. Wire [`TeachingTipElement.OnClosed`](#teachingtipelement) back into the state that drives this property; a later `false → true` transition then re-opens the tip.  **Mount is the one exception** (issue #949): a first render that declares `true` does open the tip. WinUI drops a pending open if the tip is written again while it is still unparented, and Reactor configures controls before parenting them, so the mount-time open is deferred until the control is loaded. One consequence worth knowing: because that write lands after the setter pass, a `.Set(t => t.IsOpen = false)` cannot override a declared mount-time `true` the way setters normally win. Declare the value instead of reaching for `.Set` — this property is the supported channel for it. |

### `CallSite` [#callsite]

Spec 010 — the C# source location that created this element, or `null` when nothing stamped it.

This is a property of the ELEMENT, not of the current flag state. An element stamped while mapping was on keeps its location after the flag is turned off, and a hand-assigned value is honoured regardless of the flag; conversely an element built while mapping was off, or produced by a factory the provider does not reach, stays `null` forever. Elements are immutable, so this is fixed at construction.

NOTE ON THE NAME: spec 010 proposes `Element.Source`. That name is unusable — five existing element records already declare a positional `Source` member of an incompatible type (`ImageElement(string Source)`, `WebView2Element(Uri? Source)`, `MediaPlayerElementElement(string? Source)`, plus `AnimatedIconElement` and `ParallaxViewElement`), and a base property of a different type makes their positional parameters fail to bind (CS8866). `CallSite` is the collision-free equivalent.

The slot is present in every build configuration (the library ships as a Release-built NuGet package, so a `#if DEBUG` gate would make the property invisible to consumers). The *cost* is what is gated: nothing writes this slot unless a source-map provider is wired into the consuming compilation, and the generated interceptors check [`ReactorSourceMap.Enabled`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/diagnostics/ReactorSourceMap#enabled) before stamping.

Tagging is NOT keyed on that runtime flag. A stamped element carries this value in its [`Element.Extensions`](#extensions) bucket, and `Reconciler.NeedsTag` already tags anything with a non-null bucket — so the back-pointer follows the stamp, not the flag. A hand-assigned `CallSite` is therefore tagged and readable even with the flag off (see the `HandStampedLeafIsTaggedWithFlagOff` selftest), and an element the provider never reached stays untagged and reports no location rather than a wrong one.

Populated per call site, so it is a compile-time constant for a given DSL invocation and survives fluent modifier chains automatically (record `with` copies it). It is deliberately NOT consulted by [`Element.ShallowEquals`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) — see the reconciler's allow-list.

STORAGE: this is a shim over the spec 047 §4.4 [`Element.Extensions`](#extensions) bucket, exactly like [`Element.Attached`](#attached) and [`Element.ThemeBindings`](#themebindings). Declaring it inline on the record instead costs +24 bytes on every element ever allocated, measured, in every build — a permanent retail tax for a debug-only feature. The public shape is identical either way, so this is a storage decision, not an API one.

```csharp
public SourceLocation? CallSite  // get, init
```

### `ConnectedAnimationKey` [#connectedanimationkey]

Connected animation key for cross-container transitions. When set, the reconciler automatically captures a visual snapshot on unmount (via ConnectedAnimationService.PrepareToAnimate) and starts the animation on mount if a prepared animation with the same key exists. Set via fluent extension method: Border(child).ConnectedAnimation("hero")

```csharp
public string? ConnectedAnimationKey  // get, init
```

### `ContextValues` [#contextvalues]

Context values provided to this element's subtree via .Provide(). The reconciler pushes these onto the context scope when entering this element's subtree and pops them when leaving.

```csharp
public IReadOnlyDictionary<ContextBase, object?>? ContextValues  // get, init
```

### `ElementTransition` [#elementtransition]

Element enter/exit transition configuration (.Transition() modifier). When set, the reconciler animates mount (enter) and unmount (exit) with compositor animations, deferring removal until exit animation completes.

```csharp
public ElementTransition? ElementTransition  // get, init
```

### `Extensions` [#extensions]

Cross-cutting extras (attached properties, transitions, theme bindings, animation configs, resource overrides, context values) bucketed into a lazy sub-record (spec 047 §4.4). The common case — a leaf with none of these — leaves this slot null, so the 14 fields below cost one reference instead of 14 inline slots on every [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element). The setter is `internal` (PR #455 CR item #6): ordinary code uses the field shim properties (Attached, ThemeBindings, AnimationConfig, …) below and never observes this slot. Keeping the setter off the public surface removes an initializer-ordering footgun — a public `with { Extensions = X }` after a shim write would have silently discarded the shim. The engine and perf-critical internal paths may still set it directly.

```csharp
public ElementExtras? Extensions  // get
```

**Remarks**

Spec 047 §4.4.

# Elements: Interop
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/interop

Element records are immutable descriptions of a control. You usually create them with a factory method and change them with modifiers.

**Learn more:** [Coming from XAML](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/get-started/xaml-developers)

## `XamlHostElement` [#xamlhostelement]

An element that embeds an arbitrary FrameworkElement (UserControl, custom control, etc.) into the Reactor tree. The factory creates the control; the updater patches it.

```csharp
public record XamlHostElement(Func<FrameworkElement> Factory, Action<FrameworkElement>? Updater = null) : Element
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting`. Inherits from [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element).

**Created by:** [`XamlHost`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/factories/interop#xamlhost)

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Factory` | `Func<FrameworkElement>` |  |  |
| `TypeKey` | `string?` |  | Optional discriminator for the reconciler's CanUpdate check. When set, two XamlHostElements can only update in place if their TypeKeys match. Use this to prevent unrelated host elements from being reconciled against each other. |
| `Updater` | `Action<FrameworkElement>?` | `null` |  |

**Remarks**

Spec 058 §15 (P5.28) — migrated to a generated monomorphic decorator (`[WrapDecorator]`), replacing the hand-written `XamlHostDescriptor`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` |  | Opens the flyout declaratively. Like [`FlyoutElement.IsOpen`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/dialogs-and-flyouts#flyoutelement) this is a one-shot trigger: the flyout is shown on mount when already `true`, and on the `false` → `true` edge of an update. Setting it back to `false` does not close the flyout — the user dismisses it (outside click, Esc, or invoking a command). The target normally opens the flyout on click without this. |
| `Placement` | `FlyoutPlacementMode` |  | Preferred position of the flyout relative to its target. Defaults to [`FlyoutPlacementMode.Auto`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.primitives.flyoutplacementmode.auto), which means "no opinion — let WinUI decide": Reactor clears `FlyoutBase.Placement` so it falls back to the control's own default ([`FlyoutPlacementMode.Top`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.primitives.flyoutplacementmode.top)) instead of writing `Auto`, because WinUI's show-time validator rejects `Auto` and terminates the process. Changing an already-mounted flyout from an explicit placement back to [`FlyoutPlacementMode.Auto`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.primitives.flyoutplacementmode.auto) therefore returns it to that default, rather than leaving a stale local value that would outrank a `Style` setter. |

| `SecondaryCommands` | [`AppBarItemBase[]?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/controls/menu-items#appbaritembase) | `null` |  |
| `Target` | [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |  |

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `SettingsTag` | Well-known [`NavigationViewElement.SelectedTag`](#navigationviewelement) value that selects NavigationView's built-in settings item — the only menu entry NavigationView creates itself, so it has no [`NavigationViewItemData`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/controls/navigation-items#navigationviewitemdata) and cannot be addressed by an author-chosen tag. Also the tag reported to [`NavigationViewElement.OnItemInvoked`](#navigationviewelement) when settings is invoked. An author item carrying this tag still wins: selection searches [`NavigationViewElement.MenuItems`](#navigationviewelement) and [`NavigationViewElement.FooterMenuItems`](#navigationviewelement) before falling back to the settings item, so the sentinel can never shadow real content.  Reserved, so do not use it as an ordinary item tag. Selection would work, but `WithNavigation` skips it when mapping a tag back to a route — it routes the sentinel through its own `settingsRoute` parameter instead — so such an item would select without navigating. |

# Children strategies

## `AttachedPropWriter<TChildElement>` [#attachedpropwritertchildelement]

Spec 047 §6 / §14 Phase 1 (1.8) — writer for an attached DP from a parent container onto a child control (Grid.Row, Canvas.Left, DockPanel.Dock, etc.). Authors of container handlers register these on the child element type; the engine invokes them during child mount.

**Type-safety contract:** [`AttachedPropWriter.Get`](#get) pulls the value off the typed child element; [`AttachedPropWriter.Write`](#write) applies it to the [`UIElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.uielement) control. Both lambdas are strongly typed — no reflection, AOT-compatible.

```csharp
public sealed record AttachedPropWriter<TChildElement>(string Name, Func<TChildElement, object?> Get, Action<UIElement, object?> Write) where TChildElement : Element
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol`.

#### `Unmount` [#unmount]

Optional teardown for the children [`Imperative.Reconcile`](#reconcile) mounted. The engine has no view onto imperative slots, so when unmount dispatches to the handler it calls this instead of walking them. Unmount each owned child while it is still parented, then detach it. Declaring it does not tag every control: a control without an element tag is torn down by the engine's generic child walk, which must therefore be able to reach the owned children. That walk also tears down what the handler does not own, so tag the control ([`Reconciler.SetElementTag`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler#setelementtag)) when a slot can hold such UI.

```csharp
public Action<UnmountContext, TControl>? Unmount  // get, init
```

## `ItemsHost<TElement, TControl>` [#itemshosttelement-tcontrol]

Flat items host for native ItemCollection sinks and third-party controls that forward an IList\<object\> to an ItemsRepeater. Element children are reconciled in place: keys match across insertions and moves; unkeyed children retain positional identity. Raw items are compared with ItemEquals (object.Equals by default).

The live collection is incrementally inserted, removed and reordered, never reset on update. ObservableCollection moves emit one Move notification. Property-only and descendant-state updates do not mutate the collection.

SetCollection opts interface-typed, writable Items properties into a stable observable backing collection when their initial list has no change notifications. Native read-only ItemCollection properties keep their sink. Removed and terminally unmounted Element children receive real teardown.

```csharp
public sealed record ItemsHost<TElement, TControl>(Func<TElement, IReadOnlyList<object>> GetItems, Func<TControl, IList<object>> GetCollection) : ChildrenStrategy<TElement, TControl> where TElement : Element where TControl : UIElement
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol`. Inherits from [`ChildrenStrategy<TElement, TControl>`](#childrenstrategytelement-tcontrol).

#### `ItemEquals` [#itemequals]

Optional equality predicate for raw (non-Element) items. A positionally equal list retains its existing raw instances, matching the legacy unchanged-list fast path. On a structural update, matched raw value-equal instances are retained; Id-equal objects with changed payloads are replaced. Element children follow panel skip rules: dirty paths, changed context, theme sensitivity, resource refresh and force-rendering decline the skip. Defaults to object.Equals.

## `Panel<TElement, TControl>` [#paneltelement-tcontrol]

Panel host (StackPanel, Grid, Canvas). Engine mounts each child and appends to the panel's [`UIElementCollection`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.uielementcollection).

**Phase 1 limitation:** the dispatch is append-only; structural diff against the previous render goes through the host's child collection wholesale. Spec-042 keyed-reconcile integration is a Phase 3 follow-up.

**§14 Phase 3-final addition:** [`Panel.PerChildAttached`](#perchildattached) — optional callback invoked after each child mount AND after each child Update. Receives the mounted [`UIElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.uielement) alongside the child element so the descriptor can write WinUI attached DPs (e.g. `Grid.SetRow`, `Canvas.SetLeft`) based on attached-prop hints carried on the child element. No-op by default.

**§14 Phase 3 close-out addition:** [`Panel.PerChildAttachedAfterAll`](#perchildattachedafterall) — optional two-pass callback invoked once after every child has been mounted (Mount path) or reconciled (Update path). Receives the full `(UIElement, Element)` pair list in collection order so the descriptor can apply attached DPs that reference OTHER children by name (e.g. `RelativePanel.SetRightOf(b, a)`). Distinct from [`Panel.PerChildAttached`](#perchildattached), which fires per-child mid-pass and cannot see siblings that haven't mounted yet. Most descriptors set only one of the two; `RelativePanel` is the canonical consumer of the after-all shape.

```csharp
public sealed record Panel<TElement, TControl>(Func<TElement, IReadOnlyList<Element>> GetChildren, Func<TControl, UIElementCollection> GetCollection) : ChildrenStrategy<TElement, TControl> where TElement : Element where TControl : UIElement
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol`. Inherits from [`ChildrenStrategy<TElement, TControl>`](#childrenstrategytelement-tcontrol).

### Constructors [#constructors_8]

#### `Panel` [#panel]

Panel host (StackPanel, Grid, Canvas). Engine mounts each child and appends to the panel's [`UIElementCollection`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.uielementcollection).

**Phase 1 limitation:** the dispatch is append-only; structural diff against the previous render goes through the host's child collection wholesale. Spec-042 keyed-reconcile integration is a Phase 3 follow-up.

**§14 Phase 3-final addition:** [`Panel.PerChildAttached`](#perchildattached) — optional callback invoked after each child mount AND after each child Update. Receives the mounted [`UIElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.uielement) alongside the child element so the descriptor can write WinUI attached DPs (e.g. `Grid.SetRow`, `Canvas.SetLeft`) based on attached-prop hints carried on the child element. No-op by default.

**§14 Phase 3 close-out addition:** [`Panel.PerChildAttachedAfterAll`](#perchildattachedafterall) — optional two-pass callback invoked once after every child has been mounted (Mount path) or reconciled (Update path). Receives the full `(UIElement, Element)` pair list in collection order so the descriptor can apply attached DPs that reference OTHER children by name (e.g. `RelativePanel.SetRightOf(b, a)`). Distinct from [`Panel.PerChildAttached`](#perchildattached), which fires per-child mid-pass and cannot see siblings that haven't mounted yet. Most descriptors set only one of the two; `RelativePanel` is the canonical consumer of the after-all shape.

```csharp
public Panel(Func<TElement, IReadOnlyList<Element>> GetChildren, Func<TControl, UIElementCollection> GetCollection)
```
