## `PreMountedItems<TElement, TControl>` [#premounteditemstelement-tcontrol]

§14 Phase 3 completion — pre-mounted, Element-aware positional items host for templated controls whose host has no `ContainerContentChanging` (i.e. [`FlipView`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.flipview) templated peer). Items come from the element's `IItemViewSource` implementation — `ItemCount` + `BuildItemView(int)` — and are pre-mounted up-front into the control's flat `IList<object>` sink (e.g. `FlipView.Items`). Closes the carry-forward from §14 Phase 3 finish where `TemplatedFlipViewElement<T>` stayed legacy because the FlipView host can't share the [`TemplatedItemsErased<TElement, TControl>`](#templateditemserasedtelement-tcontrol) realization pipeline used by ListView / GridView (those route through [`Reconciler.BindKeyedItemsSource`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler) which assumes `ContainerContentChanging`).

**Update semantics:** positional reconcile against the previous element. For each shared index, the engine helper [`Reconciler.ReconcileV1Child`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler) runs the standard CanUpdate-or-Mount-or-Unmount slot decision. Excess old slots are `UnmountChild`-ed and removed; surplus new slots are mounted and appended. Mirrors the legacy `UpdateTemplatedFlipView` arm 1:1.

**Invariants asserted in Debug:** the dispatched old element is the same closed type as the new (the engine's `CanUpdate` gate guarantees this for Update arms); `items.Count` tracks the previous source's `ItemCount`. Release builds full-rebuild when an invariant is violated rather than indexing into a stale collection.

```csharp
public sealed record PreMountedItems<TElement, TControl>(Func<TElement, IItemViewSource> GetSource, Func<TControl, IList<object>> GetCollection) : ChildrenStrategy<TElement, TControl> where TElement : Element where TControl : FrameworkElement
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol`. Inherits from [`ChildrenStrategy<TElement, TControl>`](#childrenstrategytelement-tcontrol).

## `SingleContent<TElement, TControl>` [#singlecontenttelement-tcontrol]

Single-content host (Border, ContentControl, Viewbox). The engine mounts `GetChild`'s result and assigns it via `SetChild`.

A null child on mount, or null on both sides of an update, leaves native content supplied through setters alone. Declare an Empty element to intentionally clear content without rendering a child.

**Structural reconcile:** set [`SingleContent.GetCurrentChild`](#getcurrentchild_1) so the engine can read the existing slot value during `Update` and route through `Reconciler.ReconcileV1Child` — that preserves descendant component state across parent re-renders. When left null, the engine remounts the child on every update (only safe for slots that are reset every render anyway). All built-in handlers set it.

## `TabItemsHost<TElement, TControl, TItem>` [#tabitemshosttelement-tcontrol-titem]

§14 Phase 3 finish — Ports (10) + (11). Heterogeneous items host for [`TabView`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.tabview) and [`Pivot`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.pivot). Each item declares a header + an Element content + (TabView-only) an optional IsClosable / icon hint; the strategy mounts the content, builds the per-control container (e.g. `WinUI.TabViewItem`), and adds it to the host's items sink.

**Update semantics:** in-place positional reconcile against the previous element. For each shared index the existing container is kept and its `Content` reconciled through [`Reconciler.ReconcileV1Child`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler) (CanUpdate-or-mount-or-unmount); the container's own metadata (header / icon / closable) is refreshed via the optional [`TabItemsHost.UpdateContainer`](#updatecontainer) callback. Excess containers are unmounted + removed; surplus new items are created + appended. Containers (and the mounted Content subtree underneath them) therefore survive renders that don't change the tab/pivot set — re-adding every `TabViewItem` / `PivotItem` would re-trigger the tab-strip entrance animation and steal focus from descendant controls. Mirrors the legacy `UpdateTabView` / `UpdatePivot` in-place arms.

**Not covered (still legacy-only):** keyed reorder, pinnable tab headers, and the docking drag pipeline. Index-keyed pairing assumes the item at index `i` in the old list corresponds to index `i` in the new list.

```csharp
public sealed record TabItemsHost<TElement, TControl, TItem>(Func<TElement, IReadOnlyList<TItem>> GetItems, Func<TControl, IList<object>> GetCollection, Func<TItem, Element> GetContent, Func<TItem, UIElement?, object> CreateContainer, Action<TItem, TItem, object>? UpdateContainer = null) : ChildrenStrategy<TElement, TControl> where TElement : Element where TControl : FrameworkElement
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol`. Inherits from [`ChildrenStrategy<TElement, TControl>`](#childrenstrategytelement-tcontrol).

## `TemplatedItems<TItem, TElement, TControl>` [#templateditemstitem-telement-tcontrol]

Keyed templated-items host for descriptor-driven typed lists (`ListView<T>`, `GridView<T>`, future `LazyVStack<T>` / `LazyHStack<T>` / `ItemsRepeater<T>`). The strategy declares only the data shape; the engine partial [`Reconciler.BindKeyedItemsSource`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler) owns the realization plumbing (spec-042 `ReactorListState` + `KeyedListDiff`, the shared `ContainerContentChanging` handler, the per-control `ItemsSource` binding).

**Lifecycle:** Mount runs once on first render; Update runs on every subsequent render with the same control instance. Both go through [`Reconciler.BindKeyedItemsSource`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler); the boolean `isMount` parameter selects between fresh-state construction (Mount) and keyed-diff application (Update).

**Key contract:** [`TemplatedItems.KeySelector`](#keyselector) must produce stable, non-null, non-duplicate strings across renders for any given user item. Null / duplicate keys trigger the same `DiffStats.Bailout` path the legacy element-based binder uses — correctness preserved, animation degraded for that diff.

**Per-item Element:** [`TemplatedItems.BuildItemView`](#builditemview) is called lazily by the realization machinery as containers materialize, so large lists never realize all items up front. The returned [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) is reconciled into the container's `ContentControl`.

```csharp
public sealed record TemplatedItems<TItem, TElement, TControl>(Func<TElement, IReadOnlyList<TItem>> GetItems, Func<TItem, int, string> KeySelector, Func<TItem, int, Element> BuildItemView) : ChildrenStrategy<TElement, TControl> where TElement : Element where TControl : FrameworkElement
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol`. Inherits from [`ChildrenStrategy<TElement, TControl>`](#childrenstrategytelement-tcontrol).

# ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl>
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ControlDescriptor

A descriptor is the data-driven alternative to a hand-coded [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler). Authors declare property bindings (`OneWay`, [`ControlDescriptor.InitialOnly`](#initialonly), [`ControlDescriptor.Controlled`](#controlled)), an optional children strategy, and an optional factory; the interpreter ([`DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/DescriptorHandler)) executes them against the same v1 protocol surface a hand-coded handler would use.

**Phase 2 measurement gate (§13 Q1):** the descriptor and the hand-coded handler shapes are evaluated head-to-head on the same M1 / M2 / M5 / M7 / M10 micro-benches and the L4 / L9 macros, then the §13 Q1 decision matrix determines which surface ships as the primary author path. See `docs/specs/047-extensible-control-model.md` §13 Q1.

**Echo suppression (issue #206).** A `.Controlled` / `.HandCodedControlled` entry suppresses the echo of its own programmatic write automatically — the interpreter wraps the write in the public [`ReactorBinding`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding) `WriteSuppressed` primitive (or arms a value-diff predicate when `valueDiffEcho` is set), so a framework-driven write never echoes back into the user's `OnChanged` callback. Descriptor authors therefore never touch the suppressor directly; hand-coded [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler) authors call `WriteSuppressed` themselves. See `docs/guide/extending-reactor-controls.md`.

**Fluent author pattern:**

```csharp
public record ToggleSwitchElement(Optional<bool> IsOn = default) : Element;

public static readonly ControlDescriptor<ToggleSwitchElement, ToggleSwitch> Descriptor =
    new ControlDescriptor<ToggleSwitchElement, ToggleSwitch>()
        .OneWay(e => e.OnContent, (c, v) => c.OnContent = v)
        .OneWayConditional(e => e.Header, (c, v) => c.Header = v, e => e.Header is not null)
        .Controlled<bool, RoutedEventArgs>(
            get:          e => e.IsOn,
            set:          (c, v) => c.IsOn = v,
            subscribe:    (fe, h) => ((ToggleSwitch)fe).Toggled += (s, e) => h(s, e),
            unsubscribe:  (fe, h) => { /* trampoline lives for control lifetime */ },
            callback:     e => e.OnIsOnChanged,
            readBack:     c => c.IsOn);
```

```csharp
public sealed class ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl> where TElement : Element where TControl : FrameworkElement, new()
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor`.

**Learn more:** [Extending Reactor with Native Controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/extending-reactor-controls), [The Control Reconciler Protocol](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/control-reconciler-protocol)

### `AfterChildrenMount` [#afterchildrenmount]

Spec 047 §14 Phase 3 prelude (Engine A1) — optional post-children mount hook. The interpreter ([`DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/DescriptorHandler)) surfaces it through [`IElementHandler.AfterChildrenMount`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler#afterchildrenmount), which the adapter invokes after every child has mounted. Use for events that must subscribe after children-add (TabView SelectionChanged), or for imperative work that must run strictly after the prop loop AND the event subscriptions (FrameElement's mount-time navigation, which would otherwise complete before its own Navigated/NavigationFailed handlers exist). Defaults to `null` (no hook). Set it from an object initializer, or — from a generated descriptor's `Customize` hook, which receives an already-constructed descriptor — via [`ControlDescriptor.WithAfterChildrenMount`](#withafterchildrenmount).

### `OnUnmount` [#onunmount]

Optional teardown hook. The interpreter ([`DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/DescriptorHandler)) surfaces it through [`IElementHandler.Unmount`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler#unmount), which the engine invokes when the control leaves the tree. Use it to invalidate control-scoped state the descriptor created during mount and that the pool reset contract cannot see — a pending deferred write, a one-shot `Loaded` subscription, a disposable. Defaults to `null` (no hook). Set it from an object initializer, or — from a generated descriptor's `Customize` hook, which receives an already-constructed descriptor — via [`ControlDescriptor.WithUnmount`](#withunmount).

Not for event trampolines: those anchor to the control's lifetime by design (see the `unsubscribe` no-op contract on [`ControlDescriptor.Controlled`](#controlled)).

Declaring this hook makes [`DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/DescriptorHandler) force the control's `ReactorState` into existence at mount, because the engine's unmount dispatch is tag-gated. That costs one small allocation per mounted control of this type, so declare it only when there is real teardown to do.

```csharp
public DescriptorUnmountCallback<TControl>? OnUnmount  // get, init
```

### `CoercingOneWay` [#coercingoneway]

Add a one-way property whose write may coerce a sibling controlled prop's value (e.g. `Slider.Minimum` coercing `Slider.Value`). When `coercesController` returns true the write is wrapped in `ReactorBinding.WriteSuppressed` so the coercion-driven change event is dropped.

Declarative replacement for the imperative `if (ctrl.Value < n.Min) WriteSuppressed(...)` pattern in the hand-coded `SliderHandler`. Encodes the §8 audit's "coercion-tolerance" treatment for the 8 audited coercion sites (NumberBox / Slider Min/Max etc.) as a single declarative entry.

### `Controlled` [#controlled]

Add a controlled (two-way) property binding. The engine writes from element state when `get` returns a value and leaves the control authoritative when it returns [`Optional.Unset`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/Optional#unset); writes use echo suppression on Update. The control raises `subscribe`'s event on user interaction; the trampoline invokes the element's `callback` with `readBack`'s value.

**Callback gating:** if `callback` returns `null` on the element passed at Mount, no subscription happens at all — mirrors the hand-coded `Ensure*Wiring` gate.

### `HandCodedControlled` [#handcodedcontrolled]

§14 Phase 3 (3.0.1) — escape-hatch builder for controlled (two-way) props on a control that needs a hand-authored trampoline against a user-supplied per-control event payload (`TPayload`). Required for multi-event controls (e.g. `TextBox.Text` alongside `SelectionChanged`) where the single-event fast-path `DescriptorControlledPayload` would collide if two controlled entries shared the same closed generic.

The payload type is typically reused from `ControlEventPayloads.cs` (e.g. `TextBoxEventPayload`) which already has a slot per event. `slotIsNull` + `setSlot` address the specific slot on the payload this entry owns; `subscribe` wires the user-supplied native `TDelegate` directly to the control's event (no `EventHandler<TArgs>` bridge closure).

Mount/Update prop-write semantics are identical to [`ControlDescriptor.Controlled`](#controlled): unset skips writes, set values perform a bare initial write and a suppressed write on control drift. Subscription is gated on `callback` returning non-null on the mounted element.

`valueDiffEcho` replaces the Update write's suppress-counter token with the spec 047 §8 value-diff arm, which the trampoline consumes on the next change event and which drops that event only when its readback matches the written value. `armOnMount` (requires `valueDiffEcho`) arms the Mount write too. Set it when the control raises its change event after the write returns (e.g. `RichEditBox`'s `Document.SetText`) and the trampoline cannot tell that echo apart on its own: the echo lands after the trampoline is wired and would otherwise reach the callback. The `set` lambda stays a plain write; the entry does the arming.

```csharp
public ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl> HandCodedControlled<TPayload, TValue, TDelegate>(Func<TElement, Optional<TValue>> get, Action<TControl, TValue> set, Func<TControl, TValue> readBack, Action<TControl, TDelegate> subscribe, Func<TElement, Action<TValue>?> callback, TDelegate trampoline, Func<TPayload, bool> slotIsNull, Action<TPayload, TDelegate> setSlot, IEqualityComparer<TValue>? comparer = null, bool valueDiffEcho = false, bool armOnMount = false) where TPayload : class, new() where TDelegate : Delegate
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `get` | `Func<TElement, Optional<TValue>>` |  |  |
| `set` | `Action<TControl, TValue>` |  |  |
| `readBack` | `Func<TControl, TValue>` |  |  |
| `subscribe` | `Action<TControl, TDelegate>` |  |  |
| `callback` | `Func<TElement, Action<TValue>?>` |  |  |
| `trampoline` | `TDelegate` |  |  |
| `slotIsNull` | `Func<TPayload, bool>` |  |  |
| `setSlot` | `Action<TPayload, TDelegate>` |  |  |
| `comparer` | `IEqualityComparer<TValue>?` | `null` |  |
| `valueDiffEcho` | `bool` | `false` |  |
| `armOnMount` | `bool` | `false` |  |

### `Imperative` [#imperative]

§14 Phase 3 finish — Engine (4). Escape hatch entry that receives `mount`+(`update` with BOTH old and new TElement, so the entry can express a diff the per-value get/set lambdas of [`ControlDescriptor.OneWayConditional`](#onewayconditional) can't: comparing one element field while writing a derived value elsewhere, or multi-source error context like `Path.PathDataString`'s path-markup converter/pre-built Geometry branches.

**When to reach for it:** only when the standard entries can't express the diff or the write. Imperative entries skip the engine's value-comparer fast-path, so a misused Imperative entry re-runs on every render. The other entry shapes (`OneWay`, [`ControlDescriptor.OneWayConditional`](#onewayconditional), [`ControlDescriptor.CoercingOneWay`](#coercingoneway), [`ControlDescriptor.HandCodedControlled`](#handcodedcontrolled)) still cover the 95% case.

**Distinct from** [`Imperative<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/children-strategies#imperativetelement-tcontrol) (a [`ChildrenStrategy<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/children-strategies#childrenstrategytelement-tcontrol) that drives the whole CHILD subtree imperatively) — this is a property-level escape hatch that participates in the normal prop loop.

```csharp
public ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl> Imperative(Action<TControl, TElement> mount, Action<TControl, TElement, TElement> update)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mount` | `Action<TControl, TElement>` |  |
| `update` | `Action<TControl, TElement, TElement>` |  |

#### `ImperativeBridged(Action<MountContext, TControl, TElement>, Action<UpdateContext, TControl, TElement, TElement>)` [#imperativebridgedactionmountcontext-tcontrol-telement-actionupdatecontext-tcontrol-telement-telement]

§14 Phase 3 finish — Engine (2). Bridged variant of [`ControlDescriptor.Imperative`](#imperative) — the lambdas receive the [`MountContext`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/lifecycle-contexts#mountcontext) / [`UpdateContext`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/lifecycle-contexts#updatecontext) so they can call engine-internal helpers for bindings without owned child lifetime.

# ControlRegistry
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ControlRegistry

Spec 048 §8 — the global, lazy, lock-free control registry that backs the factory-as-registration pattern. Holds [`Type`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.type) → factory-of- `IV1HandlerEntry` entries; never roots a handler or WinUI control type by itself. Every static reference to a handler/control type lives in the *callers* of [`ControlRegistry.Register`](#register) — per-control factory cctors (Pattern A) or `Reg<…>` static-field initializers (Pattern B), each on a per-control rooted path. The trimmer therefore keeps a control iff its factory is reachable from the app entry point.

**Idempotent first-wins.** Repeat [`ControlRegistry.Register`](#register) calls for the same element type are a silent no-op (spec §12.1). Multiple factories legitimately map to the same element type — e.g. `TextBlock()`, `Heading()`, and `Subheading()` all produce `TextBlockElement` (spec §10.3) — and a throw from a cctor would surface as a non-deterministic `TypeInitializationException` at the first-use point. The strict throw-on-duplicate policy from spec 047 §13 Q17 is preserved on the explicit per-host [`Reconciler.RegisterHandler`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler#registerhandler) path.

**Hot path.** Per spec §9, [`ControlRegistry.Register`](#register) runs at most once per element type per process, on the cold first-use path. The steady-state per-host dispatch lookup short-circuits in the per-host `_v1Handlers` cache populated on the first registry hit; the registry itself is consulted at most once per (host, element type) pair.

**AOT.** No reflection, no [`Type.MakeGenericType`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.type.makegenerictype); the closed-type capture happens inside the generic [`ControlRegistry.Register`](#register) entry point so the AOT compiler can see the closed types statically. The internal map is keyed by [`Type`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.type) and stores [`Func`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.func-1) delegates only — no MakeGenericType, no runtime type construction.

```csharp
public static class ControlRegistry
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol`.

**Learn more:** [Extending Reactor with Native Controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/extending-reactor-controls), [The Control Reconciler Protocol](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/control-reconciler-protocol)

## Methods [#methods]

### `Register` [#register]

Spec §8 — register a handler factory for `TElement`. Idempotent first-wins: if an entry already exists for `typeof(TElement)`, this call is a silent no-op. The handler factory is invoked at most once per (host, element type) — on the first dispatch hit — and the resulting adapter is cached into the host's `_v1Handlers` map so steady-state dispatch is the existing fast per-host lookup.

The `handlerFactory` delegate **should** be a `static` lambda (no captures) — Pattern A / Pattern B both rely on the single allocation being interned in a static field at the call site. A capturing lambda is functionally correct but allocates a closure on every `Reg<>.Init` / cctor run, undoing the cost-model claim in spec §9.

**Echo suppression for value-bearing controls (issue #206).** A custom [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler) registered here that writes a value-bearing property in `Update` must guard that write with the supported public primitive [`ReactorBinding<TElement>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding-1)'s `WriteSuppressed` method (or the static [`ReactorBinding`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding)) so the control's own echo does not flow back as a spurious user edit. Never reach into the internal `ChangeEchoSuppressor`. Descriptor authors get this through `.Controlled` / `.HandCodedControlled`. See `docs/guide/extending-reactor-controls.md`.

```csharp
public static void Register<TElement, TControl>(Func<IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>> handlerFactory) where TElement : Element where TControl : UIElement
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handlerFactory` | `Func<IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>>` | A factory that, when invoked, returns a fresh handler. Strongly recommended to be a `static` lambda (e.g. `static () => new MarqueeHandler()`) so the delegate is cached in a static field and no closure is allocated. |

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `TElement` | The element record type the handler dispatches against. Used as the dispatch key ([`Type`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.type)). |
| `TControl` | The WinUI control the handler mounts. |

### `RegisterDecorator` [#registerdecorator]

Spec 048 §3.4 — decorator sibling of [`ControlRegistry.Register`](#register) for handlers that implement [`IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IDecoratorElementHandler) (a separate, non-inheriting interface from [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler)). Decorator handlers cover target-wrapping flyouts, modal lifecycle wrappers, polymorphic mounts (IconElement), interop bridges (XamlHost/XamlPage), and the keyed-reconcile panels (Stack/Grid/ Canvas/RelativePanel/WrapGrid/Flex) + Button/CheckBox/Expander — see [`IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IDecoratorElementHandler) for the full use-case list.

Stores the same [`Func`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.func-1) shape as the value-handler path, so [`Reconciler.TryResolveFromControlRegistry`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler) (dispatch arm 3) consumes both uniformly — no dispatch changes required. The adapter wrapping is the only difference: `V1DecoratorHandlerAdapter` versus `V1HandlerAdapter`.

**One-shim invariant (§3.4 authoring rule).** For any given element type, factories must touch *exactly one* of `Reg<…>.Done` or `RegDecorator<…>.Done` — never both. The first-wins TryAdd silently keeps whichever path's cctor fires first; mixing them creates a non-deterministic dispatch outcome that depends on factory call order across the app's startup graph. This contrasts with the harmless aliasing case where multiple factories share the *same* closed-generic shim (spec §10.3 Heading/Subheading both touching `Reg<TextBlockElement, TextBlock, TextBlockHandler>`).

**Singleton-handler factories.** A decorator handler exposed as a `public static readonly` singleton whose underlying type is a private nested class cannot satisfy `RegDecorator`'s `new()` constraint. Such a factory registers directly via this method with a `static` lambda returning the singleton:

```csharp
public static MyElement My(...)
{
    ControlRegistry.RegisterDecorator<MyElement>(
        static () => MyDescriptor.Handler);
    return new MyElement(...);
}
```

This is functionally equivalent to `RegDecorator<…>.Done` — the static lambda still has no captures, the TryAdd still first-wins, and the trim story still routes every reference to the private handler type through the factory call-site path the trimmer can see. (The built-in Icon/XamlPage/XamlHost decorators that formerly used this pattern are now source-generated — spec 058 §15 P5.27/P5.28 — and self-register via a generated Pattern-A cctor.)

```csharp
public static void RegisterDecorator<TElement>(Func<IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement>> handlerFactory) where TElement : Element
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handlerFactory` | `Func<IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement>>` | A factory that, when invoked, returns a fresh decorator handler. Strongly recommended to be a `static` lambda (e.g. `static () => new ButtonHandler()`) so the delegate is cached in a static field and no closure is allocated. |

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `TElement` | The element record type the decorator handler dispatches against. Used as the dispatch key ([`Type`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.type)). |

### `RegisterForDerivedTypes` [#registerforderivedtypes]

Spec 048 §3.4 — base-derived sibling of [`ControlRegistry.Register`](#register). Registers a handler for `TBase` that also catches every concrete element type whose runtime [`Type`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.type) derives from `TBase`. Exact-type registrations (via [`ControlRegistry.Register`](#register) / [`ControlRegistry.RegisterDecorator`](#registerdecorator)) take precedence over a base-derived registration, matching the per-host `V1HandlerRegistry.TryGet` precedence.

Used for the four cases that registered through `Reconciler.RegisterDescriptorForDerivedTypes` on the per-host path: `TemplatedListElementBase`, `LazyStackElementBase`, `ItemsRepeaterElement`, and `ItemsViewElement` — each is a non-generic intermediate base whose closed-T variants (`TemplatedListViewElement<Person>`, etc.) should all share the same handler.

# DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/DescriptorHandler

Spec 047 §6 / §14 Phase 2 (Q1 spike) — interpreter that drives a [`ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ControlDescriptor) against the v1 protocol surface.

Implemented as a regular [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler) so the `V1HandlerAdapter` dispatch shell is identical between the descriptor and hand-coded handler paths — the only thing that differs between the Q1 A|B variants is the body of Mount / Update. Any measured delta is the interpreter's tax, not a different dispatch shape.

**Mount sequence** (matches the hand-coded handlers' KD-1b ordering):

1. Rent the control via [`MountContext.RentControl`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/lifecycle-contexts#rentcontrol).
2. Iterate [`ControlDescriptor.Properties`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ControlDescriptor#properties_1) and invoke [`PropEntry.Mount`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/PropEntry#mounttcontrol-telement) on each — all bare initial writes happen first.
3. Iterate again and invoke [`PropEntry.EnsureSubscribed`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/PropEntry#ensuresubscribed) — controlled entries wire their change-event trampolines now (no echo on the just- written values because nothing is listening yet).
4. Apply setters.

```csharp
public class DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl> : IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> where TElement : Element where TControl : FrameworkElement, new()
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor`.

**Learn more:** [Extending Reactor with Native Controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/extending-reactor-controls), [The Control Reconciler Protocol](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/control-reconciler-protocol)

## Remarks [#remarks]

Spec 048 §7 — **unsealed** so the built-in catalog can expose a thin, `new()`-constructible registration subclass per descriptor (e.g. `TextBlockDescriptorHandler(): DescriptorHandler<…>(TextBlockDescriptor.Descriptor)`). That subclass is what the `Reg` shim instantiates via its `static () => new THandler()` lambda, so the descriptor path registers through the exact same zero-closure mechanism as a hand-coded handler. The base interpreter has no virtual members the subclass overrides; unsealing carries no dispatch cost (calls already route through the [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler) interface via the adapter).

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

## Remarks [#remarks]

Each type has two lanes (spec 066 §7.2). The plain lane holds controls whose composition visual was never taken. The visual lane holds controls whose visual was taken, reset to a fresh control's pixels by [`ElementPool.ResetTakenVisual`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ElementPool). Such a control still refuses the facade transforms and the XAML implicit transitions, so only an element that takes the visual itself and has no setters rents from it.

# IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement>
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IDecoratorElementHandler

Spec 047 §14 Phase 3 completion — decorator-style V1 handler contract for elements whose returned [`UIElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.uielement) identity may change on update or whose unmount disposition diverges from the standard pool-return.

Use this contract instead of [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler) for:

- **Target-wrapping decorators** (Flyout, MenuFlyout, CommandBarFlyout) where the returned [`UIElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.uielement) IS the user's inner `Target` child — the control type isn't known until the element is inspected, and may change on update if the user swaps Target's element type.
- **Modal lifecycle wrappers** (ContentDialog, Popup) where the returned control is a placeholder and the actual modal surface is created lazily or as a sibling.
- **Polymorphic mounts** (IconElement) where the concrete control type depends on the element's runtime subtype.
- **Interop bridges** (XamlHost, XamlPage) where the returned control hosts arbitrary user-side XAML.

Distinct from [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler) to keep the §13 Q12 "no substitution" invariant on the standard author-facing surface — only built-in V1 ports use this decorator shape. External authors continue to use [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler).

```csharp
public interface IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement> where TElement : Element
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol`.

**Learn more:** [Extending Reactor with Native Controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/extending-reactor-controls), [The Control Reconciler Protocol](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/control-reconciler-protocol)

## Methods [#methods]

### `Unmount` [#unmount]

Unmount the element and return the engine's post-unmount disposition for the control. The `element` is read from the attached state DP at unmount time; it may be null if the tag was already detached (defensive — should not happen for well-behaved decorator handlers).

# IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler

Implementations register themselves via [`Reconciler.RegisterHandler`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler#registerhandler); dispatch is exact-type by `element.GetType()` (§13 Q17). Update returns `void` — substitution is forbidden (§13 Q12); a type change flows through the unmount-and-remount path on the wrapping container.

**Hot path:** dispatch is dictionary lookup + interface call (both already paid by `V1HandlerRegistry`). Implementations should avoid allocations in [`IElementHandler.Mount`](#mount) / [`IElementHandler.Update`](#update) bodies; the `ref struct` context types are allocation-free by construction.

**Echo suppression for value-bearing controls (issue #206).** If the control raises the same change event for a programmatic property write as it does for a user edit, a write from [`IElementHandler.Update`](#update) would echo back through the trampoline into the owning component's `OnChanged` state setter — indistinguishable from real input. Guard every programmatic controlled-value write with the supported, RCW-safe public primitive [`ReactorBinding<TElement>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding-1)'s `WriteSuppressed` method (or the static [`ReactorBinding`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding)): `ctx.BindFor(ctrl, newEl).WriteSuppressed(() => ctrl.Value = newEl.Value)`. Pair it 1:1 with the write and gate it on an equality check so the token is always consumed by the engine-provoked echo. Descriptor authors get this for free through `.Controlled` / `.HandCodedControlled`. Never reach into the internal `ChangeEchoSuppressor`. See `docs/guide/extending-reactor-controls.md`.

```csharp
public interface IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> where TElement : Element where TControl : UIElement
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol`.

**Learn more:** [Extending Reactor with Native Controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/extending-reactor-controls), [The Control Reconciler Protocol](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/control-reconciler-protocol)

# Handler contexts
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/lifecycle-contexts

**Learn more:** [Extending Reactor with Native Controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/extending-reactor-controls), [The Control Reconciler Protocol](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/control-reconciler-protocol)

## `MountContext` [#mountcontext]

Spec 047 §4 / §14 Phase 1 (1.6) — mount-time context passed to [`IElementHandler.Mount`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler#mount).

**UI-thread guarantee (Q14):** handlers run on the reconciler's UI dispatcher. Mount bodies may freely access control state without synchronization. Calls from other threads throw in Debug builds today; Phase 1 plan is to measure first before tightening to unconditional throw. See `docs/specs/047/phase1-results/q14-dispatcher-affinity.md`.

**Allocation contract:** [`MountContext`](#mountcontext) is a `readonly ref struct`, so it cannot escape the call stack and never allocates on its own. Hot path (Mount body) pays only the dictionary lookup + interface call already incurred by the V1HandlerRegistry dispatch.

**Sample skeleton** (per spec §4 ToggleSwitchHandler example):

```csharp
public sealed class ToggleSwitchHandler : IElementHandler<ToggleSwitchElement, ToggleSwitch>
{
    public ToggleSwitch Mount(MountContext ctx, ToggleSwitchElement el)
    {
        var ctrl = ctx.RentControl<ToggleSwitch>();
        ctrl.IsOn = el.IsOn;
        ctrl.OnContent = el.OnContent;
        var bind = ctx.BindFor(ctrl, el);
        bind.OnCustomEvent<RoutedEventArgs>(
            (c, h) => ((ToggleSwitch)c).Toggled += (s, e) => h(s, e),
            (c, h) => { /* trampoline lives for the control's lifetime */ },
            (e, args) => e.OnIsOnChanged?.Invoke(((ToggleSwitch)args.OriginalSource).IsOn));
        return ctrl;
    }
    public void Update(UpdateContext ctx, ToggleSwitchElement oldEl, ToggleSwitchElement newEl, ToggleSwitch ctrl)
    {
        if (oldEl.IsOn != newEl.IsOn)
            ctx.BindFor(ctrl, newEl).WriteSuppressed(() => ctrl.IsOn = newEl.IsOn);
    }
}
```

```csharp
public readonly struct MountContext
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol`.

> **Obsolete.** Types with embedded references are not supported in this version of your compiler.

## `V1UnmountDisposition` [#v1unmountdisposition]

Spec 047 §14 Phase 3 completion — controls the engine's pool-return / child-traversal decision after a V1 handler's `Unmount` body runs. Returned from `IV1HandlerEntry.Unmount`; the standard hand-coded + descriptor handlers always return [`V1UnmountDisposition.CollectSelf`](#values), matching the pre-Phase-3-completion behavior. Decorator-style handlers ([`IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IDecoratorElementHandler)) return the other dispositions to opt out of pool return / let the engine continue the default unmount traversal into the wrapped child.

```csharp
public enum V1UnmountDisposition
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol`.

### Values [#values]

| Name | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CollectSelf` | `0` | Default for standard handlers. The handler created the control via `RentControl`; the engine pools the control (if poolable) and stops the traversal — children were already torn down by the handler. |
| `ContinueDefaultTraversal` | `1` | The handler's returned control is owned by another element (e.g., a decorator's wrapped `Target` child element). The engine must NOT pool the control and MUST continue the default unmount traversal as if no V1 handler had claimed it, so the inner element's own teardown runs. |
| `SkipPool` | `2` | The handler manages teardown itself; the control is a placeholder/wrapper that should NOT be pooled and whose children were already torn down by the handler. Engine returns immediately without pool collection or traversal. |

# PoolPolicy<TControl>
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/PoolPolicy

External and built-in V1 handlers attach a `PoolPolicy<TControl>` to their `RentControl` / `ReturnControl` calls to opt out of pooling (e.g. for controls with persistent native resources like MediaPlayerElement, MapControl, SwapChainPanel) or to layer an author-defined reset action on top of the engine's default contract.

Pool key is `typeof(TControl)` only (Q18). Finer keys (e.g. by style hash) are a Phase 3+ addition.

Provisional surface — see [`ReactorBinding`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding) for the `REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW` diagnostic id.

## Properties [#properties]

### `IsPoolable` [#ispoolable]

When false, `RentControl` always allocates a fresh instance and `ReturnControl` is a no-op (the control is dropped on the floor for the GC to collect). Default true.

```csharp
public bool IsPoolable  // get, init
```

### `Reset` [#reset]

Optional extra reset action, invoked last when the control is returned to the pool, after the engine's default reset. That reset clears the element pointer, the current modifier callbacks, echo-suppression and unmount state, and the Reactor-set DataContext. It keeps the attached ReactorState and its per-control ControlEventState, so event trampolines subscribed once for the control's lifetime stay subscribed and dispatch to the next element. Don't resubscribe native events here. Use it for control-specific transient state the engine can't know about (e.g. ScrollViewer.ChangeView animation queue).

```csharp
public Action<TControl>? Reset  // get, init
```

# PropEntry<TElement, TControl>
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/PropEntry

Spec 047 §6 / §14 Phase 2 (Q1 spike) — base class for descriptor entries declared on a [`ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ControlDescriptor).

The interpreter (see [`DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/DescriptorHandler)) iterates the entry list during Mount and Update. The property's value type stays inside each concrete entry — the interpreter never sees it, so iterating a heterogeneous list of entries does not box value types (each generic specialization keeps its own monomorphic code path).

**Phase ordering inside Mount:**

1. [`PropEntry.Mount`](#mounttcontrol-telement) runs once per entry. Controlled entries write their initial value bare — event subscription has not yet been wired, so a synchronous change event has no trampoline to fire (no echo). Mirrors the KD-1b fix on the hand-coded handlers. A control whose change event is raised after the write returns echoes after the wiring below; its entry arms the Mount write instead (`HandCodedControlled`'s `armOnMount`).
2. [`PropEntry.EnsureSubscribed`](#ensuresubscribed) runs once per entry. Controlled entries subscribe to their change event here, guarded by [`DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/DescriptorHandler)'s per-control subscription gate (so pool-reused controls do not double-subscribe).

On Update, [`PropEntry.Update`](#updatetcontrol-telement-telement) runs and writes through `ReactorBinding.WriteSuppressed` when the entry is controlled.

```csharp
public abstract class PropEntry<TElement, TControl> where TElement : Element where TControl : UIElement
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor`.

**Learn more:** [Extending Reactor with Native Controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/extending-reactor-controls), [The Control Reconciler Protocol](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/control-reconciler-protocol)

# ReactorBinding
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding

Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.4) — public author-facing surface for the echo suppression primitive (§13 Q19). Today this delegates to `ChangeEchoSuppressor.BeginSuppress`; Phase 4 swaps the body for per-control tolerance / coercion metadata as part of the §8 cleanup — the signature does not change. The per-binding wrapper `ReactorBinding<TElement>` (per spec §4) lands in 1.6; this static class is just the primitive entry point.

```csharp
public static class ReactorBinding
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`.

**Learn more:** [Extending Reactor with Native Controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/extending-reactor-controls)

## Methods [#methods]

### `ShouldSuppressEcho` [#shouldsuppressecho]

Read-side counterpart of [`ReactorBinding.WriteSuppressed`](#writesuppresseduielement-action). Call as the first line of a change-event handler: returns `true` when the current fire is the engine-synthesized echo of a prior `WriteSuppressed` write against `target` — **consuming one suppression token** on that counter-based path — so the handler should return early before invoking the user's callback. It also returns `true` *without* consuming a token while inside the non-consuming `ApplySetters` suppression scope. Returns `false` for a genuine user interaction (no outstanding token/scope), for a target that is not a [`FrameworkElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.frameworkelement), or when the target carries no Reactor state.

This is the public primitive the wrapper generator emits for a `[WrapControlled(Deferred = true)]` prop, so a deferred-controlled generated wrapper compiles against Reactor's public surface alone (no `InternalsVisibleTo`) — the read-side gap called out in spec 062 §14. It maps to the counter/scope channel (paired with `WriteSuppressed`), not the value-diff channel.

```csharp
public static bool ShouldSuppressEcho(UIElement target)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | `UIElement` |  |

**Exceptions**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`ArgumentNullException`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentnullexception) | `target` is `null`. |

### `WriteSuppressed` [#writesuppressed]

#### `WriteSuppressed(UIElement, Action)` [#writesuppresseduielement-action]

Runs `mutate` after registering a one-shot suppression token for `target`. The next change-event handler invocation against `target` consumes the token via `ChangeEchoSuppressor.ShouldSuppress` and short-circuits before the user's OnChanged callback fires.

No try/finally — the consumption is event-driven and the counter is harmless if a single token is left at +1 after an exceptional path (it gets consumed by the next change event for that control, which by contract should be one the engine itself just provoked).

```csharp
public static void WriteSuppressed(UIElement target, Action mutate)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | `UIElement` |  |
| `mutate` | `Action` |  |

#### `WriteSuppressed<T>(T, Action<T>)` [#writesuppressedtt-actiont]

Typed overload — saves a cast at the call site for the common case where the handler already has a strongly-typed control reference.

```csharp
public static void WriteSuppressed<T>(T target, Action<T> mutate) where T : UIElement
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | `T` |  |
| `mutate` | `Action<T>` |  |

# ReactorBinding<TElement>
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding-1

One `On<Event>` method per WinUI true-routed input family (pointer, key, tap, focus). Plain CLR events (Toggled, Click, ValueChanged, TextChanged) go through [`ReactorBinding.OnCustomEvent`](#oncustomevent); that path stores its delegate in the per-control event payload box (`ControlEventStateBox`) so pool/recycle correctly clears it.

**Trampoline-refresh pattern** (§3): the handler closure captures [`ReactorBinding._control`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding-1) but NOT the element. On each event fire, the live element is re-read via [`Reconciler.GetElementTag`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler#getelementtagframeworkelement); the binding survives re-renders without resubscribing.

**WriteSuppressed** wraps the 1.4 primitive so authors can suppress the next change-event echo on the bound control.

```csharp
public readonly struct ReactorBinding<TElement> where TElement : Element
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol`.

**Learn more:** [Extending Reactor with Native Controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/extending-reactor-controls), [The Control Reconciler Protocol](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/control-reconciler-protocol)

```csharp

```

## Methods [#methods]

### `OnCustomEvent` [#oncustomevent]

Spec 047 §9.2 — subscribe to a plain CLR event (Toggled, Click, ValueChanged, TextChanged …). The handler closure re-fetches the live element via [`Reconciler.GetElementTag`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/Reconciler#getelementtagframeworkelement) on each fire so it survives re-renders.

The subscription is anchored to the control's lifetime. The engine's pool reset contract clears the per-control event payload on return, so ported handlers are safe to call this once per Mount. Handlers should NOT call it inside [`IElementHandler.Update`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler#update) (subscriptions would multiply across renders).

# ReactorFeatureFlags
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorFeatureFlags

```csharp
public static class ReactorFeatureFlags
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`.

## Remarks [#remarks]

A flag lives here only while its feature is rolling out. Once a flag's default flips to `true` and has soaked for a release, the flag is removed along with the legacy code path it was gating — leaving permanent config knobs here would slow future refactors.

Flags are read lazily — changes after a feature has already initialized are not guaranteed to take effect. Tests that need to toggle a flag should save and restore the value around the scope that depends on it.

## Properties [#properties]

### `FocusRevalidation` [#focusrevalidation]

When true, stale `UseResource` entries refetch on window activation / app resume events. Per-resource opt-out is exposed through `ResourceOptions.RefetchOnWindowFocus` (default `false`).

```csharp
public static bool FocusRevalidation  // get, set
```

**Remarks**

Default: `false`. This mirrors TanStack Query's opt-in posture — window-focus revalidation is surprising in desktop apps where Alt-Tab is a common idiom.

### `HighlightReconcileChanges` [#highlightreconcilechanges]

When true, the reconciler records which `UIElement`s were mounted or modified during each pass and Reactor hosts ([`ReactorHost`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHost) and [`ReactorHostControl`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHostControl), via the shared `HighlightOverlayWiring`) draw semi-transparent overlays (red = new mount, yellow = property update) so you can visualize reconcile impact. The overlay is rendered via Composition visuals and is hit-test invisible.

```csharp
public static bool HighlightReconcileChanges  // get, set
```

**Remarks**

Default: `false`. Intended for interactive debugging sessions. When off, the reconciler skips all collection work so there is zero overhead.

### `UseHookBasedPaging` [#usehookbasedpaging]

When true, `DataGridComponent` reads paged data through `UseInfiniteResource` / `UseDataSource` instead of the legacy `DataPageCache`. Part of the Phase-3 migration in `docs/specs/020-async-resources-design.md` §11.

```csharp
public static bool UseHookBasedPaging  // get, set
```

**Remarks**

Default: `false`. The hook-based path is covered by `DataGridParityFixtures` but is not yet the default for consumers with custom `IDataSource` implementations.

### `WarnLayoutFootguns` [#warnlayoutfootguns]

When true, the reconciler emits a one-time diagnostic warning — at mount and on update — for layout "footguns" that silently collapse to `0×0` — most notably an `HStack`/`VStack` placed in a `Grid` [`GridSize.Auto`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/layout/GridSize#auto) track with no explicit size and no explicitly-sized children (issue #345). Each warning is written to `Debug.WriteLine`.

```csharp
public static bool WarnLayoutFootguns  // get, set
```

**Remarks**

Default: `false`. In `DEBUG` builds the detection is always on regardless of this flag — the flag is the opt-in switch for `Release` builds. When off in `Release` the detection call site is gated by a single read of this flag per mounted/updated element (the check then no-ops for any non-`Grid` element), so it is effectively free.

Detection runs on both the mount and update reconcile paths, so a warning can appear after a state-driven layout change (e.g. a column flipped to `Auto` or an explicit size removed), not just on first render. Each distinct offending placement warns at most once per process.

### `ApplySetters` [#applysetters]

Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.3) — promoted from internal. Runs each setter inside the §8.2 echo-suppression scope so user-authored `.Set(c => c.IsOn = true)` writes don't echo through the engine-wired OnXChanged callback. Provisional API; see `REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW`.

### `ApplyThemeBindings` [#applythemebindings]

Applies [`ThemeRef`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/theming/ThemeRef) bindings as a synthesized `{ThemeResource}`-driven Style. Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.3), promoted from private (per audit existing-api-surface.md); provisional API, see `REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW`.

```csharp
public static void ApplyThemeBindings(FrameworkElement fe, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ThemeRef> bindings)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fe` | `FrameworkElement` |  |
| `bindings` | `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ThemeRef>` |  |

**Remarks**

WinUI handles theme-reactive resolution natively: the live `{ThemeResource}` Style setter re-resolves on the control's effective-theme change, which tracks the per-element/inherited `ActualTheme` (an ancestor `RequestedTheme` override included), not just the app-level theme. This native self-heal is why a ThemeBindings-only element is safe to structurally skip (#758; empirically verified in `ThemeBindingsSkipSelfHealFixtures` across immediate and inherited ancestor `RequestedTheme` toggles). Contrast a `ResourceOverrides.ThemeRef`, which resolves to a CONCRETE brush at reconcile and does NOT self-heal (so it stays theme-sensitive for the skip gate).

A Style already on the control is kept: the themed Style is built `BasedOn` it, and calling this again re-wraps the same base rather than chaining another level. When that base cannot be a `BasedOn` of the control's WinUI type (a Style whose `TargetType` is an app subclass), the themed Style replaces it, as before Styles were kept, and a warning is logged once. Failures are logged, never thrown.

### `DetachReactorState` [#detachreactorstate]

Fully detaches reactor state from a control: nulls the Element and clears the ModifierEventHandlerState's Current\* delegates so any already- attached trampoline on the native event source becomes a no-op if it fires. Use when the control leaves reactor's ownership for good (XamlHost / XamlPage unmount) but may remain alive because the app holds a reference — without this, captured closures stay reachable and stale reactor callbacks can still fire.

```csharp
public static void DetachReactorState(FrameworkElement fe)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fe` | `FrameworkElement` |  |

### `GetElementTag` [#getelementtag]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

### `Reconcile` [#reconcile]

Reconciles one child slot: brings `existingControl`, the control mounted for `oldElement`, up to date with `newElement`, and returns the control the slot should now hold.

```csharp
public UIElement? Reconcile(Element? oldElement, Element? newElement, UIElement? existingControl, Action requestRerender)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `oldElement` | [`Element?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |
| `newElement` | [`Element?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |
| `existingControl` | `UIElement?` |  |
| `requestRerender` | `Action` |  |

**Remarks**

When `newElement` has the element type and key of `oldElement`, the control is patched in place and returned unchanged, unless the update had to build a new control. In every other case the old control is unmounted before the new one is returned: a changed element type or key, an update that built a new control, or a null or empty `newElement`, which returns null. Without an `existingControl` the new element is mounted. Put the result in the slot when it differs from `existingControl`. A custom control updates the child elements it hosts with this method; in an `IElementHandler`, `UpdateContext.ReconcileChild` does the same.

### `RegisterHandler` [#registerhandler]

Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.6 / 1.9) — register a v1 [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler) for the given element type. Dispatched ahead of [`Reconciler.RegisterType`](#registertype) callbacks. Throws on duplicate (including across registries) and on open-generic element types (spec §13 Q17).

```csharp
public void RegisterHandler<TElement, TControl>(IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> handler) where TElement : Element where TControl : UIElement
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handler` | [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler) |  |

**Remarks**

Value-bearing handlers (a control whose programmatic property write raises the same change event as a user edit) must suppress their own write echo with the supported public primitive [`ReactorBinding<TElement>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding-1)'s `WriteSuppressed` method (or the static [`ReactorBinding`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding)); descriptor authors get it via `.Controlled` / `.HandCodedControlled`. See [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler) and `docs/guide/extending-reactor-controls.md` (issue #206).

### `RegisterHandlerForDerivedTypes` [#registerhandlerforderivedtypes]

§14 Phase 3 close-out — register a v1 handler that catches every closed runtime type whose chain reaches `TBase`. Used by the typed templated-list descriptor ports (`TemplatedListViewElement<T>` family) so a single registration on a non-generic intermediate base routes every closed-T variant — same T-erasure pattern the legacy [`Reconciler.Mount`](#mount) switch uses.

Exact-type registrations via [`Reconciler.RegisterHandler`](#registerhandler) always win over a derived-type registration. Throws on duplicate base-type registration.

```csharp
public void RegisterHandlerForDerivedTypes<TBase, TControl>(IElementHandler<TBase, TControl> handler) where TBase : Element where TControl : UIElement
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handler` | [`IElementHandler<TBase, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler) |  |

### `RegisterType` [#registertype]

Registers a custom element type so the reconciler knows how to mount, update, and unmount it. Registered types take priority over built-in types.

Spec 047 §13 Q17 / §14 Phase 1 (1.9) — v1 semantics: - Exact-type lookup via `element.GetType()`; no base-class fallback. - Throws [`InvalidOperationException`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.invalidoperationexception) on duplicate registration, including duplicates against a previously-registered V1 handler (`V1HandlerRegistry`). - Throws on open-generic element types.

The mount and update handlers receive the Reconciler instance so they can recursively mount/update/unmount child elements without capturing external state.

The reconciler records the element on the control it gets back from `mount` or `update` (the element tag) wherever it reads the tag back itself: keyed reconciliation, the `unmount` lookup, `.Ref(...)` cleanup and exit transitions. The callbacks don't call [`Reconciler.SetElementTag`](#setelementtag) for those. Code of your own that reads the element back with [`Reconciler.GetElementTag`](#getelementtagframeworkelement), such as an event handler, still tags the control itself. The tag lives on a [`FrameworkElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.frameworkelement). `TControl` may be declared as [`UIElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.uielement), but in WinUI 3 [`FrameworkElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.frameworkelement) is its only subclass, so every control a registration returns is tagged the same way.

`mount` and `update` are expected to return a control the registration owns. The tag holds one element, so a control that already carries the tag of an element of another type (registration is by exact type, so a derived type counts), for example one `mount` got from [`Reconciler.Mount`](#mount) for a child element, keeps that tag: overwriting it would silence that element's own callbacks (the collision issue #942 tracks for target-wrapping decorators). The registration's key, ref, transitions and `unmount` are not tracked for such a control. To wrap built-in elements, compose them in a component instead.

`update` returns null after patching the control in place; returning the control it was handed means the same. Return a different control only when you replaced it.

`unmount` runs when the reconciler unmounts the control, in place of its own walk over the control's children: a child the callbacks mounted through the reconciler has to be torn down there, for example with [`Reconciler.UnmountChild`](#unmountchild). Calling [`Reconciler.UnmountChild`](#unmountchild) on the control itself from `unmount` walks its children once rather than calling `unmount` again. Without an `unmount` callback the reconciler walks the control's children itself. A control that `update` replaced is unmounted wherever the reconciler reconciles the slot that holds it: a panel, a `Border`, a named slot such as `SplitView.Pane`, a tab's content. A few slots that a control fills by hand still swap a replaced control out without `unmount`: `CommandBar` content, `Expander` content and header template, `ContentDialog`, `Flyout` and `Popup` content, content attached with `.WithFlyout`, `.WithContextFlyout` or `.WithToolTip(element)`, and the realized item content of `ListView`, `GridView`, `TreeView<T>` and templated `FlipView`.

Not part of the `REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW` surface — this is the legacy type-registry path, public since before Spec 047. The §13 Q17 hardening (throw on duplicate, no base-class fallback, no open generics) tightens previously-undefined behavior; it does not change the shape of this API.

```csharp
public void RegisterType<TElement, TControl>(Func<Reconciler, TElement, Action, TControl> mount, Func<Reconciler, TElement, TElement, TControl, Action, UIElement?> update, Action<Reconciler, TControl>? unmount = null) where TElement : Element where TControl : UIElement
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mount` | `Func<Reconciler, TElement, Action, TControl>` |  |  |
| `update` | `Func<Reconciler, TElement, TElement, TControl, Action, UIElement?>` |  |  |
| `unmount` | `Action<Reconciler, TControl>?` | `null` |  |

**Remarks**

A value-bearing custom control (one that raises the same change event for a programmatic write as for a user edit) must suppress its own write echo from the `update` callback. Use the supported public primitive [`ReactorBinding`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding)'s `WriteSuppressed` method — wrap the programmatic write, gate it on an equality check, and pair it 1:1 with the write. For new controls prefer the V1 path: a [`ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ControlDescriptor) (the primary, descriptor-first authoring shape — its `.Controlled` / `.HandCodedControlled` handle echo suppression for you), or a hand-coded [`IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/IElementHandler) via [`Reconciler.RegisterHandler`](#registerhandler) only for irregular controls (its [`ReactorBinding<TElement>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ReactorBinding-1) wraps the same primitive). See `docs/guide/extending-reactor-controls.md` (issue #206).

### `ReturnControl` [#returncontrol]

Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.5) — return a control to its per-type pool, after running the Q18 reset contract:

### `UpdateChild` [#updatechild]

Low-level update of one child control, for callers that have already checked the new element can update it in place. Code outside the framework should call [`Reconciler.Reconcile`](#reconcile), which makes that check and unmounts a control it replaces.

```csharp
public UIElement? UpdateChild(Element oldEl, Element newEl, UIElement control, Action requestRerender)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `oldEl` | [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |
| `newEl` | [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |
| `control` | `UIElement` |  |
| `requestRerender` | `Action` |  |

**Remarks**

Patches `control` to match `newEl` and returns null, or returns a new control when the update had to build one. The caller then unmounts `control` with [`Reconciler.UnmountChild`](#unmountchild) and puts the new control in its slot, in that order, as [`Reconciler.Reconcile`](#reconcile) does: unmounting reads state from the control while it is still in the tree, such as a connected-animation snapshot. It doesn't check that `newEl` has the element type and key of `oldEl`: a changed type throws `InvalidCastException` for a built-in control. The analyzer rule `REACTOR_LIFECYCLE_003` flags calls to this method and offers to switch them to [`Reconciler.Reconcile`](#reconcile).

| [Buttons](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/factories/buttons) | Buttons, toggle buttons, split buttons and hyperlink buttons. |

Pass `true`/`false` (implicit `T → Optional<T>`) to control it from a parent state. |

# Factories: Composition
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/factories/composition

Each factory method returns an element record. Most are on `Factories`, so `using static Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Factories;` covers them. A factory declared on another class names the `using static` it needs.

**Learn more:** [Components](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/components), [Advanced Patterns](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/advanced)

## `Component` [#component]

```csharp
ComponentElement Component<T>() where T : Component, new()
ComponentElement<TProps> Component<T, TProps>(TProps props) where T : Component<TProps>, new()
```

| Overload | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Component<T>()` | Embed a Component class as a child element. Usage: Component\<MyWidget\>() |
| `Component<T, TProps>(TProps)` | Embed a Component class with typed props as a child element. Returns [`ComponentElement<TProps>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/composition#componentelementtprops) so callers can use a record `with`-expression to produce a modified copy with updated typed props (records are immutable — `with` clones, it does not mutate). Usage: Component\<MyWidget, string\>("param") |

**Returns:** [`ComponentElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/composition#componentelement), [`ComponentElement<TProps>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/composition#componentelementtprops).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `props` | `TProps` |  |

## `Empty` [#empty]

Renders nothing. Useful as a default/fallback.

```csharp
Element Empty()
```

**Returns:** [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element).

## `ErrorBoundary` [#errorboundary]

```csharp
ErrorBoundaryElement ErrorBoundary(Element child, Element fallback)
ErrorBoundaryElement ErrorBoundary(Element child, Func<Exception, Element> fallback)
```

| Overload | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ErrorBoundary(Element, Element)` | Wraps a child subtree in an error boundary with a static fallback element. |
| `ErrorBoundary(Element, Func<Exception, Element>)` | Wraps a child subtree in an error boundary. If any component in the subtree throws during rendering, the fallback function is called with the exception. When the ErrorBoundary re-renders, it retries the child (error recovery). |

**Returns:** [`ErrorBoundaryElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/composition#errorboundaryelement).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `child` | [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |
| `fallback` | [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) or `Func<Exception, Element>` |  |

## `Expr` [#expr]

Inline block-expression escape hatch: invokes `render` and returns its element, or `EmptyElement.Instance` when the lambda returns `null`. Lets callers write multi-statement bodies inside a DSL tree without extracting a local function or relying on the `((Func<Element?>)(() => …))()` cast trick.

```csharp
Element Expr(Func<Element?> render)
```

**Returns:** [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `Func<Element?>` |  |

**Remarks**

Spec 033 §5. `Expr` performs no memoization, owns no `RenderContext`, and is not a reconciler boundary — it is purely composition sugar. If the body needs hooks, use `Memo(...)` or a `Component<TProps>` instead.

Exceptions thrown inside `render` propagate unchanged so the surrounding error-boundary path applies.

**Example**

```csharp
VStack(
    Header(),
    Expr(() => {
        var summary = ComputeSummary(orders);
        return summary.Total > 0
            ? TotalsBanner(summary)
            : null;
    }),
    Footer())
```

**Exceptions**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`ArgumentNullException`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentnullexception) | `render` is `null`. |

## `ForEach` [#foreach]

```csharp
Element ForEach<T>(IEnumerable<T> items, Func<T, Element> render)
Element ForEach<T>(IEnumerable<T> items, Func<T, int, Element> render)
```

| Overload | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ForEach<T>(IEnumerable<T>, Func<T, Element>)` | Map a list to elements (like .map() in React JSX): ForEach(items, item =\> TextBlock(item.Name))  When `T` implements [`IReactorKeyed`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/IReactorKeyed), each projected element is keyed from `item.Key` unless the projection already set one, so the reconciler matches rows by identity instead of by position. |
| `ForEach<T>(IEnumerable<T>, Func<T, int, Element>)` | Map with index: ForEach(items, (item, i) =\> TextBlock($"\{i\}: \{item\}"))  Keys from [`IReactorKeyed`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/IReactorKeyed) items exactly as the single-parameter overload does. |

**Returns:** [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `IEnumerable<T>` |  |
| `render` | `Func<T, Element>` or `Func<T, int, Element>` |  |

## `Memo` [#memo]

```csharp
MemoElement Memo(Func<RenderContext, Element> render, params object?[] dependencies)
KeyedMemoElement Memo<TKey>(TKey key, Func<Element> factory)
```

| Overload | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Memo(Func<RenderContext, Element>, object?[])` | Define a memoized inline function component. Skips re-render when dependencies haven't changed. Empty deps array = render once + own state changes only. Non-empty = re-render when any dep changes. Usage: Memo(ctx =\> TextBlock("stable"), someProp, otherProp) |
| `Memo<TKey>(TKey, Func<Element>)` | Opt-in typed keyed memo for virtualized rows (issue #327). Wrap a row body in `Memo(key, () => …)` to assert the body is a **pure function of `key`**. Inside a virtualized list (`VirtualList`, `LazyVStack<T>`, …) the owning [`ElementFactory<T>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/ElementFactory) caches the built element per key in a bounded LRU, so a container recycle that re-asks for the same key returns the *same* element instance — the reconciler then skips the row's rebuild + per-row diff entirely (sub-µs). This targets the fast-scroll cost of variable-height rows, where every recycle otherwise rebuilds and diffs the row from scratch.  Usage: `renderItem: i => Memo(items[i].Id, () => Border(BigVariableHeightRow(items[i])))`  **Purity is your responsibility.** The key must capture every input the factory reads. If the body also depends on, say, a selection flag, fold it into the key: `Memo((items[i].Id, isSelected), () => …)`. Closing over unkeyed mutable state will serve stale content. The cache is cleared automatically when the list's items/renderItem change.  **Apply modifiers inside the factory, not on the wrapper.** The cross-recycle cache only unwraps a *bare* `Memo(key, …)` — one with no fluent modifiers, no `.WithKey(…)`, and no attached state (Grid/Canvas attached properties, `.Provide(…)` context, or theme bindings) on the wrapper itself. Decorating the wrapper (`Memo(id, () => …).Padding(8)`) opts the row out of caching and silently loses the perf benefit; put modifiers on the element the factory returns instead: `Memo(id, () => Border(…).Padding(8))`.  Outside a virtualized factory the wrapper is transparent but *keyed*: a re-render with the same key is a no-op (the factory is not re-invoked and the inner subtree is not diffed), while a changed key replaces the inner (unmount + fresh mount of the new factory output). The exception is a component inside the subtree that updates its own state: the factory then runs again so the reconciler can walk down to that component. The cross-recycle cache only applies on the virtualized-list path. It is always safe to use anywhere an element is expected. |

**Returns:** [`MemoElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/composition#memoelement), [`KeyedMemoElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/composition#keyedmemoelement).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `Func<RenderContext, Element>` |  |
| `dependencies` | `object?[]` |  |
| `key` | `TKey` | Stable identity that fully determines `factory`'s output. |
| `factory` | `Func<Element>` | Builds the row element. Invoked once per key on a cache miss. |

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `TKey` | Key type. Boxed to [`Object`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.object) and compared with [`Object.Equals`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.object.equals) / [`Object.GetHashCode`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.object.gethashcode), so value keys (ints, strings, records, value tuples) dedupe by value. This is what lets the int-index `VirtualList` path hit the cache. |

## `RenderEachTime` [#rendereachtime]

Define an inline function component that re-renders on every parent render (no memoization), keeping its own hook scope. Made explicit so the reader can tell the always-re-render case apart from a missing deps array.

```csharp
FuncElement RenderEachTime(Func<RenderContext, Element> render)
```

**Returns:** [`FuncElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/composition#funcelement).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `Func<RenderContext, Element>` |  |

**Remarks**

Spec 033 §4. Use sparingly — components that re-render on every parent render defeat the memoization story and can amplify render storms. Prefer [`Memo`](#memo) with an explicit deps array whenever the re-render trigger can be enumerated.

## `XamlHost` [#xamlhost]

Embeds an arbitrary [`FrameworkElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.frameworkelement) (a UserControl, a custom control) created by `factory` on mount; `updater` runs after creation and on every update. Equivalent to `new XamlHostElement(factory, updater) { TypeKey = typeKey }`, but records the call site for the source map like every other factory.

```csharp
XamlHostElement XamlHost(Func<FrameworkElement> factory, Action<FrameworkElement>? updater = null, string? typeKey = null)
```

**Returns:** [`XamlHostElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/interop#xamlhostelement).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `factory` | `Func<FrameworkElement>` |  | Creates the hosted control on mount. |
| `updater` | `Action<FrameworkElement>?` | `null` | Patches the hosted control after creation and on every update. |
| `typeKey` | `string?` | `null` | Discriminator for in-place updates: two hosts update in place only when their keys match, so unrelated hosted controls are not reconciled against each other. |

## `XamlPage` [#xamlpage]

Embeds an existing XAML [`Page`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.page) in a [`Frame`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/factories/navigation#frame), navigated to `pageType` with `parameter`. Re-navigates in place when either changes. Equivalent to `new XamlPageElement(pageType, parameter)`, but records the call site for the source map like every other factory.

```csharp
XamlPageElement XamlPage(Type pageType, object? parameter = null)
```

**Returns:** [`XamlPageElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/interop#xamlpageelement).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pageType` | `Type` |  |  |
| `parameter` | `object?` | `null` |  |

## `Card` [#card]

Renders `child` inside a card-styled [`BorderElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/layout#borderelement). Defaults match the canonical WinUI card: 8px corner radius, ~16px padding, theme-aware `CardBackgroundFillColorDefaultBrush` + `CardStrokeColorDefaultBrush` 1px stroke. Re-themes on light / dark / contrast switches because the brushes resolve through [`ThemeRef`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/theming/ThemeRef).

```csharp
BorderElement Card(Element child)
```

**Returns:** [`BorderElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/layout#borderelement).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `child` | [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |

**Remarks**

Override any preset by chaining a fluent on the returned border: `Card(child).Padding(24).CornerRadius(16).Background(Theme.SubtleFill)`.
