## `Flex` [#flex]

```csharp
FlexElement Flex(params Element?[] children)
FlexElement Flex(FlexDirection direction, params Element?[] children)
```

| Overload | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Flex(Element?[])` | Creates a Yoga-based flexbox container ([`FlexElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/layout#flexelement)). Default direction is [`FlexDirection.Row`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/layout/flex-enums#values_1). |

| Name | Type | Description |

| `direction` | [`FlexDirection`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/layout/flex-enums#flexdirection) |  |

**Remarks**

Reactor-original — there is no WinUI `Flex` control. This is a custom panel backed by Yoga (Facebook's flexbox engine, see [`FlexPanel`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/layout/flex-enums#flexpanel)) for full CSS-flexbox semantics inside a WinUI tree. Prefer [`VStack`](#vstack) / [`HStack`](#hstack) for simple stacks; reach for Flex when you need wrap, justify-content / align-items, or per-child grow/shrink. (spec 039 §0.3)

Reactor-original — see [`Flex`](#flex) for the rationale.

## `InterspersedGrid` [#interspersedgrid]

Creates a grid with items interspersed with separator elements along one axis. Commonly used for split panels where children are separated by splitters.

Each item gets a proportional (\*) size from `proportions`, and separators get a fixed pixel size of `separatorSize`.

Example: InterspersedGrid(Orientation.Horizontal, children, proportions, 6, i =\> MySplitter(i)) produces columns: "0.33\*", "6", "0.33\*", "6", "0.34\*" with children and splitters placed.

```csharp
GridElement InterspersedGrid(Orientation orientation, Element[] items, double[] proportions, double separatorSize, Func<int, Element> separatorFactory)
```

**Returns:** [`GridElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/layout#gridelement).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `Orientation` |  |
| `items` | [`Element[]`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |
| `proportions` | `double[]` |  |
| `separatorSize` | `double` |  |
| `separatorFactory` | `Func<int, Element>` |  |

## `VStack` [#vstack]

```csharp

```

| Overload | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `VStack(Element?[])` | Creates a vertical [`StackElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/layout#stackelement) (WinUI `StackPanel` with [`Orientation.Vertical`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.orientation.vertical)). Default `Spacing` is 8 — see [`StackElement.Spacing`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/layout#stackelement). |
| `VStack(double, Element?[])` | Creates a vertical [`StackElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/layout#stackelement) with an explicit `Spacing` override (the first positional argument). |

**Returns:** [`StackElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/layout#stackelement).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | [`Element?[]`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |
| `spacing` | `double` |  |

**Remarks**

Reactor-original name — WinUI exposes one `StackPanel` control keyed by `Orientation`; Reactor splits it into two factories ([`VStack`](#vstack) / [`HStack`](#hstack)) because the orientation is almost always known at the call site and the shorter names reduce DSL noise. The SwiftUI / React Native names are load-bearing for cross-platform agent familiarity. (spec 039 §0.3)

Reactor-original convenience overload — see [`VStack`](#vstack) for the naming rationale.

## `Frame` [#frame]

A WinUI `Frame` that navigates to `sourcePageType` once on mount.

`Frame` is for interop with pages that already have a `.xaml` file. A `Page` declared only in C# is absent from the XAML metadata the compiler generates, so WinUI cannot resolve it; Reactor refuses such a navigation and reports it through `.NavigationFailed(...)` rather than letting it fault. For navigation inside a Reactor app use `UseNavigation<TRoute>` with `NavigationHost`.

```csharp
FrameElement Frame(Type? sourcePageType = null, object? navigationParameter = null)
```

**Returns:** [`FrameElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/navigation#frameelement).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sourcePageType` | `Type?` | `null` |  |
| `navigationParameter` | `object?` | `null` |  |

## `NavigationHost` [#navigationhost]

Creates a navigation host that renders the current route's content. Automatically provides the navigation handle via context so child components can retrieve it with `UseNavigation<TRoute>()`. Use `with { }` to set Transition, CacheMode, and CacheSize.


## `AcrylicBrush` [#acrylicbrush]

Creates a new AcrylicBrush. This allocates a WinRT DependencyObject on every call. On hot paths (e.g., inside Render methods), cache the result with `UseMemo`:

```csharp
var brush = ctx.UseMemo(() => AcrylicBrush(color, 0.8), color);
```

**Remarks**

The element reconciles to a WinUI `ProgressBar`. ## `InlineUI` [#inlineui]

```csharp
RichTextInlineUIContainer InlineUI(Element child)
RichTextInlineUIContainer InlineUI(Func<FrameworkElement> factory)
```

| Overload | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `InlineUI(Element)` | Issue #480 — embeds a Reactor `child` element inline inside a [`RichTextBlock`](#richtextblock). Mirrors WinUI's `InlineUIContainer`. The child is reconciled as any other Reactor element — descendant hooks, event wiring, and pooling all work as expected. Re-renders use the incremental update path: structurally compatible inlines are mutated in place and embedded children retain their WinUI control identity (Slider drag, focus, and animation state survive). Only structural changes (paragraph count change, inline type change, Route A↔B swap) fall back to a full block rebuild. |
| `InlineUI(Func<FrameworkElement>)` | Issue #480 — embeds a native WinUI control (produced by `factory`) inline inside a [`RichTextBlock`](#richtextblock). Escape hatch for controls without a Reactor element counterpart. The factory is re-invoked only when its delegate identity changes; passing the same factory across renders preserves the control instance. |

**Returns:** [`RichTextInlineUIContainer`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/controls/rich-text#richtextinlineuicontainer).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `child` | [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |
| `factory` | `Func<FrameworkElement>` |  |

# Hooks
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks

Hooks are how Reactor components subscribe to state, schedule effects, and reach into the framework's lifecycle from a function-shaped `Render` body. Call them on the `RenderContext` (or from a `Component`), always in the same order, and never inside a condition or a loop.

**Learn more:** [Hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks), [Effects and Lifecycle](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/effects), [Rules of Reactor](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/get-started/rules-of-reactor)

## State [#state]

Hooks that keep values between renders.

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`UseCollection`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseCollection) | Subscribes to an ObservableCollection and re-renders on Add/Remove/Reset. |
| [`UseExternalStore`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseExternalStore) | Subscribes to an external store that exposes a current snapshot getter. |
| [`UseObservable`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseObservable) | Subscribes to an INotifyPropertyChanged source and re-renders when any property changes. |
| [`UseObservableProperty`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseObservableProperty) | Subscribes to a specific property on an INotifyPropertyChanged source. |
| [`UseObservableTree`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseObservableTree) | Observes an object and all nested INotifyPropertyChanged values reachable through its properties. |
| [`UsePersisted`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UsePersisted) | Like UseState, but the value survives unmount/remount via an in-memory cache. |
| [`UseReducer`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseReducer) | Declares a piece of state with a functional updater variant. |
| [`UseRef`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseRef) | Returns a mutable ref object that persists across renders. |
| [`UseState`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseState) | Declares a piece of state. |

## Effects and memoization [#effects-and-memoization]

Hooks that run side effects or cache values between renders.

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`UseCallback`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseCallback) | Returns a stable callback reference that doesn't change between renders. |
| [`UseEffect`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseEffect) | Runs a side effect after render. |
| [`UseMemo`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseMemo) | Memoizes a computed value, recomputing only when dependencies change. |

## `AnnounceHandle` [#announcehandle]

Handle returned by [`UseAnnounce`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseAnnounce). Provides an imperative [`AnnounceHandle.Announce`](#announcestring) method for screen reader live-region announcements plus a zero-size [`AnnounceHandle.Region`](#region) element that must be included somewhere in the component's rendered tree.


### Methods [#methods]

#### `Announce` [#announce]

##### `Announce(string)` [#announcestring]

Announces a message to screen readers (polite — queued after current speech).

```csharp
public void Announce(string message)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` |  |

##### `Announce(string, bool)` [#announcestring-bool]

Announces a message to screen readers.

```csharp
public void Announce(string message, bool assertive)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | The text to announce. |
| `assertive` | `bool` | If true, interrupts current speech immediately. If false (default), queued after current speech finishes. |

**Remarks**

Thread-safe. When called on the UI thread the announcement is raised synchronously. When called from any other thread it is marshalled to the captured UI [`DispatcherQueue`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.dispatching.dispatcherqueue) and runs asynchronously (fire-and-forget) — it may complete after this method returns. Calls made before the live-region [`AnnounceHandle.Region`](#region) has mounted are ignored.

## `Mutation<TInput, TResult>` [#mutationtinput-tresult]

Handle returned by the `UseMutation` hook. Carries the pending/error/last-result state and the [`Mutation.RunAsync`](#runasync) entry point.

```csharp
public sealed class Mutation<TInput, TResult>
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hooks`.

### Remarks [#remarks_1]

**Concurrency.** Overlapping [`Mutation.RunAsync`](#runasync) calls each get their own cancellation token; both complete and fire their callbacks in completion order. [`Mutation.LastResult`](#lastresult) is whichever finishes last. If you want strictly-serialized mutations, wrap [`Mutation.RunAsync`](#runasync) behind your own gate (or disable the trigger control while [`Mutation.IsPending`](#ispending) is true).

**Reset.** [`Mutation.Reset`](#reset) clears [`Mutation.Error`](#error) and [`Mutation.LastResult`](#lastresult) but does **not** cancel in-flight work — this is an explicit choice so a "dismiss the error banner" action doesn't abort the user's retry.

### Properties [#properties_2]

#### `Error` [#error]

Most recent error, or null if the last completion was a success or [`Mutation.Reset`](#reset) was called.

```csharp
public Exception? Error  // get
```

#### `IsPending` [#ispending]

True while at least one [`Mutation.RunAsync`](#runasync) call is in-flight.

```csharp
public bool IsPending  // get
```

#### `LastResult` [#lastresult]

Most recent successful result, or default if none yet.

```csharp
public TResult? LastResult  // get
```

### Methods [#methods_2]

#### `Reset` [#reset]

Clear [`Mutation.Error`](#error) and [`Mutation.LastResult`](#lastresult). Does not cancel or affect any in-flight [`Mutation.RunAsync`](#runasync) call.

```csharp
public void Reset()
```

#### `RunAsync` [#runasync]

Kick off the mutator with `input`. Returns a task that completes with the mutator's result or fault.

```csharp
public Task<TResult> RunAsync(TInput input)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `TInput` |  |

**Remarks**

Ordering: [`MutationOptions.OnOptimistic`](#onoptimistic) fires synchronously before the mutator starts. [`MutationOptions.OnSuccess`](#onsuccess) or [`MutationOptions.OnError`](#onerror) fires on the hook's dispatcher thread after completion.

If [`MutationOptions.OnOptimistic`](#onoptimistic) throws, the mutator is never invoked and the returned task is faulted with the optimistic exception — prevents half-applied state where the optimistic patch ran but the real request can't.

## `MutationOptions<TInput, TResult>` [#mutationoptionstinput-tresult]

Callbacks and side-effects for the `UseMutation` hook. All callbacks are optional; all run on the dispatcher thread except [`MutationOptions.OnOptimistic`](#onoptimistic) which runs synchronously on the caller of [`Mutation.RunAsync`](#runasync) — the typical case is a render-thread click handler, so the optimistic update lands in the very next frame without a dispatcher hop.

```csharp
public sealed record MutationOptions<TInput, TResult>(Action<TInput>? OnOptimistic = null, Action<TResult, TInput>? OnSuccess = null, Action<Exception, TInput>? OnError = null, string[]? InvalidateKeys = null)
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hooks`.

### Remarks [#remarks_2]

**InvalidateKeys.** On success, each key is passed to [`QueryCache.Invalidate`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/query-cache#invalidate). Sibling `UseResource` hooks subscribed to those keys will observe the invalidation and refetch on their next render.

Error path: [`MutationOptions.OnError`](#onerror) fires but [`MutationOptions.InvalidateKeys`](#invalidatekeys) does **not** — the assumption is the server state didn't change, so the cache is still valid.

### Constructors [#constructors_1]

#### `MutationOptions` [#mutationoptions]

Callbacks and side-effects for the `UseMutation` hook. All callbacks are optional; all run on the dispatcher thread except [`MutationOptions.OnOptimistic`](#onoptimistic) which runs synchronously on the caller of [`Mutation.RunAsync`](#runasync) — the typical case is a render-thread click handler, so the optimistic update lands in the very next frame without a dispatcher hop.

```csharp

```

**Parameters**

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `OnSuccess` | `Action<TResult, TInput>?` | `null` |  |
| `OnError` | `Action<Exception, TInput>?` | `null` |  |

**Remarks**

**InvalidateKeys.** On success, each key is passed to [`QueryCache.Invalidate`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/query-cache#invalidate). Sibling `UseResource` hooks subscribed to those keys will observe the invalidation and refetch on their next render.

Error path: [`MutationOptions.OnError`](#onerror) fires but [`MutationOptions.InvalidateKeys`](#invalidatekeys) does **not** — the assumption is the server state didn't change, so the cache is still valid.

# Pending
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/pending

**Learn more:** [Hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks)

## `PendingComponent` [#pendingcomponent]

Component backing the `Pending` element. Hosts a [`PendingScope`](#pendingscope), subscribes to its [`PendingScope.Changed`](#changed) event, and chooses between [`PendingProps.Fallback`](#fallback) and [`PendingProps.Child`](#child).

```csharp
public sealed class PendingComponent : Component<PendingProps>
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hooks`. Inherits from [`Component<TProps>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/Component-1).

### Remarks [#remarks]

The child subtree is always rendered. When the scope reports any loading resource, the child's `Visibility` is flipped to `Collapsed` and the fallback is shown instead. Because the subtree stays mounted, its hooks keep running, their fetches complete in the background, and the UI swaps to the real content on the next render frame after the scope reports clean.

### Constructors [#constructors]

#### `PendingComponent` [#pendingcomponent_1]

```csharp
public PendingComponent()
```

### Methods [#methods]

#### `Render` [#render]

```csharp
public override Element Render()
```

## `PendingFactory` [#pendingfactory]

Entry-point factory for the `Pending` bubble-up element. See `docs/specs/020-async-resources-design.md` §10 for the full mechanism.

```csharp
public static class PendingFactory
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hooks`.

### Methods [#methods_1]

#### `Pending` [#pending_1]

Wraps `child` with a fresh [`PendingScope`](#pendingscope). Renders `fallback` instead of `child` while any `UseResource`/`UseInfiniteResource` in the subtree is in the `Loading` state. `Reloading(previous)` does **not** trigger the fallback — spec §10.1.

```csharp
public static Element Pending(Element fallback, Element child)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fallback` | [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |
| `child` | [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) |  |

**Remarks**

The child subtree is always mounted so its hooks register with the scope. The element simply chooses which rendered tree to show — there is no unwinding of rendering, and no reconciler involvement.

Marked `[ReactorSourceTransparent]` (see [`ReactorSourceTransparentAttribute`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/diagnostics/ReactorSourceTransparentAttribute), spec 010) because it is a pure forwarder: the element is really built by the `Component<,>` call on the next line, inside Reactor's own assembly, where no consumer call site exists to intercept. Without the annotation a `Pending(...)` element reports no location at all. With it, the interceptor in the consumer's compilation stamps the line they wrote `Pending(` on, which is the answer they were looking for.

## `PendingScope` [#pendingscope]

Shared loading-state ref-count consumed by the `Pending` element and populated by `UseResource` / `UseInfiniteResource` hooks inside the scope. When the scope observes **any** registered resource in the `Loading` state (not `Reloading`), the owning `Pending` element renders its fallback instead of the child subtree.

```csharp
public sealed class PendingScope
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hooks`.

### Remarks [#remarks_1]

**Semantics.** Only `Loading` triggers the fallback — spec §10.1. A `Reloading(previous)` is "we already have something to show" and the subtree continues to render normally.

**Threading.** All members are thread-safe. [`PendingScope.Changed`](#changed) fires on the thread that caused the mutation — consumers (typically `Pending`'s re-render trigger) marshal it to the dispatcher themselves.

**Scope nesting.** Each `Pending` provides a fresh scope to its subtree, so nested `Pending`s are independent. A hook registers only with its nearest ancestor scope.

**Remarks**

If `d1`'s compile-time type is an array of reference types (e.g. `string[]`), it is treated as a dependency *list* and compared element-wise — matching the `params object[]` overload — not as a single reference-compared value. A dependency whose static type is not an array is always compared as one value, even if its runtime value happens to be an array.

# UseColorScheme
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseColorScheme

Returns the app-global [`ColorScheme`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/theming/enums#colorscheme) — [`ColorScheme.Light`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/theming/enums#values_1) or [`ColorScheme.Dark`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/theming/enums#values_1), read from `Application.Current.RequestedTheme`.

The value is re-evaluated on every render — when the app theme changes, [`ReactorHost`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHost) triggers a re-render so this hook naturally picks up the new value.

This hook does **not** observe per-element `RequestedTheme` overrides: it consults the application, not the calling component's position in the tree, so a component inside a `.RequestedTheme(Dark)` subtree still reports the app theme. It also never returns [`ColorScheme.HighContrast`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/theming/enums#values_1) in a running app — use [`UseHighContrast`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseHighContrast) for forced-colors mode.

```csharp
public ColorScheme UseColorScheme()
```

Declared on [`RenderContext`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/RenderContext).

**Learn more:** [Theming Tokens](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/theming-tokens), [Hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks)

# UseCommand
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseCommand

Processes a Command for use in a component. Always consumes a **stable hook shape** (independent of whether the command is sync/async or debounced), so a command at a given call site can flip between sync↔async or [`Command.DebounceMs`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command#debouncems) 0↔N across renders without ever reordering hook slots. For a pure sync command with no [`Command.DebounceMs`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command#debouncems) the original command is returned unchanged (identity preserved). For async commands, wraps ExecuteAsync with automatic IsExecuting tracking and re-entrance guards. When [`Command.DebounceMs`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command#debouncems) \> 0, wraps the dispatch with a leading-edge debounce: a fire within the window of the prior accepted fire is dropped and [`Command.IsDebouncing`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command#isdebouncing) (hence [`Command.IsEnabled`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command#isenabled)=false) reflects the window so the bound control disables, re-enabling when the window elapses. The returned command has a sync Execute action, ExecuteAsync = null, and preserves the authored DebounceMs value (re-passing it through UseCommand is a no-op — debounce is never applied twice).

```csharp
public Command UseCommand(Command command)
public Command<T> UseCommand<T>(Command<T> command)
```

Declared on [`RenderContext`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/RenderContext).

**Learn more:** [Commanding](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/commanding), [Hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks)

## Overloads [#overloads]

| Overload | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`UseCommand(Command)`](#usecommandcommand) | Processes a Command for use in a component. |
| [`UseCommand<T>(Command<T>)`](#usecommandtcommandt) | Processes a parameterized Command for use in a component. |

# UseDataSource
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseDataSource

Projects an [`IDataSource<T>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/IDataSource) through `UseInfiniteResource`, surfacing its pages as an [`InfiniteResource<TItem>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/paging#infiniteresourcetitem). | [`UseDataSource<T>(RenderContext, IDataSource<T>, DataRequest, QueryCache, InfiniteResourceOptions?, IHookDispatcher?)`](#usedatasourcetrendercontext-idatasourcet-datarequest-querycache-infiniteresourceoptions-ihookdispatcher) | Projects an `IDataSource<T>` through `UseInfiniteResource`, surfacing its pages as an `InfiniteResource<TItem>`. |

### `UseDataSource<T>(RenderContext, IDataSource<T>, DataRequest, InfiniteResourceOptions?, IHookDispatcher?)` [#usedatasourcetrendercontext-idatasourcet-datarequest-infiniteresourceoptions-ihookdispatcher]

Overload that reads the ambient [`QueryCache`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/query-cache#querycache) from [`AppContexts.QueryCache`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/AppContexts#querycache). [`ReactorHost`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHost) installs a process-wide default cache at startup; tests or subtrees may override it via `.Provide(AppContexts.QueryCache, customCache)`.

```csharp
public static InfiniteResource<T> UseDataSource<T>(this RenderContext ctx, IDataSource<T> source, DataRequest request, InfiniteResourceOptions? options = null, IHookDispatcher? dispatcher = null)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | [`IDataSource<T>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/IDataSource) |  |  |
| `request` | [`DataRequest`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/descriptors#datarequest) |  |  |
| `options` | [`InfiniteResourceOptions?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/paging#infiniteresourceoptions) | `null` |  |
| `dispatcher` | [`IHookDispatcher?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/hook-types#ihookdispatcher) | `null` |  |

**Remarks**

The initial page size comes from `options.PageSize` (default 50) when `options` is supplied, or `request.PageSize` otherwise, and is clamped to at least 1. This size stays fixed across renders and query restarts. To change it, have the parent remount the calling component with a different key, e.g. `.WithKey($"tasks:{pageSize}")`, or increment a parent-owned reset version used by `.WithKey($"tasks:{resetVersion}")`.

### `UseDataSource<T>(RenderContext, IDataSource<T>, DataRequest, QueryCache, InfiniteResourceOptions?, IHookDispatcher?)` [#usedatasourcetrendercontext-idatasourcet-datarequest-querycache-infiniteresourceoptions-ihookdispatcher]


| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | [`IDataSource<T>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/IDataSource) |  |  |
| `request` | [`DataRequest`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/descriptors#datarequest) |  |  |
| `cache` | [`QueryCache`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/query-cache#querycache) |  |  |
| `options` | [`InfiniteResourceOptions?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/data/paging#infiniteresourceoptions) | `null` |  |
| `dispatcher` | [`IHookDispatcher?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/hook-types#ihookdispatcher) | `null` |  |

**Remarks**

The initial page size comes from `options.PageSize` (default 50) when `options` is supplied, or `request.PageSize` otherwise, and is clamped to at least 1. This size stays fixed across renders and query restarts. To change it, have the parent remount the calling component with a different key, e.g. `.WithKey($"tasks:{pageSize}")`, or increment a parent-owned reset version used by `.WithKey($"tasks:{resetVersion}")`.

### `UseDataSource<TItem>(IDataSource<TItem>, DataRequest, InfiniteResourceOptions?)` [#usedatasourcetitemidatasourcetitem-datarequest-infiniteresourceoptions]

Projects a data source into a paged resource using the ambient query cache.

**Remarks**

# UseDevtools
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseDevtools

1. The binary was built with `Reactor.DevtoolsSupport` enabled (build-time capability gate).
2. The process was launched with `--devtools app` or `--devtools run` (session-scoped opt-in by the user running the app).

The value is frozen for the session; this call does not consume a hook slot and does not cause re-renders. Components use it to gate dev-only UX so the subtree is never constructed in retail sessions:

```csharp
var dev = ctx.UseDevtools();
return VStack(Content(), dev ? DebugOverlay() : null);
```

```csharp
public static bool UseDevtools(this RenderContext ctx)
```

### `UseEffect(Action, object[])` [#useeffectaction-object]

Runs a side effect after render. The effect re-runs when any dependency changes. Pass an empty array for "run once on mount" semantics. Returns a cleanup action that runs before the next effect or on unmount.

### `UseEffect<T1>(Action, T1)` [#useeffectt1action-t1]

Single-dependency `UseEffect` overload that avoids the `params object[]` allocation (and value-type boxing) on the deps-unchanged path. Semantically identical to the params overload called with one dependency: the effect re-runs only when `d1` changes.

```csharp
public void UseEffect<T1>(Action effect, T1 d1)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `effect` | `Action` |  |
| `d1` | `T1` |  |

**Remarks**

If `d1`'s compile-time type is an array of reference types (e.g. `string[]`), it is treated as a dependency *list* and compared element-wise — matching the `params object[]` overload — not as a single reference-compared value. A dependency whose static type is not an array is always compared as one value, even if its runtime value happens to be an array.

# UseElementFocus
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseElementFocus

Bind the ref to an element via `.Ref(ref)`. Calling `RequestFocus` schedules [`FocusManager.Focus`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/FocusManager#focus) on the UI dispatcher; if the ref's target has not mounted yet the call is a no-op.

# UseExternalStore
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseExternalStore

```csharp
public TSnapshot UseExternalStore<TSnapshot>(Func<Action, Action> subscribe, Func<TSnapshot> getSnapshot, IEqualityComparer<TSnapshot>? comparer = null)
```

Declared on [`RenderContext`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/RenderContext).

**Learn more:** [Reactivity Model](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/reactivity-model), [Hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks)

## Parameters [#parameters]

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subscribe` | `Func<Action, Action>` |  |  |
| `getSnapshot` | `Func<TSnapshot>` |  |  |
| `comparer` | `IEqualityComparer<TSnapshot>?` | `null` |  |

## Remarks [#remarks]

`subscribe` is the effect dependency that decides whether the subscription is torn down and re-established, so it must be a **stable** delegate across renders. Pass a method group (e.g. `store.Subscribe`) or a [`UseCallback`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseCallback#usecallbackaction-object)-memoized delegate. A fresh capturing lambda (`onChanged => store.Subscribe(onChanged)`) is a new delegate every render and will unsubscribe/resubscribe on each one. This mirrors React's guidance for `useSyncExternalStore`.

`getSnapshot` must return a **cached/stable** value that only changes identity when the underlying data changes. Returning a fresh, never-equal value on every call (e.g. `() => items.ToArray()`) combined with an unstable `subscribe` can spin: re-render re-runs the effect, the immediate re-check observes a "change", and that forces another render. Memoize the snapshot or return a value the supplied comparer treats as equal when nothing changed.

## Use from a class component [#use-from-a-class-component]

Class components can call the same hook directly. These overloads forward to the ones above:

```csharp
protected TSnapshot UseExternalStore<TSnapshot>(Func<Action, Action> subscribe, Func<TSnapshot> getSnapshot, IEqualityComparer<TSnapshot>? comparer = null)
```

**Remarks**

If `d1`'s compile-time type is an array of reference types (e.g. `string[]`), it is treated as a dependency *list* and compared element-wise — matching the `params object[]` overload — not as a single reference-compared value. A dependency whose static type is not an array is always compared as one value, even if its runtime value happens to be an array.

# UseMemoCells
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseMemoCells

Memoize cell construction for `items`. On the first render the builder runs for every index; on subsequent renders, an item that compares [`Object.Equals`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.object.equals) against the previous render's value at the same index reuses the previous element. Any change to `dependencies` invalidates the entire cache and rebuilds every cell.

```csharp
public static Element[] UseMemoCells<T>(this RenderContext ctx, IReadOnlyList<T> items, Func<T, int, Element> builder, params object[] dependencies) where T : notnull
```

An extension method on [`RenderContext`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/RenderContext), declared in `UseMemoCellsExtensions`.

**Learn more:** [Hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks), [Performance](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/performance)

## Parameters [#parameters]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `IReadOnlyList<T>` | Source items, one cell per item. |
| `builder` | `Func<T, int, Element>` | Builder for a single cell. Must be a pure function of `(item, index)` plus `dependencies`. Closure captures missing from the deps list are flagged by the `REACTOR_HOOKS_007` analyzer. |
| `dependencies` | `object[]` | Trailing-`params` list of values the builder closes over. Equivalent semantics to `UseMemo`: any change invalidates the entire memo. |

## Type parameters [#type-parameters]

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `T` | Item type. |

## Remarks [#remarks]

Spec 034 §C.

## Example [#example]

```csharp
var scheme = ctx.UseColorScheme();
var children = ctx.UseMemoCells(
    stocks,
    (item, i) => Cell(item, scheme),
    scheme);   // ← deps; framework invalidates on change
```

## Use from a class component [#use-from-a-class-component]

Class components can call the same hook directly. These overloads forward to the ones above:

```csharp
public static Element[] UseMemoCells<T>(this Component component, IReadOnlyList<T> items, Func<T, int, Element> builder, params object[] dependencies) where T : notnull
```

# UseMemoCellsByIndex
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseMemoCellsByIndex

Memoize cell construction when the data source already knows which indices changed. Skips the per-cell [`Object.Equals`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.object.equals) scan entirely; the builder runs only for indices in `changedIndices`. When the item count changes between renders the overload falls back to a full rebuild (`changedIndices` is treated as "rebuild everything") because the index space no longer matches the prior render. Callers whose lists grow or shrink frequently will get better incremental reuse from [`UseMemoCells`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseMemoCells) or [`UseMemoCellsByKey`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseMemoCellsByKey), both of which can short-circuit per-cell on value or key equality across length changes.

On the steady-state path (unchanged count) the returned array reuses the previous render's element instance for every index NOT named in `changedIndices`, and publishes a positional structural-skip hint (Spec 034 §C) keyed by reference on that array so the reconciler can update only the changed cells and skip the reference-equal remainder. The returned array is therefore the hook's retained memoized state AND the key of that hint: treat it as immutable and declare every change through a subsequent render's `changedIndices` (React-style immutability — see AGENTS.md "Never mutate"). Mutating an unchanged slot in place both corrupts the memo's view of the previous render and can cause the reconciler to skip the mutated cell.

```csharp
public static Element[] UseMemoCellsByIndex<T>(this RenderContext ctx, IReadOnlyList<T> items, IReadOnlyList<int> changedIndices, Func<T, int, Element> builder, params object[] dependencies) where T : notnull
```

An extension method on [`RenderContext`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/RenderContext), declared in `UseMemoCellsExtensions`.

**Learn more:** [Hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks), [Performance](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/performance)

## Parameters [#parameters]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `IReadOnlyList<T>` | Source items. |
| `changedIndices` | `IReadOnlyList<int>` | Indices whose item differs from the previous render. Negative indices and indices \>= `items.Count` throw [`ArgumentOutOfRangeException`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentoutofrangeexception). Duplicate indices are a caller-contract violation but are tolerated: they are de-duplicated before the named cells are rebuilt, so each cell is rebuilt exactly once and the structural-skip hint's theme tally stays exact. |
| `builder` | `Func<T, int, Element>` | Cell builder; same contract as [`UseMemoCells`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseMemoCells). |
| `dependencies` | `object[]` | Trailing-`params` deps. |

## Remarks [#remarks]

Spec 034 §C. A cell is "theme-sensitive" when it carries ThemeBindings or a ThemeRef-backed ResourceOverride; the hook tracks how many cells are theme-sensitive (carried forward incrementally) so the reconciler falls back to the full walk — which re-resolves themed brushes against the current effective theme — instead of structurally skipping such a range.

## Use from a class component [#use-from-a-class-component]

Class components can call the same hook directly. These overloads forward to the ones above:

```csharp
public static Element[] UseMemoCellsByIndex<T>(this Component component, IReadOnlyList<T> items, IReadOnlyList<int> changedIndices, Func<T, int, Element> builder, params object[] dependencies) where T : notnull
```

# UseNavigation
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseNavigation

Child mode: retrieves an ancestor's [`NavigationHandle<TRoute>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/navigation/NavigationHandle) from context. Throws if no ancestor provides one (i.e., no root `UseNavigation` with a `NavigationHost` exists above this component in the tree).

### `UseNavigation<TRoute>()` [#usenavigationtroute]

```csharp
public NavigationHandle<TRoute> UseNavigation<TRoute>() where TRoute : notnull
```

### `UseNavigation<TRoute>(TRoute)` [#usenavigationtroutetroute]

Root mode: creates a navigation stack with the given initial route. Returns a stable [`NavigationHandle<TRoute>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/navigation/NavigationHandle) across re-renders. Wire this handle to a `NavigationHost` in the DSL to render route content. The handle is automatically provided to descendants via context so child components can call `UseNavigation<TRoute>()` (parameterless) to access it.

```csharp
public NavigationHandle<TRoute> UseNavigation<TRoute>(TRoute initial) where TRoute : notnull
```

# UseNavigationLifecycle
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseNavigationLifecycle

- `onNavigatedTo` — fires after this page becomes active.
- `onNavigatingFrom` — fires before navigating away. Call `ctx.Cancel()` to block.
- `onNavigatedFrom` — fires after this page is no longer active.

Callbacks are always updated to the latest references on every render.


# UseOpenWindow
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseOpenWindow

Open or reuse a secondary window keyed by `key`. Renders that pass the same `key` share the same [`ReactorWindow`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorWindow); if the spec changes across renders the live window is updated via [`ReactorWindow.Update`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorWindow#update). The returned handle is identity-stable across renders so long as the key is stable.

```csharp
public ReactorWindow? UseOpenWindow(WindowKey key, WindowSpec spec, Func<Component> factory)
```

Declared on [`RenderContext`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/RenderContext).

**Learn more:** [Windows](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/windows), [Hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks)

## Parameters [#parameters]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | [`WindowKey`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowKey) |  |
| `spec` | [`WindowSpec`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec) |  |
| `factory` | `Func<Component>` |  |

## Remarks [#remarks]

Unmount semantics: when the calling component unmounts, the opened window stays open. Components that want the inverse behavior must close the window explicitly — e.g. by registering a `UseEffect` cleanup that calls [`ReactorWindow.Close`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorWindow#close) on the returned handle. (spec 036 §4.3 / §15.6)

**Note — asymmetry with [`UseTrayIcon`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseTrayIcon):** tray icons are component-scoped and close on unmount; opened windows are app-scoped and survive unmount. The asymmetry is deliberate (a window is normally expected to outlive the menu item that opened it, while a tray icon belongs to the component that declared it), so the two hooks behave inversely despite the matching naming.

Returns `null` when no UI dispatcher has been captured — happens in unit-test contexts where no `ReactorApp.Run` is in flight. In production this is unreachable.

## Use from a class component [#use-from-a-class-component]

Class components can call the same hook directly. These overloads forward to the ones above:

```csharp
protected ReactorWindow? UseOpenWindow(WindowKey key, WindowSpec spec, Func<Component> factory)
```

### `UsePersisted<T>(string, T)` [#usepersistedtstring-t]

Like UseState, but the value survives unmount/remount via an in-memory cache. On first mount, uses cached value if available, otherwise uses initialValue. Value is saved to cache on unmount.

```csharp
public (T Value, Action<T> Set) UsePersisted<T>(string key, T initialValue)
```

| Name | Type | Description |

**Remarks**

Spec 033 §2. The cache is currently process-wide ([`ApplicationPersistedScope.Default`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/persistence#default)) and bounded by an LRU policy. The two-arg form is flagged by `REACTOR_PERSIST_001` (`UsePersistedScopeAnalyzer`); new code should use the three-arg overload to make the intended scope explicit.

### `UsePersisted<T>(string, T, PersistedScope)` [#usepersistedtstring-t-persistedscope]

Persisted-state hook with explicit scope (spec 033 §2). Use [`PersistedScope.Window`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/persistence#values) for state that should be bounded by the host's lifetime; [`PersistedScope.Application`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/persistence#values) for process-wide state.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `initialValue` | `T` |  |
| `scope` | [`PersistedScope`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/persistence#persistedscope) |  |

**Remarks**

[`PersistedScope.Window`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/persistence#values) resolves to the [`ReactorWindow.PersistedScope`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorWindow#persistedscope) of the window whose host renders this component; content without an owning window (tray flyouts, `ReactorHostControl`, unit-test contexts) falls back to the process-wide scope. Two windows of the same component class therefore hold independent state under [`PersistedScope.Window`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/persistence#values). (spec 036 §3.4 / §4.4 — closes spec 033 §7.5.)

# UseReducedMotion
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseReducedMotion

Use this to skip entrance/exit animations, disable pan inertia, terminate force-graph simulations immediately, and keep only ≤ 150 ms opacity fades (WCAG 2.3.3).

The value is seeded during the first render and then tracked live through `UISettings.AnimationsEnabledChanged`. That event needs Windows 10 2004 (19041); on older builds the preference is re-read whenever a theme or palette change arrives instead, so it updates on the next such notification rather than immediately.

# UseState
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseState

When `threadSafe` is true, reads and writes are synchronized with a per-hook lock so concurrent setter calls from many threads serialize. When false (default), cross-thread setter calls are auto-marshaled onto the captured UI dispatcher — the write and the rerender both run on the UI thread, so background-thread setters from `Task.Run`, `PeriodicTimer`, or callbacks after `await … ConfigureAwait(false)` work correctly without any extra opt-in. Use `threadSafe`: `true` when you need many concurrent setters to apply in-place (i.e., without an intervening UI thread hop) or when the setter result must be visible to its caller before the next UI tick.

```csharp
public (T Value, Action<T> Set) UseState<T>(T initialValue, bool threadSafe = false)
```

Declared on [`RenderContext`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/RenderContext).

**Learn more:** [Hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks)

| Name | Type | Default | Description |

| `threadSafe` | `bool` | `false` |  |

# UseValidationContext
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseValidationContext

When the context is component-local (no ancestor provided one) it is published to the rendered subtree automatically, so `FormField`, the visualizers, and nested components find it without an explicit `.Provide(ValidationContexts.Current, ctx)`. Writing that call yourself still works and takes precedence.

The component also re-renders when the context changes, which is what makes `ctx.MarkAllTouched()` in a submit handler visible: it mutates the context without touching component state, so nothing else would schedule a repaint.

```csharp
public static ValidationContext UseValidationContext(this RenderContext ctx)
```

An extension method on [`RenderContext`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/RenderContext), declared in `ValidationContextHookExtensions`.

**Learn more:** [Forms and Input](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/forms), [Hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks)

## Use from a class component [#use-from-a-class-component]

Class components can call the same hook directly. These overloads forward to the ones above:

```csharp
public static ValidationContext UseValidationContext(this Component component)
```

# UseWindowDragMove
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseWindowDragMove

```csharp
public Action UseWindowDragMove()
```

Declared on [`RenderContext`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/RenderContext).

**Learn more:** [Windows](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/windows), [Advanced Windowing](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/windowing-advanced), [Hooks](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/hooks)

## Remarks [#remarks]

The loop is framework-managed (not OS-managed) because WinUI 3 routes pointer input through a child input-site HWND, so synthesizing `WM_NCLBUTTONDOWN` against the top-level HWND silently falls back to keyboard/cursor-track Move mode rather than mouse-driven click-drag. The polling approach is reliable but trades away OS Aero Snap during the drag. See spec 054 §5.3.

## Use from a class component [#use-from-a-class-component]

Class components can call the same hook directly. These overloads forward to the ones above:

```csharp
protected Action UseWindowDragMove()
```

| [`ReactorApplication`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApplication) | Application subclass that implements IXamlMetadataProvider so the native XAML schema context can resolve managed types from XBF theme resources. |
| [`ReactorHost`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHost) | Hosts a Reactor component tree inside a WinUI Window. |
| [`ReactorHostControl`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHostControl) | A fully self-contained WinUI ContentControl that hosts a Reactor component tree. |
| [`ReactorWindow`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorWindow) | Owns one OS top-level Window and one `ReactorHost`. |
| [`RenderStats`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/RenderStats) | Snapshot of render loop performance, updated every ~1 second by `ReactorHost`. |
| [`UIThreadOnlyAttribute`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/UIThreadOnlyAttribute) | Marks a method or property setter that must be invoked on the UI thread — the annotated method (or the property's setter) calls `ThreadAffinity.ThrowIfNotOnUIThread`, which throws `InvalidOperationException` when reached from a background thread once the UI dispatcher has been captured. (The guard is a no-op before the first window bootstraps, while `ReactorApp.UIDispatcher` is still null.) Property getters are not guarded, so the REACTOR_THREAD_001 analyzer flags writes to an annotated property, not reads. |
| [`WindowIcon`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon) | Abstraction over `AppWindow.SetIcon` and `AppWindow.SetIcon`. |
| [`WindowKey`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowKey) | Stable identity for a top-level surface within a process. |
| [`WindowSpec`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec) | Immutable (init-only) declarative description of a top-level Reactor window. |

Resolve [`LaunchActivation.Arguments`](#arguments) as a deep-link URI through the supplied [`DeepLinkMap<TRoute>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/navigation/DeepLinkMap). Returns `true` only when [`LaunchActivation.Arguments`](#arguments) is non-empty **and** the map matched a registered pattern. The shell-launch convention for Reactor is that jump-list / tray / thumbnail-toolbar entries carry deep-link URIs in their argument strings (see [`JumpListItem.ForUri`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/taskbar#foruri)); this helper plumbs that convention into the navigation system. (spec 036 §11.6)

## `LaunchKind` [#launchkind]

How the process was launched.

```csharp
public enum LaunchKind
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor`.

### Remarks [#remarks]

The OS shell presents jump-list entries, tray "Open" / double-click commands, and thumbnail-toolbar buttons as plain process re-launches — all three arrive at `OnLaunched` with the same shape (a non-empty argument string and no extended activation kind). Reactor cannot distinguish them from the WinUI surface, so all three roll up under [`LaunchKind.JumpList`](#values). Apps that need finer granularity should encode it in the argument URI itself (e.g. a path prefix or query parameter) and inspect [`LaunchActivation.Arguments`](#arguments).

### Values [#values]

| Name | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Normal` | `0` | Launched via the standard executable / shortcut entry point. |
| `JumpList` | `1` | Launched with a non-empty argument string from a shell re-launch — jump list, tray "Open", or thumbnail-toolbar button. The three sources are indistinguishable at the WinUI activation surface. |
| `Toast` | `2` | Launched in response to a toast click. |
| `Protocol` | `3` | Launched via a custom URI protocol handler. |
| `File` | `4` | Launched via file association. |

## `IWindowPersistenceStore` [#iwindowpersistencestore]

Storage adapter for [`WindowSpec.PersistenceId`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec#persistenceid). Implementations retain opaque per-id byte payloads; Reactor handles the serialization shape (`WINDOWPLACEMENT` + monitor-layout fingerprint). (spec 036 §8)

```csharp
public interface IWindowPersistenceStore
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting.Persistence`.

### Remarks [#remarks_2]

Implementations must be thread-safe for concurrent reads from arbitrary threads (Reactor reads on the UI thread today, but production callers may share a store across multiple processes / consoles). Writes happen on the UI thread on close.

Implementations must never throw into the caller. Read failures return `false` with the out-parameter `data` set to `null`; write failures are swallowed with a diagnostic log line. Reactor treats the store as best-effort — a corrupt or missing entry simply falls back to the spec's default placement.

### Methods [#methods_2]

## `JsonFileStore` [#jsonfilestore]

Default unpackaged-app persistence store. Writes a JSON document (one base64 string per persistence id) to `%LOCALAPPDATA%/<ProcessName>/reactor-windows.json`. Atomic via write-then-rename; bounded at [`JsonFileStore.MaxFileSizeBytes`](#maxfilesizebytes) (1 MB) on read to refuse pathological payloads. (spec 036 §8 / §0.5)

```csharp
public sealed class JsonFileStore : IWindowPersistenceStore
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting.Persistence`.

### Remarks [#remarks_3]

Read failures (missing file, malformed JSON, oversize) return `false` from [`JsonFileStore.TryRead`](#tryread_1) with no exception bubbling out — the spec calls for "warn-and-default" semantics on corruption.

Writes are best-effort and survive disk-full / permission denied without throwing.

**Concurrency.** Read-merge-write is serialized two ways: an in-process lock orders threads sharing an instance, and a named `CrossProcessWriteGuard` extends that ordering across separate instances and separate processes. Without the latter, two writers could each read the pre-merge document and the second rename would silently discard the first's entry — even when the two wrote *different* persistence ids. Each write stages through a temp file named for the writing process and thread, so a crash mid-write cannot leave a shared temp that another process renames over the real file.

Readers take no guard, but they do open with [`FileShare.Delete`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.io.fileshare.delete) in addition to [`FileShare.Read`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.io.fileshare.read), and the commit uses `File.Replace` rather than `File.Move(overwrite: true)`. Measured on Windows: `Move` cannot replace a destination any process still holds open — it fails even when that reader granted delete sharing — whereas `Replace` succeeds precisely when the reader does grant it. Both halves are required; with only one, a concurrent reader in a second app instance silently kills the write, because write failures are swallowed by contract. The reader then continues against the file it opened, seeing either the previous document or the next one, never a torn one.

## `UnpackagedAppDataStore` [#unpackagedappdatastore]

Unpackaged-app persistence store backed by the Windows App SDK's first-class app-data root, `Microsoft.Windows.Storage.ApplicationData.GetForUnpackaged()` (Windows App SDK ≥ 2.2.0). Persists to `<ApplicationData.LocalPath>/reactor-windows.json`. (spec 063 §4)

```csharp
public sealed class UnpackagedAppDataStore : IWindowPersistenceStore
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting.Persistence`.

### Remarks [#remarks_5]

**Opt-in.** Auto-detection still selects [`JsonFileStore`](#jsonfilestore) for unpackaged processes; assign an instance to [`ReactorApp.WindowPersistenceStore`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp#windowpersistencestore) before the first `OpenWindow` to use this one instead. The two stores key their data differently — this one by the `publisher`/`product` pair you supply, [`JsonFileStore`](#jsonfilestore) by the entry process's name — so switching does not migrate an existing app's saved layouts. (spec 063 §6, D2 / D3)

**Why the path surface and not `LocalSettings`.** This store uses `ApplicationData.LocalPath` and deliberately does **not** use the sibling `LocalSettings` key/value surface. On the runtime this repo pins, `GetForUnpackaged().LocalSettings` opens `HKCU\SOFTWARE\<publisher>\<product>` — a **roaming** hive — rather than the machine-local `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Classes\Local Settings\Software\…` it is contracted to use (WindowsAppSDK issue 6559, RuntimeCompatibilityChange `ApplicationData_GetForUnpackaged_LocalSettings`). Window placement is monitor-topology- and DPI-dependent, so roaming it between a user's machines restores windows onto monitors that do not exist there. `LocalPath` resolves under `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, which does not roam. (spec 063 §3.1)

That behaviour is a property of the installed 2.x Windows App Runtime, which services in place, rather than of the SDK version an app pins — so it can differ machine to machine for the same build. `LocalPath` has no such variance, which is a second reason this store is built on it. (spec 063 §3.2)

**Concurrency.** Safe to share across instances and processes: the underlying [`JsonFileStore`](#jsonfilestore) serializes read-merge-write with a named cross-process guard. That matters more for this store than for [`JsonFileStore`](#jsonfilestore)'s own default path, because this identity is deliberately *shared* — two differently-named executables from one publisher/product resolve the same file, where the process-name-keyed default would have given them separate ones. (spec 063 §5)

Read/write failures follow the [`IWindowPersistenceStore`](#iwindowpersistencestore) "warn-and-default" contract — they never throw into the caller. The *constructor* may throw, matching [`JsonFileStore`](#jsonfilestore): an invalid publisher/product is an authoring error, not a runtime condition.

### Constructors [#constructors_3]


| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `publisher` | `string` | Publisher segment of the app-data root. The SDK validates this and rejects path-traversal, rooted, and empty values with an [`ArgumentException`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentexception); Reactor does not sanitize it further. |
| `product` | `string` | Product segment of the app-data root. |

**Exceptions**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |

### `DefaultRenderErrorHandler` [#defaultrendererrorhandler]

App-wide replacement for the built-in render-error fallback, which shows the full exception text (type, message, stack trace). `null` (the default) keeps the built-in fallback. (issue #1291)

```csharp
public static RenderErrorHandler? DefaultRenderErrorHandler  // get, set
```

**Remarks**

Consulted at error time by every [`ReactorHost`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHost) and [`ReactorHostControl`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHostControl) that has no handler of its own — including windows opened after this is set, tray flyouts, and embedded host controls. A host overrides it with [`ReactorHost.RenderErrorHandler`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHost#rendererrorhandler), and a window with [`WindowSpec.RenderErrorHandler`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec#rendererrorhandler).

Covers every place Reactor catches a render-time exception outside an `ErrorBoundary`: the root render, child component renders, the reconcile pass, effect flushes, and effect cleanups during dispose. See [`RenderErrorHandler`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/render-errors#rendererrorhandler).

### `PrimaryWindow` [#primarywindow]


### `ShutdownPolicy` [#shutdownpolicy]

Process-shutdown policy. Defaults to [`ShutdownPolicy.OnPrimaryWindowClosed`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/window-options#values_2).

```csharp
public static ShutdownPolicy ShutdownPolicy  // get, set
```

**Remarks**

Settable from any thread and at any point in the process lifetime, and read back immediately. Reactor takes ownership of the event loop at startup (see [`ReactorApp.TakeOwnershipOfDispatcherLifetime`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp)), so this value is consulted when a decision is due rather than mirrored into platform state — there is no window in which the policy and the platform can disagree.

Two moments consult it. A surface close reaches [`ReactorApp.EvaluateShutdownPolicy`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp), which reads the value then, so a change made any time beforehand counts. Startup is the exception: [`ReactorApp.ExitIfStartupOpenedNoSurface`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp) runs the instant the launch path finishes, so a zero-surface startup is judged against whatever the policy holds at that instant. Set it before `Run`, or on the UI thread before the startup callback returns — a write posted from another thread during startup can land too late to be seen.

### `WindowPersistenceStore` [#windowpersistencestore]

Process-wide store backing [`WindowSpec.PersistenceId`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec#persistenceid). Defaults are picked lazily on first window open: packaged apps get [`PackagedSettingsStore`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/persistence#packagedsettingsstore); unpackaged apps get [`JsonFileStore`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/persistence#jsonfilestore). Setting this property after the first `OpenWindow` throws — windows that already loaded their placement from the previous store would get a half-populated state. (spec 036 §8)

```csharp

```

**Remarks**

Unpackaged apps can opt into [`UnpackagedAppDataStore`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/persistence#unpackagedappdatastore) by assigning one here before the first `OpenWindow`. It persists under the Windows App SDK's app-data root for an explicit publisher/product pair instead of the entry process's name, so saved layouts survive an executable rename. It is not the auto-detected default because the two stores key their data differently, so switching does not migrate existing saved layouts. (spec 063 §4)

## Methods [#methods]

### `Exit` [#exit]

Exit the process. UI-thread only. With `exitCode` set to its default (`0`), routes through [`Application.Exit`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.application.exit) so WinUI gets a clean unwind. With a non-zero exit code, calls [`Application.Exit`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.application.exit) first to release resources, then [`Environment.Exit`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.environment.exit) with the requested code so the parent process sees it (assigning [`Environment.ExitCode`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.environment.exitcode) would only take effect on a natural managed-entry-point return, which an app under `Application.Start` does not perform).

```csharp
public static void Exit(int exitCode = 0)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exitCode` | `int` | `0` |  |

### `RegisterAllBuiltIns` [#registerallbuiltins]

Registers every built-in Reactor control handler with the global [`ControlRegistry`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ControlRegistry) in one call.

```csharp
public static void RegisterAllBuiltIns()
```

**Remarks**

**When to call.** Call this once at process startup if your app constructs element records directly (the `new TextBlockElement(…) { … }` hot-loop idiom documented in `docs/guide/advanced.md` "Hot loops") rather than exclusively through factory methods. Factory methods already self-register on first call, so an app that only ever builds UI through the fluent/factory DSL does not need this.

**Trimming.** This method is the deliberate opt-out of spec-048's lazy-registration trim story: calling it roots the entire built-in catalog, so a NativeAOT/trimmed build that calls it keeps every built-in handler and WinUI control. Apps that want a minimal trimmed binary should *not* call this and instead let each factory register only the controls it uses — or register specific controls explicitly: [`ControlRegistry.Register`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ControlRegistry#register) for control-backed handlers, or [`ControlRegistry.RegisterDecorator`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/extensibility/ControlRegistry#registerdecorator) for decorator-backed elements (overlays, validation, composite wrappers). Because this is an ordinary method (not a `[ModuleInitializer]`), the trimmer removes it — and everything it names — when it is unreachable.

Registration is idempotent and process-wide; calling it more than once is a cheap no-op after the first call.

### `RegisterControlAssembly` [#registercontrolassembly]

See https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/142.

#### `Run<TRoot>(string, double?, double?, bool, WindowIcon?, Action<ReactorHost>?)` [#runtrootstring-double-double-bool-windowicon-actionreactorhost]

Launches the app. `width` / `height` are DIPs; leave them `null` (the default) to let the OS pick the initial window size, exactly as a plain XAML `Window` does. Enable the `Reactor.DevtoolsSupport` runtime host configuration switch in DEBUG builds to allow the `mur devtools` / `--devtools` surface: component switching via VS Code, MCP agent tools, and component listing.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `"Reactor App"` | Window caption text. |
| `width` | `double?` | `null` | Initial DIP width; `null` defers to the OS. |
| `height` | `double?` | `null` | Initial DIP height; `null` defers to the OS. |
| `fullScreen` | `bool` | `false` | Open with the full-screen presenter. |
| `icon` | [`WindowIcon?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon) | `null` | Optional window icon — the Win32 `HICON` Windows shows in the window's caption and the Alt-Tab switcher. Use an `.ico`: build it with [`WindowIcon.FromPath`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon#frompath) for a file beside the app, or [`WindowIcon.FromResource`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon#fromresource) for a packaged `ms-appx:///` asset. When omitted, Reactor falls back to `Assets\AppIcon.ico` and then to the executable's embedded icon. Distinct from `TitleBar(...).Icon(...)`, which sets the app mark drawn inside the window. Note that in a **packaged** app this does not change the taskbar button or Task Manager — the shell draws those from package identity and the manifest's `Square44x44Logo`; see [`WindowSpec.Icon`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec#icon). |
| `configure` | `Action<ReactorHost>?` | `null` | Optional callback invoked on the UI thread before the root mounts. |

### `TryRegisterControlAssembly` [#tryregistercontrolassembly]

Tolerant variant of [`ReactorApp.RegisterControlAssembly`](#registercontrolassemblyassembly): registers the assembly's XAML metadata provider if it has one, and silently does nothing (returning `false`) if it does not. A pure-code control library — e.g. code-only panels with no XAML files (and therefore no compiler-generated provider) — has nothing to register and needs nothing. Reflection discovery does not preserve the provider under trimming/NativeAOT. Generated wrappers use the instance overload when a suitable provider is visible at compile time, and this method only as a best-effort fallback.

```csharp
public static bool TryRegisterControlAssembly(Assembly assembly)
```

# ReactorAppContext
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorAppContext

The argument to [`ReactorApp.Run`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp#runactionreactorappcontext)'s startup callback. Carries the launch activation; all surface-management operations (open / find a window or tray icon, register events) go directly through the static [`ReactorApp`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp) API — call sites mix freely. (spec 036 §4.3)

```csharp
public sealed class ReactorAppContext
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor`.

**Learn more:** [Windows](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/windows)

## Remarks [#remarks]

Keep the context small on purpose: the static [`ReactorApp`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp) surface is the single source of truth for windows / tray icons / shutdown policy, and remains valid before `Run` enters this callback and after it returns. Doubling the API on the context just doubled the discovery cost without adding capability.

## Properties [#properties]

### `LaunchActivation` [#launchactivation]

How the process was launched. See [`LaunchActivation`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/launch#launchactivation).

```csharp
public LaunchActivation LaunchActivation  // get
```

### `OnUnhandledException` [#onunhandledexception]

**Remarks**


### `EffectiveRenderErrorHandler` [#effectiverendererrorhandler]

The handler this host would use right now: its own [`ReactorHost.RenderErrorHandler`](#rendererrorhandler), else [`ReactorApp.DefaultRenderErrorHandler`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp#defaultrendererrorhandler), else `null` (built-in fallback).

```csharp
public RenderErrorHandler? EffectiveRenderErrorHandler  // get
```

### `IsIdle` [#isidle]

True when the render loop has no pending or in-flight render and no re-render queued for the next tick. Mirrors the early-out predicate inside [`ReactorHost.WaitForIdleAsync`](#waitforidleasync); exposed so test harnesses can drive bounded-convergence wait loops without polling the same fields reflectively. The renderPending read uses Volatile.Read so off-thread callers see a stable snapshot of the Interlocked-managed field. A disposed host reports idle (nothing left to render, ever) to match the disposed-arm short-circuit in [`ReactorHost.WaitForIdleAsync`](#waitforidleasync); otherwise convergence loops would spin to their pass cap during/after host teardown and emit misleading non-idle diagnostics.

```csharp
public bool IsIdle  // get
```

### `OnRenderComplete` [#onrendercomplete]

Optional callback invoked after each render pass with phase timings (ms): treeBuildMs, reconcileMs, effectsMs. Used by perf harnesses to capture the breakdown of a Reactor render cycle.

```csharp
public Action<double, double, double>? OnRenderComplete  // get, set
```

### `WaitForIdleAsync` [#waitforidleasync]

Awaits until the render loop is idle (no pending or in-flight renders). Yields to the dispatcher at Low priority in a loop so that Normal-priority RenderLoop callbacks and Low-priority re-renders all complete before returning. Used by test harnesses to replace blind Task.Delay waits.

```csharp
public Task WaitForIdleAsync(int maxYields = 50)
```

# ReactorHostControl
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHostControl

Usage in XAML (`xmlns:reactor="using:Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting"`): \<reactor:ReactorHostControl ComponentType="local:StatsCard" /\> — or declare an empty host and mount it from code-behind — \<reactor:ReactorHostControl x:Name="reactorHost" /\>

Usage in code-behind: reactorHost.Mount(new MyComponent()); — or — reactorHost.Mount(ctx =\> VStack(TextBlock("Hello from Reactor!"))); — or — reactorHost.ComponentFactory = () =\> new MyComponent();

Features: - Thread-safe render batching (setState from any thread) - Low-priority re-enqueue so layout/paint/input aren't starved - Render performance stats (FPS, frame timing) - Automatic theme change detection and re-render - Connected animation flushing - Error boundary with fallback UI - Clean lifecycle via Loaded/Unloaded

```csharp
public sealed class ReactorHostControl : ContentControl, IDisposable
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting`. Inherits from [`ContentControl`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.controls.contentcontrol).

**Learn more:** [Coming from XAML](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/get-started/xaml-developers)

## Constructors [#constructors]

### `ReactorHostControl` [#reactorhostcontrol_1]

#### `ReactorHostControl()` [#reactorhostcontrol_2]

Creates an empty host. This is the constructor XAML uses (`<reactor:ReactorHostControl ... />`); set [`ReactorHostControl.ComponentType`](#componenttype) or [`ReactorHostControl.ComponentFactory`](#componentfactory), or call `Mount`, to give it a root.

```csharp
public ReactorHostControl()
```

#### `ReactorHostControl(Component?, ILogger?)` [#reactorhostcontrolcomponent-ilogger]

```csharp

```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `component` | [`Component?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/Component) | `null` |  |
| `logger` | `ILogger?` | `null` |  |

## Properties [#properties]

### `ComponentFactory` [#componentfactory]

Factory to create the root component. Set this or use Mount() for more control. If set, the component is created and mounted when the control is Loaded. Example: ComponentFactory = () =\> new MyComponent();

```csharp
public Func<Component>? ComponentFactory  // get, set
```

### `ComponentType` [#componenttype]

The root component's type, for declaring a host in XAML: `<reactor:ReactorHostControl ComponentType="local:StatsCard" />`. When the control is Loaded and nothing has been mounted, an instance is created and mounted, receiving [`ReactorHostControl.Props`](#props) like a [`ReactorHostControl.ComponentFactory`](#componentfactory) root. [`ReactorHostControl.ComponentFactory`](#componentfactory) wins when both are set.

```csharp
public Type? ComponentType  // get, set
```

**Remarks**

The instance is created through the app's XAML type information (`Application.Current` as [`IXamlMetadataProvider`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.markup.ixamlmetadataprovider)), not reflection: naming a type in markup makes the XAML compiler generate an activator for its public parameterless constructor, so this stays trim- and AOT-safe. A type that is only ever assigned from code has no such entry, and the host shows an error saying so in place of the root; set [`ReactorHostControl.ComponentFactory`](#componentfactory) there instead.

Read once, at Loaded, like [`ReactorHostControl.ComponentFactory`](#componentfactory); changing it after the root has mounted does not remount. Use [`ReactorHostControl.Mount`](#mountcomponent) to swap roots.

**Exceptions**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`ArgumentException`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentexception) | The type does not derive from [`Component`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/Component), or is abstract or an open generic. |

### `EffectiveRenderErrorHandler` [#effectiverendererrorhandler]

The handler this control would use right now: its own [`ReactorHostControl.RenderErrorHandler`](#rendererrorhandler), else [`ReactorApp.DefaultRenderErrorHandler`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp#defaultrendererrorhandler), else `null` (built-in fallback).

```csharp
public RenderErrorHandler? EffectiveRenderErrorHandler  // get
```

### `IsIdle` [#isidle]

True when the render loop has no pending or in-flight render and no re-render queued for the next tick — same contract as [`ReactorHost.IsIdle`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHost#isidle). Safe to read from any thread. A disposed control reports idle: it will never render again.


### `RenderErrorHandler` [#rendererrorhandler]

Replaces the built-in render-error fallback for this control only. `null` (the default) falls through to [`ReactorApp.DefaultRenderErrorHandler`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp#defaultrendererrorhandler) at error time. ### `Stats` [#stats]

Live render performance snapshot, updated every ~1 second. Always available (FPS, frame time). DEBUG builds include per-reconcile element counters.

```csharp

```

**Remarks**

Returned by value, unlike [`ReactorHost.Stats`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorHost#stats): the XAML compiler emits type metadata for every public property of a control declared in markup, and a `ref`-returning property becomes `typeof(RenderStats&)` in the app's generated `XamlTypeInfo.g.cs`, which does not compile. The copy is a few dozen bytes, read about once a second.

### `WaitForIdleAsync` [#waitforidleasync]

Completes once the render loop is idle (see [`ReactorHostControl.IsIdle`](#isidle)) — after a `setState`, a [`ReactorHostControl.Mount`](#mountcomponent), or any other change that schedules a render, await this before reading the realized tree back. ## Remarks [#remarks]

Public mutators ([`ReactorWindow.Activate`](#activate), [`ReactorWindow.Hide`](#hide), [`ReactorWindow.Show`](#show), [`ReactorWindow.Close`](#close), [`ReactorWindow.Update`](#update), [`ReactorWindow.SetSize`](#setsize), [`ReactorWindow.SetPosition`](#setposition), [`ReactorWindow.CenterOnScreen`](#centeronscreen), [`ReactorWindow.Mount`](#mountcomponent)) must be called on the UI thread captured by [`ReactorApp.UIDispatcher`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp#uidispatcher). Disposal is idempotent — a second [`ReactorWindow.Close`](#close) or [`ReactorWindow.Dispose`](#dispose) is a no-op, not an exception.

## Methods [#methods]

### `Activate` [#activate]

Show and focus the window. UI-thread only. No-op after disposal.

```csharp

```

### `BeginDragMove` [#begindragmove]

Begin a window drag/move loop as if the title bar had been clicked-and-dragged.

```csharp
public void BeginDragMove()
```

**Remarks**

Call from a left-button `PointerPressed` handler. We snapshot the initial cursor + window screen position, then run a dispatcher timer that polls `GetCursorPos` at ~60Hz and calls `AppWindow.Move` until `GetAsyncKeyState(VK_LBUTTON)` reports the button is no longer pressed. The timer-based approach is necessary because WinUI 3 routes pointer input through a child `InputSiteBridge` HWND, so synthesizing `WM_NCLBUTTONDOWN` (or `WM_SYSCOMMAND` + `SC_MOVE | HTCAPTION`) on the top-level HWND silently falls into keyboard/cursor-track move mode rather than mouse-driven click-drag (DefWindowProc doesn't see a recent WM_LBUTTONDOWN message). The polling approach is simple, reliable, and doesn't depend on the OS's non-client message routing. The trade-off vs. the OS modal drag loop is no Aero Snap during the drag — acceptable for the small floating windows (command palettes, tool palettes) that need IsMovableByBackground.


**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `y` | `double` |  |

**Remarks**

The DIP→physical conversion uses the **current window's** DPI. On mixed-DPI multi-monitor setups, moving across to a monitor with a different scale factor can land at a slightly different physical position than a caller expects, because Windows virtual-screen coordinates are physical pixels with no global DIP coordinate space. For predictable cross-monitor placement, prefer [`ReactorWindow.CenterOnScreen`](#centeronscreen) (which resolves against the destination [`DisplayArea`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.windowing.displayarea)) or move in two steps — `SetPosition` onto the target monitor, then adjust within it. (spec 036 §5.2)
