# Taskbar and jump lists
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/taskbar

**Learn more:** [Desktop integration](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/desktop-integration)

## `JumpList` [#jumplist]

Process-scoped jump list — the right-click flyout that appears on the app's taskbar button or Start tile. Driven through `Windows.UI.StartScreen.JumpList` for packaged apps and Win32 `ICustomDestinationList` for unpackaged. (spec 036 §11.3)

```csharp
public static class JumpList
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor`.

### Remarks [#remarks]

**Security note:** [`JumpListItem.Arguments`](#arguments) are command-line strings handed to a freshly launched process by the shell. Apps must parse them through `Reactor.Cli`'s arg parser before acting on them — a malformed shortcut, a forged jump-list entry left by another process, or a stale entry from an earlier installation will otherwise reach the new process unchecked. Reactor itself never auto-acts on these strings; [`ReactorAppContext.LaunchActivation`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorAppContext#launchactivation) surfaces them so the app can validate before dispatching.

Unpackaged apps must set [`JumpList.AppUserModelId`](#appusermodelid) before the first [`JumpList.UpdateAsync`](#updateasync) call — without it the shell has no stable identity to attach the jump list to.

### Properties [#properties]

#### `AppUserModelId` [#appusermodelid]

Application User Model ID used by the shell to associate the jump list with this process. Required for unpackaged apps; ignored when the process runs under an MSIX package (the package manifest supplies it).

```csharp
public static string? AppUserModelId  // get, set
```

#### `ShowFrequent` [#showfrequent]

Whether the OS-managed "Frequent" category is shown. The list contents are owned by the shell — apps can only toggle visibility.

```csharp
public static bool ShowFrequent  // get, set
```

#### `ShowRecent` [#showrecent]

Whether the OS-managed "Recent" category is shown. The list contents are owned by the shell — apps can only toggle visibility.

```csharp
public static bool ShowRecent  // get, set
```

### Methods [#methods]

#### `ClearAsync` [#clearasync]

Clear all user-defined jump-list entries. UI-thread only.

```csharp
public static Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> ClearAsync()
```

**Returns:** The removed arguments observed by the clear transaction.

**Remarks**

Like [`JumpList.UpdateAsync`](#updateasync), a successful clear consumes Windows' removal records. Retain the returned arguments before publishing destinations again.

#### `GetRemovedArgumentsAsync` [#getremovedargumentsasync]

Read the argument strings of entries removed by the user. UI-thread only.

```csharp
public static Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> GetRemovedArgumentsAsync()
```

**Remarks**

This does not update the list or acknowledge removals. Call before [`JumpList.UpdateAsync`](#updateasync) and remove matching entries from the app's destination tracking data. A successful update clears its removal records; also retain the arguments returned by that update to capture removals that occurred after this query. Only reintroduce a destination after new user activity. On unpackaged apps, only shell links targeting the current executable are returned; shell-item destinations are not created by this wrapper. Argument strings are compared ordinally, not as parsed command lines.

#### `UpdateAsync` [#updateasync]

Replace the jump list's user-defined entries. UI-thread only.

```csharp
public static Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> UpdateAsync(IEnumerable<JumpListItem> items)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `IEnumerable<JumpListItem>` |  |

**Returns:** All distinct removed arguments observed in this update transaction, including removals not present in `items`. The result reports observations, not commit success; logged shell HRESULT failures retain the existing non-throwing behavior.

**Remarks**

Clears any previously-set entries first; the OS-managed Recent and Frequent categories are unaffected (toggle them via [`JumpList.ShowRecent`](#showrecent) / [`JumpList.ShowFrequent`](#showfrequent)). COM activation and marshaling failures propagate as exceptions — callers may catch if fire-and-forget is desired. Individual HRESULT failures from shell APIs (e.g., `BeginList`, `CommitList`) are logged via `DiagnosticLog` but do not throw. Entries currently recorded as removed by Windows are omitted. A successful update clears the platform's removal records. Retain the returned arguments in the app's destination tracking data to avoid reintroducing them on the next update without new user activity.

## `JumpListItem` [#jumplistitem]

Shape of a single jump-list entry. (spec 036 §11.3 / §11.6)

```csharp
public sealed record JumpListItem(string Title, string Arguments, JumpListItemKind Kind = JumpListItemKind.Task, string? Description = null, WindowIcon? Icon = null, string? GroupCategory = null)
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor`.

### Constructors [#constructors]

#### `JumpListItem` [#jumplistitem_1]

Shape of a single jump-list entry. (spec 036 §11.3 / §11.6)

```csharp
public JumpListItem(string Title, string Arguments, JumpListItemKind Kind = JumpListItemKind.Task, string? Description = null, WindowIcon? Icon = null, string? GroupCategory = null)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Title` | `string` |  | User-visible label for the entry. |
| `Arguments` | `string` |  | Command-line arguments handed to a fresh process invocation when the user activates the entry. **Recommended convention:** use a deep-link URI string (the same shape [`DeepLinkMap.Resolve`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/navigation/DeepLinkMap#resolve) accepts) and resolve via [`LaunchActivation.TryResolve`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/launch#tryresolve) in the startup callback. The [`JumpListItem.ForUri`](#foruri) factory makes that convention discoverable. **Security:** these strings round-trip through the shell back into the next process launch. Apps must validate them via `Reactor.Cli`'s arg parser or [`DeepLinkMap<TRoute>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/navigation/DeepLinkMap) before acting on them — Reactor itself never auto-executes the arguments. |
| `Kind` | [`JumpListItemKind`](#jumplistitemkind) | `JumpListItemKind.Task` | Whether this is a regular task, a separator, or part of a custom group. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Optional tooltip / accessible description. |
| `Icon` | [`WindowIcon?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon) | `null` | Optional icon shown next to the title. The two jump-list paths want different things, and each silently skips what it cannot use: **Packaged** — `WindowIcon.FromResource` only. The WinRT `JumpListItem.Logo` takes a packaged `Uri`, so a filesystem path is skipped. **Unpackaged** — `WindowIcon.FromPath` only. The Win32 path hands the source to `IShellLink.SetIconLocation`, which wants a filesystem path, so an `ms-appx:` URI is skipped instead. See `JumpListComInterop.BuildShellLinkArray`. Binary sources (`WindowIcon.FromBytes` / `FromRgba`) work on neither: they have no URI and no path. Both arms skip them via the empty-`Source` guard. Ship a sidecar `.ico` or a packaged asset for jump-list entries. |
| `GroupCategory` | `string?` | `null` | Group label for [`JumpListItemKind.Custom`](#values) items. |

### Properties [#properties_1]

#### `Arguments` [#arguments]

Command-line arguments handed to a fresh process invocation when the user activates the entry. **Recommended convention:** use a deep-link URI string (the same shape [`DeepLinkMap.Resolve`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/navigation/DeepLinkMap#resolve) accepts) and resolve via [`LaunchActivation.TryResolve`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/launch#tryresolve) in the startup callback. The [`JumpListItem.ForUri`](#foruri) factory makes that convention discoverable.

**Security:** these strings round-trip through the shell back into the next process launch. Apps must validate them via `Reactor.Cli`'s arg parser or [`DeepLinkMap<TRoute>`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/navigation/DeepLinkMap) before acting on them — Reactor itself never auto-executes the arguments.

#### `Icon` [#icon]

Optional icon shown next to the title. The two jump-list paths want different things, and each silently skips what it cannot use:

- **Packaged** — `WindowIcon.FromResource` only. The WinRT `JumpListItem.Logo` takes a packaged `Uri`, so a filesystem path is skipped.
- **Unpackaged** — `WindowIcon.FromPath` only. The Win32 path hands the source to `IShellLink.SetIconLocation`, which wants a filesystem path, so an `ms-appx:` URI is skipped instead. See `JumpListComInterop.BuildShellLinkArray`.

Binary sources (`WindowIcon.FromBytes` / `FromRgba`) work on neither: they have no URI and no path. Both arms skip them via the empty-`Source` guard. Ship a sidecar `.ico` or a packaged asset for jump-list entries.

### Methods [#methods_1]

#### `EncodeArgument` [#encodeargument]

Encode a single argv value per `CommandLineToArgvW` rules. Public so callers building command lines piecewise can reuse the same escaper Reactor uses internally for jump-list entries.

```csharp
public static string EncodeArgument(string argument)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `argument` | `string` |  |

#### `EncodeArguments` [#encodearguments]

Encode a sequence of argv-style argument values as a single command-line string compatible with `CommandLineToArgvW`. Whitespace, quotes, and trailing-backslash sequences are quoted/escaped per the documented MSVC parsing rules so that round-tripping the result through the OS command-line parser yields back the original sequence.

```csharp
public static string EncodeArguments(IEnumerable<string> arguments)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `arguments` | `IEnumerable<string>` |  |

**Remarks**

Useful directly for jump-list entries (see [`JumpListItem.ForCommandLine`](#forcommandline)), thumbnail-toolbar buttons, and any other surface where an argument string is handed to the shell for re-launch. Reactor's own CLI parser (`Reactor.Cli`) consumes `CommandLineToArgvW`-encoded input, so encoded strings round-trip without further escaping.

#### `ForCommandLine` [#forcommandline]

Build a jump-list entry whose [`JumpListItem.Arguments`](#arguments) string is tokenized: each element of `arguments` becomes one argv slot when the launched process parses its command line via `CommandLineToArgvW`. Values containing whitespace, quotes, or backslashes are escaped so a malicious value can't break out into a neighbouring argument.

Use this factory whenever the arguments include data that did not originate from a string literal in your source code (deep-link payloads, file paths, user-typed identifiers). The raw-string [`JumpListItem`](#jumplistitem_1) constructor and [`JumpListItem.ForUri`](#foruri) are still appropriate when the caller has already produced a well-formed deep-link URI. (spec 036 §11.3 security checklist)

```csharp
public static JumpListItem ForCommandLine(string title, IEnumerable<string> arguments, string? description = null, WindowIcon? icon = null, string? groupCategory = null)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` |  |  |
| `arguments` | `IEnumerable<string>` |  |  |
| `description` | `string?` | `null` |  |
| `icon` | [`WindowIcon?`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon) | `null` |  |
| `groupCategory` | `string?` | `null` |  |

## `TaskbarOverlay` [#taskbaroverlay]

Taskbar overlay icon ("badge") for a top-level window. Backs [`ReactorWindow.Overlay`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorWindow#overlay). (spec 036 §11.2)

```csharp
public sealed class TaskbarOverlay
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor`.

### Remarks [#remarks_1]

Setting [`TaskbarOverlay.Icon`](#icon_1) to null clears the overlay. The icon should be 16×16 logical pixels — larger images are downscaled by the shell with quality loss; we emit a one-shot `Debug.WriteLine` when a [`WindowIcon.FromPath`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon#frompath) source can't be loaded as an HICON.

The overlay needs a raw `HICON`, so it accepts a filesystem path or in-memory data ([`WindowIcon.FromBytes`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon#frombytes) / [`WindowIcon.FromRgba`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon#fromrgba)) and skips [`WindowIcon.FromResource`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon#fromresource). A procedurally-drawn badge is a natural fit for [`WindowIcon.FromRgba`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon#fromrgba), which needs no file on disk.

Accessibility: [`TaskbarOverlay.AccessibleDescription`](#accessibledescription) flows through the `pszDescription` parameter of `ITaskbarList3.SetOverlayIcon` — without it the overlay is invisible to assistive tech (spec §0.6).

### Properties [#properties_3]

#### `AccessibleDescription` [#accessibledescription]

Accessible description handed to the shell's `SetOverlayIcon(pszDescription)` — required for assistive tech to announce the overlay. (spec 036 §0.6)

```csharp
public string? AccessibleDescription  // get, set
```

#### `Icon` [#icon_1]

The current overlay icon. Null clears.

```csharp
public WindowIcon? Icon  // get, set
```

# Tray icon
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/tray-icon

**Learn more:** [Windows](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/windows), [Desktop integration](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/desktop-integration)

## `ReactorTrayIcon` [#reactortrayicon]

Top-level system-tray icon — a peer of [`ReactorWindow`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorWindow). Created via [`ReactorApp.OpenTrayIcon`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp#opentrayicon). Provides the icon bitmap, tooltip, and click events; reconciles a Reactor [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) as its flyout via [`ReactorTrayIcon.ShowFlyout`](#showflyout). (spec 036 §11.4)

```csharp
public sealed class ReactorTrayIcon : IDisposable
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor`.

### Remarks [#remarks]

Public mutators must run on the UI thread captured by [`ReactorApp.UIDispatcher`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp#uidispatcher). Disposal is idempotent — a second [`ReactorTrayIcon.Close`](#close) / [`ReactorTrayIcon.Dispose`](#dispose) call is a no-op.

The flyout-content reconciliation runs in a [`RenderContext`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/components/RenderContext) without an owning [`ReactorWindow`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorWindow); hooks like [`UseWindow`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseWindow) return their documented fallback values (spec 036 §7.1).

### Events [#events]

#### `Click` [#click]

Fires on the UI thread when the user left-clicks the icon.

**Security:** see [`ReactorTrayIcon.DoubleClick`](#doubleclick) remarks. Treat click handlers as triggers for reversible UI actions only.

```csharp
public event EventHandler? Click
```

#### `DoubleClick` [#doubleclick]

Fires on the UI thread when the user double-clicks the icon.

**Security — clicks are not authenticated:** the tray click callback arrives as a Win32 `WM_APP+1` message that any process at the same Integrity Level can synthesise via `PostMessage` to the hidden tray window. Use click handlers for reversible UI actions only (open a window, toggle state, show a flyout); gate any privileged or destructive operation behind a deliberate in-app confirmation step. (W-6, threat model 2026-05-08.)

```csharp
public event EventHandler? DoubleClick
```

# UIThreadOnlyAttribute
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/UIThreadOnlyAttribute

Marks a method or property setter that must be invoked on the UI thread — the annotated method (or the property's setter) calls `ThreadAffinity.ThrowIfNotOnUIThread`, which throws [`InvalidOperationException`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.invalidoperationexception) when reached from a background thread once the UI dispatcher has been captured. (The guard is a no-op before the first window bootstraps, while [`ReactorApp.UIDispatcher`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp#uidispatcher) is still null.) Property getters are not guarded, so the REACTOR_THREAD_001 analyzer flags writes to an annotated property, not reads.

```csharp
public sealed class UIThreadOnlyAttribute : Attribute
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting`. Inherits from [`Attribute`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.attribute).

**Learn more:** [Coming from XAML](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/get-started/xaml-developers)

## Remarks [#remarks]

The marker exists for the `REACTOR_THREAD_001` analyzer (`UIThreadAffinityAnalyzer`). In a consumer compilation the Reactor framework is a metadata-only reference, so the analyzer cannot inspect a callee's body for the runtime guard — `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty and IL is not available. A metadata-visible attribute is the committed mechanism the analyzer keys off, so this type must be `public`.

This is a plain marker attribute with no members and no reflection surface, so it is trim- and AOT-safe. Keep it in sync with the members that call `ThreadAffinity.ThrowIfNotOnUIThread`; the analyzer reads the attribute rather than a hard-coded member list.

## Constructors [#constructors]

### `UIThreadOnlyAttribute` [#uithreadonlyattribute_1]

```csharp
public UIThreadOnlyAttribute()
```

# Window options
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/window-options

## `AspectRatioBasis` [#aspectratiobasis]

Whether [`WindowSpec.AspectRatio`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec#aspectratio) applies to the outer window rectangle (caption + borders included) or to the client (content) area.

```csharp
public enum AspectRatioBasis
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor`.

### Remarks [#remarks]

[`AspectRatioBasis.Window`](#values) is the simpler / cheaper mode and matches the raw shape of the OS `WM_SIZING` contract — the framework just enforces a ratio on the rect the OS hands us.

[`AspectRatioBasis.Client`](#values) is what most media/game/canvas apps want (a 1:1 client area for a square video player, a 16:9 client area for a game viewport). The framework computes the chrome inset via `AdjustWindowRectExForDpi` at the current window style + DPI, so the ratio stays accurate across DPI changes and across [`WindowStyle`](#windowstyle) flips. Has no effect when [`WindowSpec.AspectRatio`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec#aspectratio) is null.

### Values [#values]

| Name | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Window` | `0` | Ratio applies to the outer window rect, including caption and borders. Default. |
| `Client` | `1` | Ratio applies to the client area. The framework auto-accounts for chrome. |

# WindowIcon
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon

Abstraction over [`AppWindow.SetIcon`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.windowing.appwindow.seticon) and [`AppWindow.SetIcon`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.windowing.appwindow.seticon). Pass to [`WindowSpec.Icon`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec#icon), to a tray icon, or to a taskbar overlay. (spec 036 §4.1)

```csharp
public sealed class WindowIcon
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor`.

**Learn more:** [Windows](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/windows), [Advanced Windowing](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/windowing-advanced)

## Remarks [#remarks]

Three source kinds are supported: a filesystem path ([`WindowIcon.FromPath`](#frompath)) for `.ico` resources alongside an unpackaged app, an `ms-appx:///`-style packaged-app resource URI ([`WindowIcon.FromResource`](#fromresource)), and icon data held in memory ([`WindowIcon.FromBytes`](#frombytes) / [`WindowIcon.FromRgba`](#fromrgba)). Empty strings and empty buffers are rejected at construction so a malformed icon never reaches the WinUI APIs.

Consumers differ in what they can accept, because most of them need a raw Win32 `HICON` while a couple need a [`Uri`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.uri):

- [`WindowSpec.Icon`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec#icon) — [`WindowIcon.FromPath`](#frompath) and [`WindowIcon.FromResource`](#fromresource). An `ms-appx:` source is mapped to a file beside the app before it reaches `AppWindow.SetIcon`, which needs a filesystem path: handed the URI itself inside a packaged app it silently applies a default icon. A binary source is **not** accepted here — see [`WindowIcon.FromBytes`](#frombytes).
- Tray icons, taskbar overlays, and thumbnail-toolbar buttons — [`WindowIcon.FromPath`](#frompath) and the binary factories. They need an `HICON`, which comes either from `LoadImageW` on a file or from `CreateIconFromResourceEx` on in-memory data; neither can read a packaged resource URI, so [`WindowIcon.FromResource`](#fromresource) is skipped with a diagnostic.
- Jump lists — [`WindowIcon.FromResource`](#fromresource) on the packaged path (the WinRT API takes the URI directly) and [`WindowIcon.FromPath`](#frompath) on the unpackaged one. Every other kind is silently skipped.

Instances are immutable and safe to share: a binary source copies the caller's buffer, so a later write to that array cannot change what the shell renders.

## Properties [#properties]

### `IsBinary` [#isbinary]

True when constructed via [`WindowIcon.FromBytes`](#frombytes) or [`WindowIcon.FromRgba`](#fromrgba).

```csharp
public bool IsBinary  // get
```

### `IsResource` [#isresource]

True when constructed via [`WindowIcon.FromResource`](#fromresource).


Which factory produced this icon.

```csharp

```

### `Source` [#source]

The path or resource URI this icon was constructed from, or [`String.Empty`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.string.empty) for a [`WindowIconKind.Binary`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/window-options#values_5) icon, which has no addressable source. Test [`WindowIcon.Kind`](#kind) rather than inferring it from here.

```csharp
public string Source  // get
```

## Methods [#methods]

### `FromBytes` [#frombytes]

Create an icon from encoded icon data held in memory — an `.ico` container, a PNG, or a bare `RT_ICON` DIB blob — so an app whose icon lives in an embedded resource, a database, or a download does not have to write a temporary file first. (issue #1185)

```csharp
public static WindowIcon FromBytes(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` | The encoded bytes. Copied, so the caller may reuse or overwrite its buffer. |

**Remarks**

Consumed by the tray icon, the taskbar overlay, and thumbnail-toolbar buttons, which need a raw `HICON` and get one via `CreateIconFromResourceEx`. A multi-frame `.ico` is honoured: the frame nearest the size the surface asks for is selected, exactly as `LoadImageW` would have done from a file.

**Not accepted by [`WindowSpec.Icon`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec#icon).** Putting a binary icon on a window means owning the `HICON` for the window's lifetime, which `AppWindow.SetIcon(IconId)` does not do for you. A binary icon declared there is reported as not applied, so the window falls back to `Assets\AppIcon.ico` or its PE icon rather than showing nothing. Jump lists and the `TitleBar` icon default skip it for the same reason they skip a PE icon: both need a [`Uri`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.uri).

An unrecognised signature is logged via `System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine` rather than throwing, mirroring [`WindowIcon.FromPath`](#frompath)'s treatment of an unrecognised extension — the loader is the authority on what it accepts, and refusing data it would have loaded is worse than letting it report the failure.

The bytes are held for this instance's lifetime. That is the point of the API, but it is worth knowing when a long-lived spec holds a large multi-resolution `.ico`.

### `FromPath` [#frompath]

Create an icon from a filesystem path (typically a `.ico`) for an unpackaged app. Throws on null/empty input.

An unrecognised extension or missing file is logged via `System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine` so misconfiguration is diagnosable, but no exception is raised — apps that deploy assets asynchronously, or icons that exist as a sidecar to a relocated executable, still construct successfully and surface the underlying load failure on [`WindowIcon.Apply`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon). (W-4 hardening.)

```csharp
public static WindowIcon FromPath(string path)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` |  |

### `FromResource` [#fromresource]

Create an icon from a packaged-app resource URI (e.g. `ms-appx:///Assets/AppIcon.ico`). Throws on null/empty input.

The URI is mapped to a file beside the app (the package install root when packaged) before it reaches `AppWindow.SetIcon`, which requires a filesystem path. Manifest visual assets (`Square44x44Logo` and friends) are named by resource identifier rather than filename and are not addressable this way.

```csharp
public static WindowIcon FromResource(string uri)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uri` | `string` |  |

### `FromRgba` [#fromrgba]

Create an icon from a raw straight-alpha RGBA8 pixel buffer — the shape Rust's tray crates expose as `Icon::from_rgba`. (issue #1185)

```csharp
public static WindowIcon FromRgba(ReadOnlySpan<byte> pixels, int width, int height)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pixels` | `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` | Exactly `width * height * 4` bytes, top-down, one pixel as R, G, B, A. Copied (as an assembled icon image), so the caller may reuse or overwrite its buffer. |
| `width` | `int` | Icon width in pixels, between 1 and 4096. |
| `height` | `int` | Icon height in pixels, between 1 and 4096. |

**Remarks**

The buffer is converted once, at construction, into the 32-bpp icon-resource layout the platform loader wants (bottom-up BGRA plus an AND mask). See [`WindowIcon.FromBytes`](#frombytes) for which surfaces consume a binary icon.

**Exceptions**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`ArgumentOutOfRangeException`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentoutofrangeexception) | `width` or `height` is outside 1–4096. |
| [`ArgumentException`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentexception) | `pixels` is not exactly `width * height * 4` bytes. |

**Learn more:** [Windows](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/windows), [Advanced Windowing](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/windowing-advanced)

## Remarks [#remarks]

Identity is by ordinal name within the current process. Implicit conversion from `string` exists so call sites can pass a literal directly:

.

## Constructors [#constructors]

### `WindowKey` [#windowkey_1]

Stable identity for a top-level surface within a process. Used by [`ReactorApp.FindWindow`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp#findwindow), [`WindowSpec.Key`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec#key), and the `UseOpenWindow` hook to dedupe re-renders that should reuse a window rather than open a new one. (spec 036 §4.4)

```csharp
public WindowKey(string Name)
```

# WindowSpec
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowSpec

Immutable (init-only) declarative description of a top-level Reactor window. Hand to [`ReactorApp.OpenWindow`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorApp#openwindowwindowspec-funccomponent-actionreactorhost) to open a window; hand to [`ReactorWindow.Update`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorWindow#update) to diff against the current spec and apply only changed fields.

```csharp
public sealed record WindowSpec
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor`.

**Learn more:** [Windows](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/windows), [Advanced Windowing](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/windowing-advanced)

## Remarks [#remarks]

All sizes and positions are **DIPs** (device-independent pixels) — no Win32 / no `SizeInt32` in user code. (spec 036 §4.1)

[`WindowSpec.Validate`](#validate) enforces the cross-field invariants and is called by the hosting layer (the [`ReactorWindow`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorWindow) constructor and [`ReactorWindow.Update`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorWindow#update)) before the spec is used; tests may call it directly. It requires `Width`/`Height` to be positive *when set* (`null` defers the initial extent to the OS), max ≥ min when both are set, and [`WindowSpec.ManualPosition`](#manualposition) iff [`WindowSpec.StartPosition`](#startposition) is [`WindowStartPosition.Manual`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/window-options#values_9).


### `Icon` [#icon]

Optional window icon — the Win32 `HICON` Windows shows in the window's caption and the Alt-Tab switcher. Build it with [`WindowIcon.FromPath`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon#frompath) for a file beside the app or [`WindowIcon.FromResource`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon#fromresource) for a packaged `ms-appx:///` asset.

```csharp
public WindowIcon? Icon  // get, init
```

**Remarks**

Distinct from `TitleBar(...).Icon(...)`, which draws an app mark inside the window's client area. A window may set both, and they may legitimately differ. When this is `null`, Reactor falls back to `Assets\AppIcon.ico` beside the app and then to the executable's embedded icon.

In an **unpackaged** app this also drives the taskbar button and Task Manager, because there is no package identity to take precedence. In a **packaged** app it does not: the shell resolves those two surfaces through package identity and the manifest's `Square44x44Logo`, never looking at the window handle. A packaged app that wants a consistent icon everywhere must ship a matching manifest logo in addition to setting this.

A binary source ([`WindowIcon.FromBytes`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon#frombytes) / [`WindowIcon.FromRgba`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/WindowIcon#fromrgba)) is **not** accepted here — this surface needs a filesystem path, because that is what `AppWindow.SetIcon` takes. Declaring one falls through to the same convention/PE fallback as declaring no icon at all, so the window is never left barer than it would otherwise have been. Binary sources are for the tray icon, the taskbar overlay, and thumbnail-toolbar buttons.

### `IgnorePointerInput` [#ignorepointerinput]

Apply the Win32 `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT` extended style so mouse events pass THROUGH the window to whatever's underneath. Default false. Used by spec 045 §2.6 tear-off so the drag preview doesn't block clicks on drop-target overlays below it.

```csharp
public bool IgnorePointerInput  // get, init
```

**Remarks**

[`WindowSpec.Validate`](#validate) throws when this field is true with `Opacity == 1.0`; the runtime mutator `ReactorWindow.SetIgnorePointerInput(true)` also throws if the live window is not layered.

### `ManualPosition` [#manualposition]

**Remarks**

Coordinates that target a different monitor on a mixed-DPI desktop may land at a slightly different physical position because Windows virtual-screen coordinates are physical pixels with no global DIP coordinate space. For absolute placement on a specific non-primary monitor, prefer [`WindowStartPosition.CenterOnOwner`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/window-options#values_9) (with an owner already on that monitor) or call [`ReactorWindow.SetPosition`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/ReactorWindow#setposition) after the window opens.

### `TitleBarHeight` [#titlebarheight]

System caption height. `null` (the default) leaves the platform default alone; a mounted `TitleBar(...)` element's `HeightOption` then applies instead, if it declares one.

```csharp
public WindowTitleBarHeight? TitleBarHeight  // get, init
```

**Remarks**

Requires a content-extended window — the native `AppWindow.TitleBar.PreferredHeightOption` setter throws `ERROR_INVALID_STATE` otherwise. Reactor applies the value only once the window is content-extended (including the deferred flip a `TitleBar(...)` element performs at mount) and warns instead of throwing when the window never extends.

This sizes the **system caption** only. A mounted WinUI `TitleBar` control does not follow it, which is why `TitleBar(...).Tall()` — which sizes both — is the preferred spelling when the window renders a `TitleBar(...)` element. (issue #917)

### `TitleBarTheme` [#titlebartheme]

Theme of the system caption buttons (`AppWindow.TitleBar.PreferredTheme`). `null` (the default) leaves the platform default alone; a mounted `TitleBar(...)` element's `PreferredTheme` then applies instead, if it declares one. (issue #1297)

```csharp
public WindowTitleBarTheme? TitleBarTheme  // get, init
```

**Remarks**

WinUI does not derive the caption theme from the content's `RequestedTheme`; an app that themes its content opposite to the system sets this to match. Removing a declaration restores the value the caption had before Reactor first applied one; a value set imperatively and never declared is left alone.

### `Width` [#width]

Must be positive when set. `null` (the default) leaves the initial width to the OS — Reactor does not override that axis, so the window keeps the width Windows picks for a new top-level window (the same behavior a plain XAML `Window` gets). When both axes are `null` no `AppWindow.Resize` call is made at all.


# XAML interop
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hosting/xaml-interop

**Learn more:** [Coming from XAML](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/get-started/xaml-developers)

## `PageHelper` [#pagehelper]

Helper methods for hosting Reactor components inside XAML Pages that participate in Frame-based navigation.

IMPORTANT: WinUI's Frame.Navigate requires pages to have XAML metadata (IXamlType registration). Code-only Page subclasses — including generic base classes like ReactorPage\<T\> — crash with a null access violation in ActivationAPI::ActivateInstance because GetXamlTypeNoRef() returns null.

The correct pattern for Reactor pages in Frame navigation:

1\. Create a minimal .xaml file for the page: \<Page x:Class="MyApp.Pages.ButtonPage" ... /\>

2\. In the code-behind, use PageHelper to mount the component:

public sealed partial class ButtonPage: Page \{ private ReactorHostControl? _host;

public ButtonPage() \{ InitializeComponent(); \}

protected override void OnNavigatedTo(NavigationEventArgs e) \{ base.OnNavigatedTo(e); _host = PageHelper.Mount\<MyComponent\>(this, e); \}

protected override void OnNavigatedFrom(NavigationEventArgs e) \{ base.OnNavigatedFrom(e); PageHelper.Unmount(ref _host); \} \}

```csharp
public static class PageHelper
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting`.

### `DebounceMs` [#debouncems]

Leading-edge debounce window, in milliseconds. `0` (the default) disables debouncing and preserves the un-debounced behavior exactly.

When \> 0 and the command is processed through [`UseCommand`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseCommand#usecommandcommand), the first fire is accepted and any subsequent fire within `DebounceMs` of it is dropped (a no-op). For the duration of the window [`Command.IsDebouncing`](#isdebouncing) is true, so [`Command.IsEnabled`](#isenabled) reports false and the bound control visibly disables, then re-enables when the window elapses. This is the framework-owned replacement for the "wrap a sync action in `Task.Delay` to absorb double-clicks" pattern (issue #136).

For async commands, [`Command.IsExecuting`](#isexecuting) already tracks the lambda's lifetime; `DebounceMs` is the time-based generalization that keeps the disabled window open past the lambda's return (the effective disabled window is the longer of the two).

**DebounceMs only works through [`UseCommand`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseCommand#usecommandcommand).** The debounce state (last-fire window + re-enable timer) lives in the `UseCommand` hook's backing store, which is the only place that persists across renders (the [`Command`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command) record itself is reconstructed every render). A raw `new Command { DebounceMs = … }` bound directly to a control — without being passed through `UseCommand` — has nowhere to persist that state and is therefore **inert: it does NOT debounce**. Always wrap a debounced command with `UseCommand`:

```csharp
var run = UseCommand(new Command { Label = "Run", Execute = Run, DebounceMs = 1500 });
```

```csharp
public int DebounceMs  // get, init
```

### `FromCommand` [#fromcommand]

#### `FromCommand<T>(ICommand, string, IconData?, string?, KeyboardAcceleratorData?)` [#fromcommandticommand-string-icondata-string-keyboardacceleratordata]

Creates a parameterized Command from an ICommand. The ICommand receives the Command's parameter when Execute is called. CanExecute defaults to true because Command\<T\>.CanExecute is a static bool and the parameter is not known at creation time. To evaluate CanExecute dynamically, call this within a component's Render method with a known parameter and pass command.CanExecute(parameter) explicitly.

```csharp
public static Command<T> FromCommand<T>(ICommand command, string label, IconData? icon = null, string? description = null, KeyboardAcceleratorData? accelerator = null)
```

## `DragData` [#dragdata]

The drag payload. Supports typed-payload round-trip (Phase 6a), standard WinUI formats (text / URI / HTML / RTF / files / bitmap — Phase 6b eager + lazy), and custom format identifiers. Same-process transfers stash the in-memory [`DragData`](#dragdata) via a per-drag GUID in `DataPackage.Properties`; eager standard formats are also written directly to the [`DataPackage`](https://learn.microsoft.com/uwp/api/windows.applicationmodel.datatransfer.datapackage) so cross-process drops (Notepad, Word, File Explorer, …) can consume them natively. Lazy providers are adapted via [`DataPackage.SetDataProvider`](https://learn.microsoft.com/uwp/api/windows.applicationmodel.datatransfer.datapackage.setdataprovider) and invoked on demand.

```csharp
public sealed class DragData
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Input`.

#### `TryGetSafeLocalFiles` [#trygetsafelocalfiles]

Filters dropped files to local-only paths, removing UNC, DOS-device, reparse, and shell-virtual entries that the source process picked. Apps that open/parse/render dropped files should prefer this over [`DragData.TryGetFiles`](#trygetfiles); UNC paths trigger NTLM authentication on stat/open, reparse points can escape the directory the user thought they shared, and Internet-zone files lose their MOTW warning if the app reads bytes without consulting `Zone.Identifier`. TASK-069.

```csharp
public bool TryGetSafeLocalFiles(out IReadOnlyList<IStorageItem> value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `IReadOnlyList<IStorageItem>` |  |

## `DragOperations` [#dragoperations]

Drag-and-drop operation flags. Source declares what it allows via `ElementExtensions.OnDragStart`; target negotiates the final operation by setting [`DragTargetArgs.AcceptedOperation`](#acceptedoperation).

```csharp
public enum DragOperations
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Input`.

### Values [#values]

| Name | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `None` | `0` | No operation — used to reject a drop. |
| `Copy` | `1` | Copy the payload, leaving the source intact. |
| `Move` | `2` | Move the payload — source should remove the item on successful drop. |
| `Link` | `4` | Create a link/reference to the payload. |
| `All` | `7` | Any of Copy, Move, or Link. |

# Element refs
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/element-refs

**Learn more:** [Input and gestures](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/input-and-gestures)

## `ElementRef` [#elementref]

Opaque ref to a mounted [`FrameworkElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.frameworkelement). Populated by the reconciler when the element is mounted; consumed by [`FocusManager.Focus`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/FocusManager#focus) and friends. Null until the target element is mounted. Survives re-renders — the same [`ElementRef`](#elementref) instance is reused by the reconciler while the underlying control is recycled from the element pool.

```csharp
public sealed class ElementRef
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Input`.

### Constructors [#constructors]

#### `ElementRef` [#elementref_1]

```csharp
public ElementRef()
```

### Properties [#properties]

#### `Current` [#current]

The currently-mounted control, or null if the referenced element has not mounted yet (or has been unmounted without a replacement).

```csharp
public FrameworkElement? Current  // get
```

## `ElementRef<T>` [#elementreft]

Strongly-typed wrapper around [`ElementRef`](#elementref) that surfaces the mounted element as `T` instead of the base [`FrameworkElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.frameworkelement), removing the `(Button)ref.Current` cast at every consumer.

```csharp
public sealed class ElementRef<T> where T : FrameworkElement
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Input`.

### Remarks [#remarks]

Spec 033 §3. Construct via `ctx.UseElementRef<T>()` and bind to an element via `.Ref(typedRef)`. The typed wrapper is reflection-free and AOT-safe — `T` is used only for the cast on read.

**Threading:** the reconciler populates the underlying ref on the UI thread during element mount/update. Reading [`ElementRef.Current`](#current_1) from a non-UI thread is permitted but the value may be stale by the time the caller dereferences it.

**Accessibility:** programmatic focus via `Current?.Focus()` moves the keyboard focus and triggers WinUI's standard focus-changed UIA event, but it does *not* by itself produce a screen-reader announcement of surrounding content. When the focus change should be accompanied by an announcement (e.g. "saved", "validation error") use [`UseAnnounce`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/hooks/UseAnnounce) in addition to the focus call. Modifiers applied to the element (notably `.AutomationName(...)`) are preserved across re-renders, so the typed ref does not affect the UIA tree shape.

### Type parameters [#type-parameters]

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `T` | The concrete WinUI control type the ref will be attached to. Constrained to [`FrameworkElement`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.frameworkelement) so the safe-cast in [`ElementRef.Current`](#current_1) is well-defined. |

### Properties [#properties_1]

#### `Current` [#current_1]

The mounted control as `T`, or `null` when the referenced element has not mounted yet, has been unmounted, or the concrete control is not assignable to `T`.

```csharp
public T? Current  // get
```

**Remarks**

In RELEASE builds a type mismatch silently yields `null`; in DEBUG builds the reconciler raises [`Debug.Fail`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.debug.fail) at attach time so the mismatch is loud during development.

### Methods [#methods]

#### `ToString` [#tostring]

Returns a string that represents this object.

```csharp
public override string ToString()
```

### Operators [#operators]

#### `op_Implicit` [#op_implicit]

Implicit conversion to the untyped [`ElementRef`](#elementref) so the typed wrapper composes with the existing `.Ref(...)` modifier and [`FocusManager`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/FocusManager) overloads without overload bloat.

```csharp
public static implicit operator ElementRef(ElementRef<T> typed)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `typed` | [`ElementRef<T>`](#elementreft) |  |

### `FocusAsync` [#focusasync]

Asynchronously focus the referenced element using WinUI's FocusManager.TryFocusAsync. Use it when the caller needs confirmation that the focus change succeeded. Call it on the target control's UI thread: it does not dispatch, so a background caller must marshal to that thread first (for example through the control's DispatcherQueue).


# Gestures
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/gestures

**Learn more:** [Input and gestures](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/input-and-gestures)

## `GesturePhase` [#gesturephase]

Phase of a continuous gesture (pan / pinch / rotate / long-press). The callback contract: [`GesturePhase.Began`](#values) fires exactly once at the start, [`GesturePhase.Changed`](#values) fires zero or more times as the gesture progresses, then either [`GesturePhase.Ended`](#values) (normal completion) or [`GesturePhase.Cancelled`](#values) (system aborted, pointer lost, escape key, …) fires exactly once.

```csharp
public enum GesturePhase
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Input`.

### Values [#values]

| Name | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Began` | `0` | Gesture has just become recognized and its parameters are stable. |
| `Changed` | `1` | Gesture is in progress; deltas are being reported. |
| `Ended` | `2` | Gesture completed normally. |
| `Cancelled` | `3` | Gesture was cancelled (pointer capture lost, window focus lost, …). |

## `LongPressGesture` [#longpressgesture]

Immutable snapshot of a long-press gesture. Fires [`GesturePhase.Began`](#values) the moment the press threshold is crossed, [`GesturePhase.Ended`](#values) when the pointer is released after that point, or [`GesturePhase.Cancelled`](#values) if the pointer moves beyond the cancel distance or capture is lost.

```csharp
public readonly record struct LongPressGesture(Point Position, TimeSpan Duration, GesturePhase Phase)
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Input`.

## `LongPressGestureConfig` [#longpressgestureconfig]

Mouse input is opt-in via [`LongPressGestureConfig.EnableMouseEmulation`](#enablemouseemulation); when enabled, the reconciler arms a dispatcher timer on [`UIElement.PointerPressed`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.uielement.pointerpressed) and cancels it on release, capture loss, or pointer motion beyond [`LongPressGestureConfig.CancelDistance`](#canceldistance).

# StandardCommand
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/StandardCommand

Factory methods for the 16 standard application commands with pre-filled metadata (label, icon, keyboard accelerator). Each command has sync and async overloads: var cut = StandardCommand.Cut(() =\> CutSelection()); var save = StandardCommand.Save(async () =\> await SaveAsync()); Labels use plain English by default. Override with `with` for localization: var cut = StandardCommand.Cut(action) with \{ Label = intl.Message(keys.Cut) \};

```csharp
public static class StandardCommand
```

# Layout
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/layout

**Learn more:** [Layout](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/layout), [Flex Layout](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/flex-layout)

## Types [#types]

| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Attached layout properties](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/layout/attached) | Records that hold the attached properties set by the layout modifiers. |
| [Flex enums](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/layout/flex-enums) | Enums that control the flex layout. |
| [`GridSize`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/layout/GridSize) | Strongly-typed grid track size, used by the typed `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Factories.Grid(GridSize[], GridSize[], Element?[])` factory in place of the legacy string-form (`"Auto"`, `"*"`, `"200"`, `"1.5*"`) tracks. |
| [`GridSizeExtensions`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/layout/GridSizeExtensions) | Fluent extension methods for `GridSize` to set the optional `Min` and `Max` properties. |

# Attached layout properties

## `CanvasAttached` [#canvasattached]

Attached property data for Canvas children. Set via .Canvas(left:, top:) extension.

```csharp
public record CanvasAttached(double Left = 0, double Top = 0)
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`.

### Remarks [#remarks]

[`CanvasAttached.AnchorX`](#anchorx) / [`CanvasAttached.AnchorY`](#anchory) are 0..1 fractions of the element's rendered size that are subtracted from [`CanvasAttached.Left`](#left)/[`CanvasAttached.Top`](#top) after layout. Anchor 0,0 (default) keeps the legacy top-left positioning. Anchor 0.5,0.5 centers the element on (Left, Top); 1,1 anchors at bottom-right. Useful for chart labels and other elements that need to align around a logical point rather than their top-left corner.

### Constructors [#constructors]

#### `CanvasAttached` [#canvasattached_1]

Attached property data for Canvas children. Set via .Canvas(left:, top:) extension.

```csharp

```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `Top` | `double` | `0` |  |

**Remarks**

[`CanvasAttached.AnchorX`](#anchorx) / [`CanvasAttached.AnchorY`](#anchory) are 0..1 fractions of the element's rendered size that are subtracted from [`CanvasAttached.Left`](#left)/[`CanvasAttached.Top`](#top) after layout. Anchor 0,0 (default) keeps the legacy top-left positioning. Anchor 0.5,0.5 centers the element on (Left, Top); 1,1 anchors at bottom-right. Useful for chart labels and other elements that need to align around a logical point rather than their top-left corner.

# GridSize
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/layout/GridSize

```csharp
public readonly record struct GridSize
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor`.

**Learn more:** [Layout](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/layout)

## Remarks [#remarks]

Spec 033 §1. The smart constructors [`GridSize.Auto`](#auto), [`GridSize.Star`](#star), and [`GridSize.Px`](#px) validate their inputs at the boundary; the implicit conversion to [`GridLength`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.gridlength) lets the typed form compose with anything that takes a WinUI [`GridLength`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.gridlength).

The string parser ([`GridSize.Parse`](#parse)) is invariant-culture only — track strings are never localized. Whitespace is trimmed; `"Auto"` matches case-insensitively; numeric forms use [`CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.globalization.cultureinfo.invariantculture).

When Min or Max are specified, the track size is clamped to that range. For example, `GridSize.Px(100) with { Min=50 and Max=200 }` will be set to 100 initially and depending on changes clamped to 50 and 200. Min can be set higher as Max in which case the track size will be clamped to the Max value.

## Constructors [#constructors]

### `GridSize` [#gridsize_1]

```csharp

```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `double` |  |  |
| `type` | `GridUnitType` |  |  |
| `min` | `double?` | `null` |  |
| `max` | `double?` | `null` |  |

### `Message` [#message]

#### `Message(MessageKey, IDictionary<string, object>?)` [#messagemessagekey-idictionarystring-object]

Loads a string resource by key, then formats it with ICU MessageFormat. Falls back to the default locale if the key is missing in the current locale.

```csharp
public string Message(MessageKey key, IDictionary<string, object>? args = null)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | [`MessageKey`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/localization/MessageKey) |  |  |
| `args` | `IDictionary<string, object>?` | `null` |  |

#### `Message(MessageKey, (string Name, object? Value), (string Name, object? Value)[])` [#messagemessagekey-string-name-object-value-string-name-object-value]

Compact tuple-args overload for the common case of formatting a single message with a handful of ICU placeholders. Builds a plain [`Dictionary`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.dictionary-2) in-place — no reflection, AOT-safe.

```csharp
public string Message(MessageKey key, (string Name, object? Value) arg1, params (string Name, object? Value)[] more)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | [`MessageKey`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/localization/MessageKey) |  |
| `arg1` | `(string Name, object? Value)` |  |
| `more` | `(string Name, object? Value)[]` |  |

**Remarks**

Tuples with a null `Value` are dropped before the dictionary is built — this matches the behavior of the prior reflection path, which skipped null-valued properties so the formatter saw the placeholder as "missing" rather than substituting an empty string.

**Example**

```csharp
t.Message(Greeting, ("name", "World"));
t.Message(SearchResults, ("count", 0), ("query", "test"));
```

### `RichMessage` [#richmessage]

#### `RichMessage(MessageKey, IDictionary<string, object>?, Dictionary<string, Func<string, Element>>?)` [#richmessagemessagekey-idictionarystring-object-dictionarystring-funcstring-element]

Formats a message that contains rich text tags (e.g., \<bold\>text\</bold\>), mapping each tag to an element factory. Returns a GroupElement containing the resulting child elements (text spans + wrapped elements).

```csharp
public Element RichMessage(MessageKey key, IDictionary<string, object>? args = null, Dictionary<string, Func<string, Element>>? tags = null)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | [`MessageKey`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/localization/MessageKey) |  |  |
| `args` | `IDictionary<string, object>?` | `null` |  |
| `tags` | `Dictionary<string, Func<string, Element>>?` | `null` |  |

**Remarks**

The .resw value uses XML-like tags: "Click \<link\>here\</link\> to read the \<bold\>docs\</bold\>." Tags are mapped via the `tags` dictionary. Unrecognized tags are rendered as plain text (tag markers stripped). Nested tags are not supported — only the outermost tag is processed.

#### `RichMessage(MessageKey, (string Name, object? Value), (string Name, object? Value)[])` [#richmessagemessagekey-string-name-object-value-string-name-object-value]

Compact tuple-args overload of the dict-based `RichMessage` — same allocation profile as the tuple-args `Message` overload. Tags must be supplied via the dict-based overload; this variant is for the common case where the developer just wants the formatted text. Null-valued tuples are dropped (see the tuple-args `Message` remarks).

```csharp
public Element RichMessage(MessageKey key, (string Name, object? Value) arg1, params (string Name, object? Value)[] more)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | [`MessageKey`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/localization/MessageKey) |  |
| `arg1` | `(string Name, object? Value)` |  |
| `more` | `(string Name, object? Value)[]` |  |

# ReswResourceProvider
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/localization/ReswResourceProvider

Production implementation of [`IStringResourceProvider`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/localization/IStringResourceProvider) that reads .resw files directly from disk as XML.

NOTE: This bypasses MRT (Modern Resource Technology) and the Windows PRI resource system. The standard approach would be to use ResourceLoader from Microsoft.global::Windows.ApplicationModel.Resources, which relies on the .resw files being compiled into a .pri (Package Resource Index) at build time. However, ResourceLoader has significant friction in unpackaged app scenarios:

\- ResourceLoader(subtreeName) fails with FileNotFoundException for named .resw files in unpackaged apps, even when the PRI contains the resources. - MRT locale negotiation uses the OS language settings, not the app's explicit locale choice, which conflicts with Reactor's LocaleProvider model where the app controls the active locale at runtime.

By reading .resw XML directly, we get: - Identical behavior for packaged and unpackaged apps - Locale resolution driven by LocaleProvider, not the OS - No dependency on MRT initialization or PRI packaging

REVISIT: If Reactor apps move to packaged deployment (MSIX) as the default, or if MRT Core improves unpackaged support, consider switching back to ResourceLoader for better OS integration (e.g., per-language resource packs, system-level font/layout negotiation).

```csharp
public sealed class ReswResourceProvider : IStringResourceProvider
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Localization`.

**Learn more:** [Localization](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/localization)

## Constructors [#constructors]

### `ReswResourceProvider` [#reswresourceprovider_1]

Creates a ReswResourceProvider that reads .resw files from the Strings/ folder relative to the application base directory.

```csharp
public ReswResourceProvider(string defaultLocale = "en-US", string? stringsBasePath = null)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultLocale` | `string` | `"en-US"` | The default/source locale (e.g., "en-US"). |
| `stringsBasePath` | `string?` | `null` | Absolute path to the Strings folder, or null to auto-detect from the application base directory. REVISIT: This auto-detection assumes Strings/ is next to the exe, which may not hold for all deployment layouts. |


**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `locale` | `string` |  |

| `key` | `string` |  |

# Modifiers
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers

Modifiers are extension methods on element records. Each one returns a changed copy of the element, so you can chain them: `TextBlock("Hi").Margin(8).Bold()`.

**Learn more:** [Modifier System](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/modifier-system), [Styling and Theming](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/styling)

## Common modifiers [#common-modifiers]

Modifiers that most elements have, grouped by purpose.

| Area | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Layout and spacing](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/layout-and-spacing) | Size, margin, padding, alignment and the attached layout properties. |
| [Appearance](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/appearance) | Background, foreground, borders, corners, opacity, transforms, styles and theme. |
| [Typography](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/typography) | Fonts, text alignment, wrapping, trimming and other text formatting. |
| [Accessibility](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/accessibility) | Automation names, landmarks, live regions and other accessibility properties. |
| [Focus and keyboard](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/focus-and-keyboard) | Tab order, access keys, directional focus and focus traps. |
| [Input and events](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/input-and-events) | Pointer, keyboard, gesture and drag and drop events, and whether an element takes input. |
| [Lifecycle and identity](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/lifecycle) | Keys, refs, mount and unmount callbacks, size changes and context values. |
| [Animation](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/animation) | Transitions, keyframes, layout animations, interaction states and scroll-linked animation. |
| [Tooltips and flyouts](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/tooltips-and-flyouts) | Tooltips, flyouts and context flyouts attached to any element. |
| [Validation](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/validation) | Validators, required fields and error styling. |
| [Native properties](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/native-properties) | The Set modifier, which changes the real WinUI control directly. |

## Control modifiers [#control-modifiers]

Modifiers that only some controls have, grouped by the area of those controls.

| Area | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Shared controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/shared-controls) | Modifiers that several kinds of controls share, such as headers, placeholders and selection events. |
| [Layout](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/layout) | Modifiers that only the controls in the Layout area have. |
| [Buttons](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/buttons) | Modifiers that only the controls in the Buttons area have. |
| [Input](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/input) | Modifiers that only the controls in the Input area have. |
| [Collections](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/collections) | Modifiers that only the controls in the Collections area have. |
| [Navigation](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/navigation) | Modifiers that only the controls in the Navigation area have. |
| [Dialogs and flyouts](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/dialogs-and-flyouts) | Modifiers that only the controls in the Dialogs and flyouts area have. |
| [Media and icons](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/media) | Modifiers that only the controls in the Media and icons area have. |
| [Shapes](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/shapes) | Modifiers that only the controls in the Shapes area have. |
| [Status and info](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/status-and-info) | Modifiers that only the controls in the Status and info area have. |
| [Forms](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/forms) | Modifiers that only the controls in the Forms area have. |
| [Interop](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/interop) | Modifiers that only the controls in the Interop area have. |

## Types [#types]

| Type | Description |

## `Semantics` [#semantics]

Wraps this element in a SemanticPanel that provides custom automation semantics to screen readers. Use this for composite components that need to describe their role and value (e.g., a star rating widget built from Image elements that should announce as "slider, 3 of 5 stars").

Analogous to SwiftUI's .accessibilityRepresentation \{\} and Compose's Modifier.semantics \{ role = Role.Slider \}.

```csharp
SemanticElement Semantics<T>(this T el, string? role = null, string? value = null, double? rangeMin = null, double? rangeMax = null, double? rangeValue = null, bool isReadOnly = true) where T : Element
```

Declared in `ElementExtensions`.

**Applies to:** any element.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `role` | `string?` | `null` |  |
| `value` | `string?` | `null` |  |
| `rangeMin` | `double?` | `null` |  |
| `rangeMax` | `double?` | `null` |  |
| `rangeValue` | `double?` | `null` |  |
| `isReadOnly` | `bool` | `true` |  |

**Example**

```csharp
StarRating(value: 3, max: 5)
    .Semantics(role: "slider", value: "3 of 5 stars",
               rangeValue: 3, rangeMin: 0, rangeMax: 5)
```

# Modifiers: Appearance
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/appearance

Modifiers are extension methods that return a changed copy of the element, so you can chain them.

**Learn more:** [Styling and Theming](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/styling), [Theming Tokens](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/theming-tokens)

## `ApplyStyle` [#applystyle]

Apply a named WinUI Style to the element's control. Style is on FrameworkElement — works on any element. Usage: TextBlock("Hello").ApplyStyle("BodyTextBlockStyle")

**Applied at mount only.** This routes through `OnMount`, and the reconciler runs `OnMountAction` only when there is no previous element (first mount). Conditionally chaining a style therefore will not apply or remove it when the condition flips on an in-place update — give the variants different [`WithKey`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/lifecycle#withkey) values to force a remount when the style itself must change.

**Unresolved keys do not throw.** If `styleName` is not found in the application's resources (including merged dictionaries), or is found but is not a [`Style`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.style), the element keeps its default appearance and a warning naming the key is emitted on the `Microsoft-UI-Reactor` ETW provider (and to `Debug.WriteLine` in DEBUG builds). Earlier versions threw out of the mount action instead. The warning fires once per distinct key, so one bad key in a virtualized list does not warn per realized item; past a few hundred distinct unresolved keys the de-duplication stops and every miss warns again, because staying quiet there would hide a real typo. Under NativeAOT the ETW half is compiled out unless the app sets `EventSourceSupport=true`; the DEBUG mirror is unaffected.

```csharp
T ApplyStyle<T>(this T el, string styleName) where T : Element
```

Declared in `ElementExtensions`.

**Applies to:** any element.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `styleName` | `string` |  |

## `Resources` [#resources]

Configures per-control resource overrides via WinUI's lightweight styling mechanism. Overrides are injected into [`FrameworkElement.Resources`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.frameworkelement.resources) so the control's [`VisualStateManager`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.visualstatemanager) picks them up automatically — hover, pressed, and disabled states all respect the overrides without requiring a custom template.

**Brand-colored button:**

```csharp
Button("Submit").Resources(r => r
    .Set("ButtonBackground", "#0078D4")
    .Set("ButtonBackgroundPointerOver", "#106EBE")
    .Set("ButtonBackgroundPressed", "#005A9E"))
```

**Scoped cascading:** resources set on a parent panel cascade to child controls, matching WinUI's resource lookup behavior.

```csharp
T Resources<T>(this T el, Action<ResourceBuilder> configure) where T : Element
```

Declared in `ElementExtensions`.

**Applies to:** any element.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `configure` | `Action<ResourceBuilder>` |  |

# Control modifiers: Buttons
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/buttons

Modifiers are extension methods that return a changed copy of the element, so you can chain them.

**Learn more:** [Controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls), [Commanding](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/commanding)

## `AccentButton` [#accentbutton]

Applies the WinUI `AccentButtonStyle` — the accent-color primary-button look. The Style is resolved from `Application.Current.Resources` once; its colors still follow light/dark/contrast switches because the Style's own setters use `{ThemeResource}` values, which WinUI re-resolves on theme change.

**Applied at mount only.** Like [`ApplyStyle`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/appearance#applystyle) this runs through `OnMount`, which the reconciler gates on first mount — so conditionally chaining it (e.g. `isPrimary? btn.AccentButton(): btn`) will *not* apply or remove the style when the condition flips on an in-place update. Give the two variants different [`WithKey`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/lifecycle#withkey) values to force a remount when the style must change.

```csharp
ButtonElement AccentButton(this ButtonElement el)
DropDownButtonElement AccentButton(this DropDownButtonElement el)
SplitButtonElement AccentButton(this SplitButtonElement el)
ToggleSplitButtonElement AccentButton(this ToggleSplitButtonElement el)
```

Declared in `ElementExtensions`.

**Applies to:** [`ButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#buttonelement), [`DropDownButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#dropdownbuttonelement), [`SplitButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#splitbuttonelement), [`ToggleSplitButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#togglesplitbuttonelement).

## `Command` [#command]

```csharp
ButtonElement Command(this ButtonElement el, Command command)
HyperlinkButtonElement Command(this HyperlinkButtonElement el, Command command)
RepeatButtonElement Command(this RepeatButtonElement el, Command command)
ToggleButtonElement Command(this ToggleButtonElement el, Command command)
```

Declared in `ElementExtensions`.

| Overload | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Command(ButtonElement, Command)` | Binds a [`Command`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command) to a custom-content [`ButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#buttonelement) by lifting it onto the typed [`ButtonElement.Command`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#buttonelement) property (issues #133, #153, unified in #637). The reconciler invokes Execute/ExecuteAsync on click, folds the command's [`Command.IsEnabled`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command#isenabled) into the IsEnabled descriptor entry (re-applied when the command's derived enabled state changes — field-aware, not on every render — and coexisting with `.IsDisabledFocusable()`'s coercion), and flows Description / Accelerator / AccessKey — all field-aware, with no per-render [`ButtonElement.Setters`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#buttonelement) lambda. Pairs with `Button(content)` so icon-plus-label buttons auto-disable like the `Button(Command)` factory. The modifier makes the command fully take over: any [`ButtonElement.OnClick`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#buttonelement) already on the element is cleared so the command — not a stale click handler — dispatches (issue #637; matches the pre-#637 modifier, and the `Button(Command)` factory which builds the element with no `OnClick`). A raw `.Set(...)` setter runs after the command metadata and therefore overrides it. |
| `Command(HyperlinkButtonElement, Command)` | Binds a [`Command`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command) to a [`HyperlinkButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#hyperlinkbuttonelement), clearing any existing `OnClick` so the command takes over dispatch. See [`Command`](#command). (issues #133, #637) |
| `Command(RepeatButtonElement, Command)` | Binds a [`Command`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command) to a [`RepeatButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#repeatbuttonelement), clearing any existing `OnClick` so the command takes over dispatch. See [`Command`](#command). (issues #133, #637) |
| `Command(ToggleButtonElement, Command)` | Binds a [`Command`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command) to a [`ToggleButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#togglebuttonelement). The command fires on each toggle (check and uncheck), matching the `ToggleButton(Command)` factory; any existing toggle callback (`OnIsCheckedChanged` / `OnCheckedStateChanged`) is cleared so the command takes over dispatch. See [`Command`](#command). (issues #133, #637) |

**Applies to:** [`ButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#buttonelement), [`HyperlinkButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#hyperlinkbuttonelement), [`RepeatButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#repeatbuttonelement), [`ToggleButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#togglebuttonelement).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | [`Command`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command) |  |

## `DisabledFocusable` [#disabledfocusable]

Keeps the button keyboard-focusable while presenting it as disabled (visually dimmed, click suppressed). Use for submit buttons gated on validation: a true `.IsEnabled(false)` removes the button from tab order, which combined with commit-on-blur inputs like NumberBox/ DatePicker produces a focus trap where Tab skips a Submit that is \*about\* to become valid. Conceptually the Fluent UI React `disabledFocusable` / ARIA `aria-disabled` pattern; UIA still sees the button as enabled (a custom AutomationPeer override for full AT "unavailable" reporting is a tracked follow-up).

```csharp
ButtonElement DisabledFocusable(this ButtonElement el, bool disabled = true)
```

Declared in `ElementExtensions`.

> **Obsolete.** Use IsDisabledFocusable() — aligns with WinUI naming (see #268).

**Applies to:** [`ButtonElement`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/buttons#buttonelement).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `bool` | `true` |  |

# ElementExtensions
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/ElementExtensions

TextBlock("Hello") .Bold() .Margin(16) .HAlign(HorizontalAlignment.Center) .Set(tb =\> tb.IsTextScaleFactorEnabled = false) // still TextBlockElement!

The Set() extension gives strongly-typed native property access: Button("Click", onClick) .Set(b =\> b.FlowDirection = FlowDirection.RightToLeft)

```csharp
public static class ElementExtensions
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor`.

## Methods [#methods]

### `Command` [#command]

Binds a [`Command`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command) to an [`AppBarButtonData`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/controls/menu-items#appbarbuttondata): maps Execute, IsEnabled, Icon, Accelerator, AccessKey, and Description — the same plumbing as the `AppBarButton(Command)` factory, but usable on a hand-built app-bar button. (issue #133)

```csharp
public static AppBarButtonData Command(this AppBarButtonData el, Command command)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | [`Command`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/input/Command) |  |

# ElementExtras
Source: https://microsoft.github.io/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/ElementExtras

Cross-cutting "extras" bucket for [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) (spec 047 §4.4). Holds the 14 rarely-set fields (attached properties, transitions, theme bindings, animation configs, resource overrides, context values) that used to sit inline on every element. Bucketing them into a lazy sub-record lets the common case (a leaf with none of these) pay one reference slot instead of 14. The fields are exposed on [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) via get/init shim properties that read from / write into this record, so call sites see no API change. Value-equality (default record) so equality helpers and `with`-writers behave exactly as before. Unlike [`ElementModifiers`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/modifiers/ElementModifiers) nothing merges Extras, so there is no Merge.

**Construction-cost tradeoff (spec 047 §4.4 / §11.6):** the common no-extras leaf now saves a reference slot (the §4.4 win), but each extra-setting fluent call (`.Grid()`, `.Background(Theme…)`, `.Animate()`, `.Provide()`, …) clones this sub-record *in addition to* the [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) clone — so an element that sets several extras does N small `ElementExtras` allocations during construction where the inline layout did zero. Net win for the common case; watch the §11.6 byte-gate M2/M3 (callback/modifier-heavy leaves) when it is measured on the baseline box, as those are the construction-cost-sensitive scenarios.

```csharp
public record ElementExtras
```

Namespace: `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`.

**Learn more:** [Modifier System](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/modifier-system)

## Remarks [#remarks]

Spec 047 §4.4.


```csharp
public AnimationConfig? AnimationConfig  // get, init
```

### `Attached` [#attached]

```csharp
public IReadOnlyDictionary<Type, object>? Attached  // get, init
```

### `CallSite` [#callsite]

Spec 010 — the DSL call site that produced the owning element.

Bucketed here rather than declared inline on [`Element`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/reference/elements/Element) so that an element nobody stamped pays nothing. An inline `SourceLocation?` widens EVERY element instance by 24 bytes in every build and every configuration — measured at +24.0 B/op on the M12 control-model bench with source mapping switched off — which is a permanent retail tax for a debug-only feature. Living in the §4.4 extras bucket makes the cost proportional to the number of stamped elements instead of the number of elements.

It is NOT free, and the trade is worth stating precisely. As a nullable struct this field is stored inline, so it widens the bucket itself: measured at 152 B/instance with it and 24 B of that attributable to this field (an 8-byte path reference, a 4-byte line, the nullable flag, padded). Any element carrying a behavioral extra — Attached, ThemeBindings, animations, ResourceOverrides, ContextValues — pays that whether or not source mapping is on, and whether or not the consumer even has the generator. The M12 benchmark cannot see it, because M12 leaves are extras-free and allocate no bucket at all. Accepted because it is bounded and proportional to elements that already allocate this object, versus +24 B on EVERY element (measured) for the inline-on-the-record alternative. ElementExtrasAllocationTests pins both halves.

Read through `Element.CallSite`, which is the public shim; the bucket is an implementation detail.

```csharp
public SourceLocation? CallSite  // get, init
```

**Remarks**

Spec 047 §4.4 bucketing; spec 010 slot.

### `ConnectedAnimationKey` [#connectedanimationkey]

Connected animation key for cross-container transitions. When set, the reconciler automatically captures a visual snapshot on unmount (via ConnectedAnimationService.PrepareToAnimate) and starts the animation on mount if a prepared animation with the same key exists. Set via fluent extension method: Border(child).ConnectedAnimation("hero")

```csharp
public string? ConnectedAnimationKey  // get, init
```

When set, the reconciler injects these into [`FrameworkElement.Resources`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.ui.xaml.frameworkelement.resources) so that the control's VisualStateManager picks them up for hover/pressed/disabled states. Set via fluent extension: `Button("Go").Resources(r => r.Set("ButtonBackground", "#0078D4"))`

```csharp

```

### `ThemeBindings` [#themebindings]

Theme-resource bindings for brush properties (Background, Foreground, BorderBrush). When set, the reconciler resolves from WinUI theme resources instead of using local values. Set via fluent extension methods: TextBlock("hi").Background(Theme.Accent)
